facing downwards, and black in color, within the left side of the belly.
The holding of the nostrils with the little finger, the ring finger, and the thumb constitutes the *kumbhaka* and the *recaka*;
one should then perform the *kumbhaka* and *recaka* again.
Having meditated upon the wind as a six-cornered mandala arising from the seed-syllables *yaṃ raṃ vaṃ laṃ haṃ āṃ hrīṃ kroṃ*, which has emerged through recitation and possesses a magnificent form— (p.
One should practice two wind-seeds for the duration of eight seed-measures;
this is indeed known by the wise as *prāṇāyāma*.
Having performed inhalation through the left [nostril], retention through the right,
and again exhalation through the right, one should perform retention and exhale through the left.
Again, perform inhalation through the left, retention, and exhalation through the right;
having thus made this procedure firm, the purification is established in the vital breath (prāṇa).

Thus it is said. And he says: having dried [the body] sixteen times with the seed-syllable *yaṃ* by means of inhalation (*pūraka*), having burned it sixty-four times with *raṃ* by means of retention (*kumbhaka*), and having expelled the ashes thirty-two times with *vaṃ* by means of exhalation (*recaka*), one should bathe it sixteen times with *vaṃ* by means of inhalation, and [sixty-four times] with *laṃ*.

Perform *piṇḍīkaraṇa* (compression) sixty-four times with *kumbhaka* while reciting "haṃ" thirty-two times; perform *prāṇasthāpana* (establishing the vital breath) thirty-two times with *recaka* while reciting "āṃ" sixteen times; having made it firm by means of *pūraka* sixty-four times while reciting "hrīṃ";
and perform purification sixty-four times with *kumbhaka* using the seed-syllable "kroṃ" thirty-two times.

Having established [the deity] with the *recaka* breath—this is the sequence. Thus, having performed *prāṇāyāma*, having dissolved [everything] with *vaṃ*, having made it solid with *laṃ*, and having meditated on the limbs of the body with *haṃ*, one should establish the *jīva* in its own place within the Supreme Self as the state of the Perfect Self, reciting *hrīṃ so'haṃ haṃsaḥ*. From the presence of the Supreme Self, *prakṛti* [emerges].
From *prakṛti* comes the principle of *mahat*; from *mahat*, the *ahaṅkāra*; from that, space (*ākāśa*);

from space, air (*vāyu*); from air, fire (*agni*); from fire, water (*āpaḥ*); and from water, earth (*pṛthvī*)—having thus established the elements in their respective places in this sequence, one [should contemplate] the *kuṇḍalinī* as having become merged with nectar by means of the mantra "So 'ham."
One should establish the five elements and the individual soul (jīvātman) in their respective places upon the path of Brahman. Thus concludes the purification of the elements (bhūtaśuddhi).

Now, the installation of the vital breaths (prāṇapratiṣṭhāpanam). Then, having meditated upon oneself in the form of the Goddess and placing the hand upon the heart, one should perform the installation of the vital breaths: Oṃ ĀṂ Hrīṃ Kroṃ Yaṃ Raṃ Laṃ Vaṃ Śaṃ Ṣaṃ Saṃ Haṃ Saḥ. My vital breaths are here, my vital breaths are here. My life-force is stationed here, it is stationed here.

"May all my senses remain here, remain here! O my speech, mind, skin, eyes, ears, tongue, nose, and vital breaths, having come here, may you dwell happily for a long time—Svāhā! Having thus performed the *prāṇapratiṣṭhā* (the ritual installation of the life-force), [one should recite] one's own root mantra...

Oṃ. Of this Śrī Bhuvaneśvarī mantra, Śrī Śakti is the Ṛṣi, Gāyatrī is the Chandas, Śrī Bhuvaneśvarī is the Devatā, Hrīṃ is the Bīja, Śrīṃ is the Śakti, Klīṃ is the Kīlaka; my application (viniyoga) is in the recitation for the sake of attaining my desired goal. Having thus remembered with palms joined, one should contemplate the Śakti...

Salutation to the seed-syllable *hrīṃ* in the heart; salutation to the power (*śakti*) *śrīṃ* in the secret place; salutation to the peg (*kīlaka*) *klīṃ* in the two feet; salutation at the navel for the application in recitation (*japa*). One should perform the ninefold pervasive placement (*vyāpaka-nyāsa*) over all limbs with the root mantra.

Now, the ritual placement of mantras (mantra-nyāsa): Oṃ hṛllekhāyai namaḥ on the head; Oṃ aiṃ gaganāyai namaḥ on the face; Oṃ raktāyai namaḥ on the heart; Oṃ iṃ karālikāyai namaḥ on the private parts;
Oṃ mahocchuṣmāyai namaḥ on both feet; Oṃ aiṃ juṃ uṃ hṛllekhāyai namaḥ.

Having performed the placement upon all the limbs, one should place them thus: "Oṃ, obeisance to Hṛllekhā" on the upper face; "Oṃ Aiṃ, obeisance to Gaganā" on the eastern face; "Oṃ Juṃ, obeisance to Raktā" on the southern face; "Oṃ Iṃ, obeisance to Karālikā" on the northern face;
and "Oṃ, obeisance to Mahocchuṣmā" on the western face. Having performed this placement:
One should perform the six-limbed placement (*ṣaḍaṅganyāsa*) on the hands: *oṃ hrāṃ* to the two thumbs; *oṃ hrīṃ* to the two index fingers;
*oṃ hrūṃ* to the two middle fingers; *oṃ hraiṃ* to the two ring fingers; *oṃ hrauṃ* to the two little fingers; *oṃ hraḥ* to the palms and backs of the hands.
Oṃ hrāṃ hṛdayāya namaḥ; Oṃ hrīṃ śirase svāhā; Oṃ hrūṃ śikhāyai vaṣaṭ; Oṃ hraiṃ kavacāya huṃ; Oṃ hrauṃ netratrayāya vauṣaṭ; Oṃ hraḥ astrāya phaṭ.
Having thus performed the three successive *tāla* gestures above, and having performed the binding of the directions (*digbandhana*) as before, [place] Oṃ on the forehead.
Salutation to Brahman and Gāyatrī on the right cheek; salutation to Sāvitrī and Viṣṇu on the left cheek;
salutation to Vāgīśvarī and Vāgīśvara on the left ear; salutation to Dhanapati accompanied by Śrī at the mouth;
salutation to Madana accompanied by Rati on the right ear; salutation to Gaṇapati accompanied by Puṣṭi on the left ear.

Oṃ, salutation to Śaṅkhanidhi—place this on the left ear; Oṃ, salutation to Padmanidhi—place this on the mouth; recite the root mantra on the base of the throat; Oṃ, salutation to Brahmā together with Gāyatrī—on the right breast; Oṃ, salutation to Viṣṇu together with Sāvitrī—on the left breast; Oṃ, salutation to Maheśvara together with Vāgīśvarī—[on the right breast].
One should place the mantra *oṃ śrīsahitadhanapataye namaḥ* on the right shoulder; *oṃ ratisahitamanmathāya namaḥ* on the left shoulder;
*oṃ śaṅkhanidhaye namaḥ* and *oṃ padmanidhaye namaḥ* on the two feet; the root mantra (*mūla*) at the navel;
*oṃ brāhmyai namaḥ* on the forehead; and *oṃ māheśvaryyai namaḥ* on the left shoulder.

On the left side: *oṃ kaumāryai namaḥ*; on the belly: *oṃ vaiṣṇavyai namaḥ*; on the right side: *oṃ vārāhyai namaḥ*; on the right shoulder: *oṃ indrāṇyai namaḥ*; on the back of the neck: *oṃ cāmuṇḍāyai namaḥ*; in the heart:
*oṃ mahālakṣmyai namaḥ*. One should perform the pervasive placement (*vyāpaka-nyāsa*) nine times with the root mantra.

Now, the Mātṛkā-nyāsa: Oṃ. Of this Śrī-mātṛkā-nyāsa, Brahmā is the seer (ṛṣi), Gāyatrī is the meter (chandaḥ), the venerable Mātṛkā Sarasvatī is the deity (devatā), the consonants are the seeds (bījāni), the vowels are the powers (śaktayaḥ), and the unmanifest (avyakta) is the bolt (kīlaka). Its application (viniyoga) is in the ritual placement (nyāsa) as a limb of mine, the venerable Bhuvaneśvarī. [Thus saying,] with palms joined in reverence (kṛtāñjali):

Having recollected [the mantra], one should perform the placement (*nyāsa*): *Oṃ aiṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ*, salutation to Brahmā, the seer (*ṛṣi*), on the head; salutation to the Gāyatrī meter (*chandas*), on the mouth; salutation to the goddess Śrīmātṛkā-Sarasvatī, the deity (*devatā*), on the heart;

salutation to the consonants (*hal*), the seed-syllables (*bīja*), on the private parts; salutation to the vowels (*svara*), the powers (*śakti*), on the feet; salutation to the unmanifest (*avyakta*), the pin (*kīlaka*).

*Namo* at the navel; *śrībhuvaneśvarī* as the limbs for the ritual application (*viniyoga*) upon all the limbs. Thus is the ritual placement of the seer and other elements (*ṛṣyādinyāsa*). Now, one should perform the ritual placements of the hands and the six limbs (*kara-ṣaḍaṅganyāsa*): *Oṃ aiṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ aṃ kaṃ 5 āṃ* to the two thumbs, *namaḥ*; *Oṃ aiṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ iṃ caṃ 5 iṃ* to the two index fingers.
*Namaḥ* *oṃ aiṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ ūṃ ṭaṃ* 5 *ūṃ madhyamābhyāṃ namaḥ*. (p.
54) *Oṃ aiṃ śrīṃ hrīṃ aiṃ taṃ* 5 *aiṃ anāmikābhyāṃ namaḥ*. *Oṃ aiṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ ūṃ*.

*Paṃ* 5 *ūṃ* to the two little fingers, *namaḥ*; *oṃ aiṃ śrīṃ hrīṃ aṃ yaṃ* 10 *aṃ* to the palms and backs of the hands, *namaḥ*. Thus is the ritual placement on the hands (*karanyāsa*). Now follows the ritual placement of the six limbs (*ṣaḍaṅganyāsa*): *oṃ aiṃ śrīṃ hrīṃ aṃ kaṃ* 5 *āṃ* to the heart, *namaḥ*; *oṃ aiṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ iṃ caṃ* 5 *iṃ*.

Śirase svāhā, Oṃ Aiṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Ūṃ Ṭaṃ 5; Śikhāyai vaṣaṭ, Oṃ Aiṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Aiṃ Taṃ 5; Kavacāya huṃ, Oṃ Aiṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Ūṃ Paṃ 5; Netratrayāya vauṣaṭ, Oṃ Aiṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Aṃ Yaṃ 10 Aṃ Aḥ Astrāya phaṭ. Thus is the six-limbed assignment (ṣaḍaṅganyāsa).
Meditation:

Oṃ! [One should meditate on] the lotus whose pericarp is the letter *ra* (rasanārṇa) with the moon in the sky (*vyomendu*), whose filaments flash with pairs of vowels (*acām dvandvaiḥ*), and which possesses, in sequence, the three groups beginning with the letters *ya*, *śa*, and *la*, situated within the petals along with the five classes of consonants.

In this context, let one worship that deity consisting of the phonemes with the verse composed here, which is surrounded by the city of the earth (kṣoṇīpura) joined with the letters ending in *la* and *laṅgali* (the letter *ya*) in the three directions of hope (*āśāsu*). [The sequence is: *vyoma* (ha), *indu* (sa), *auḥ* as the essential form, the letter of the tongue (ra) as the visarga; beginning with *vyoma*.

Because it is stated that "the pericarp throbs with the fourteen vowels ending in the visarga," [it is understood that] there are vowels (*acām*) among the filaments (*kesareṣu*). It should be known that the writing of the vowels upon the filaments is directed toward the pericarp, beginning from the front petal. In the quarters (*āśāsu*), that is, the cardinal directions, and in the corners (*asriṣu*), that is, the intermediate points, is the letter *va* ending in *la* (i.e., *vla*). The letter *ṭha* is the "tail" (*lāṅgulī*). Because these two are joined together by a line...
The method of drawing it should be known as stated in the *Dakṣiṇāmūrtisaṃhitā* (published by Sarasvatībhavana):
"Then one should make a square; one should draw [the lines] within the directions so that it bestows success."
Then, outside of that, there is a group of four *ṭha* letters ending with a line.
Having drawn the [mandala] of Varuṇa, the wise one should invoke the Goddess. Thus it is said.

Since the writing of letters and so forth is prescribed even here in the worship yantra, this indicates that, according to some authorities, this very [yantra] is the *dhāraṇa-yantra*. Regarding the phrase "the lotus," it means one should meditate on her as seated upon a white lotus, because it is stated: "the lotus is likewise white.
Thus, she is to be visualized as having a white lotus seat. This is from the *Padārthādarśa* commentary on the *Śāradātilaka*.
In the fourth quarter of this verse,
the reading "varṇābjaṃ śirasi sthitaṃ viṣagadapradhvaṃsi mṛtyuñjayet" is also found in some places.
Then, having performed the assignment of the six limbs (*ṣaḍaṅganyāsa*) for the sages and so forth as before, one should assign [the vowels]: *aṃ* namaḥ, *āṃ* namaḥ, *iṃ* namaḥ, *īṃ* namaḥ,
*uṃ* namaḥ, *ūṃ* namaḥ, *ṛṃ* namaḥ, *ṝṃ* namaḥ,
*ḷṃ* namaḥ, *ḹṃ* namaḥ, *eṃ* namaḥ, *aiṃ* namaḥ, *oṃ* namaḥ, *auṃ* namaḥ, *aṃ* namaḥ, *aḥ* namaḥ.

*Namaḥ* at the sixteen-petaled [lotus] in the region of the throat: *kaṃ namaḥ*, *khaṃ namaḥ*, *gaṃ namaḥ*, *ghaṃ namaḥ*, *ṅaṃ namaḥ*, *caṃ namaḥ*, *chaṃ namaḥ*, *jaṃ namaḥ*, *jhaṃ namaḥ*, *ñaṃ namaḥ*, *ṭaṃ namaḥ*, *ṭhaṃ namaḥ*—thus in the twelve-petaled [lotus] of the *anāhata*. *ḍaṃ namaḥ*, *ḍhaṃ*...

*Namaḥ* to *ṇaṃ*, *namaḥ* to *taṃ*, *namaḥ* to *thaṃ*, *namaḥ* to *daṃ*, *namaḥ* to *dhaṃ*, *namaḥ* to *naṃ*, *namaḥ* to *paṃ*, *namaḥ* to *phaṃ*; thus [are the syllables] in the ten-petalled Maṇipūraka. (p. 55)

*Bam* namaḥ, *bham* namaḥ, *mam* namaḥ, *yam* namaḥ, *ram* namaḥ, *lam* namaḥ—thus in the six-petaled Svādhiṣṭhāna. *Vam* namaḥ, *śam* namaḥ, *sam* namaḥ—thus in the four-petaled Mūlādhāra. *Ham* namaḥ, *kṣam* namaḥ—thus in the two-petaled Ājñācakra.
Thus ends the internal nyāsa of the Mātṛkās.

Now follows the external Mātṛkā-nyāsa. Oṃ. Of this Śrī Bahirmātṛkā-nyāsa, Brahmā is the seer (ṛṣi), Gāyatrī is the meter (chandas), the venerable Bahirmātṛkā Sarasvatī is the deity (devatā), the consonants are the seeds (bījas), the vowels are the powers (śaktis), and the unmanifest (avyakta) is the bolt (kīlaka); [this is performed] for the sake of my limb of Śrī Bhuvaneśvarī.

The application (*viniyoga*) is for the external placement of the *mātṛkās*. Having said this with palms joined in reverence, and having performed the recollection of the seer (*ṛṣi*) and so forth, as well as the six-limbed placement (*ṣaḍaṅganyāsa*) as before, one should perform the placement: *Oṃ aiṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ aṃ namaḥ* on the head;
*āṃ namaḥ* on the face; *īṃ namaḥ* on the right eye; *īṃ namaḥ* on the left eye.

4 *uṃ* namaḥ to the right ear; 4 *ūṃ* namaḥ to the left ear; 4 *ṛṃ* namaḥ to the right nostril; 4 *ṝṃ* namaḥ to the left nostril; 4 *ḷ* namaḥ to the right cheek; 4 *ḹ* namaḥ to the left cheek; 4 *eṃ* namaḥ to the upper lip; 4 *aiṃ* namaḥ to the lower lip; 4 *oṃ* namaḥ to the upper teeth; 4 *auṃ* [to the lower teeth].

Namaḥ to the lower teeth (4 times); aṃ namaḥ to the head (4 times); aḥ namaḥ to the forehead (4 times); kaṃ namaḥ to the right shoulder (4 times); khaṃ namaḥ to the elbow (4 times); gaṃ namaḥ to the wrist (4 times); ghaṃ namaḥ to the base of the fingers (4 times);
ṅaṃ namaḥ to the tips of the fingers (4 times); caṃ namaḥ to the left shoulder (4 times); chaṃ to the elbow; jaṃ namaḥ to the wrist (4 times).
Jhaṃ, salutation to the base of the fingers; Ñaṃ, salutation to the tips of the fingers; Ṭaṃ, salutation to the right calf;

Ṭhaṃ, salutation to the knee; Ḍaṃ, salutation to the ankle; Ḍhaṃ, salutation to the base of the fingers; Ṇaṃ, salutation to the tips of the fingers; Taṃ, salutation to the left calf; Thaṃ, salutation to the knee; Daṃ, salutation to...

4 *dhaṃ* namas to the ankle; 4 *naṃ* namas to the base of the fingers; 4 *paṃ* namas to the tips of the fingers; 4 *phaṃ* namas to the right side; 4 *baṃ* namas to the left side; 4 *bhaṃ* namas to the back; 4 *maṃ* namas to the navel;
4 *yaṃ* namas to the skin-self at the heart; 4 *raṃ* namas to the blood-self at the right shoulder.

Laṃ, salutation to the self of flesh, at the hump [of the neck]. 4. Vaṃ, salutation to the self of fat, on the left shoulder. 4. Śaṃ, salutation to the self of bone, from the heart to the right hand. 4. Ṣaṃ, salutation to the self of marrow, from the heart to the left hand. 4. Saṃ, salutation to the self of semen, from the heart to the right foot. 4. Haṃ.

*Prāṇātmane namaḥ* from the heart to the left foot; *laṃ jīvātmane namaḥ* from the feet to the heart; *kṣaṃ paramātmane namaḥ* from the heart to the crown of the head. This is the external Mātṛkā-nyāsa. [See verses 17 on pages 23–24 of the Stotra. Now, [The ritual continues...]
The meditation on Mātṛkā:
[One should meditate on her] whose form consists of the fifty letters, adorned with a crown of matted hair and the moon,
resembling pure crystal, and resplendent in pure silken garments.
I bow to the Supreme Goddess, who bears a rosary, a water-pot, a book, and the gesture of granting boons, and whose ornaments shimmer with pearls and gems.

Having thus meditated upon the Mātṛkā, one should perform the placement of the Vidyā (vidyānyāsa): *aiṃ* salutation to the wrist, *klīṃ* salutation to the palm, *sauṃ* salutation to the tips of the fingers—thus on the right hand. *Aiṃ* salutation to the wrist, *klīṃ* salutation to the palm... [and so forth].

*Saum*, salutation to the tips of the fingers—thus on the left hand; *aim*, salutation to the right shoulder; *klīm*, salutation to the elbow; *saum*, salutation to the palm; *aim*, salutation to the right calf; *klīm*, salutation to the knee; *saum*, salutation to the tip of the foot; *aim*, salutation to the left calf; *klīm*, salutation to the knee; *saum*, salutation to the tip of the foot. Thus.
The placement of the Vidyā-mantras.
Now, the internal sacrifice (antaryajana):
One should contemplate the Root-Vidyā in the Mūlādhāra, possessing a luster equal to ten million flashes of lightning,
resembling ten million suns, and as cool as ten million moons.
O Beloved, O lady of excellent countenance, she whose nature is like a spider's thread, who possesses three circles of points,
[is realized] through the spontaneous descent of the upward-pointing power.
Through the firmness of the root power and the awakening of the central power,
one should contemplate the Self as a mass of supreme bliss.

Having thus performed the internal sacrifice (antaryajana), one should then perform the deposition of the seats (pīṭhanyāsa): Oṃ Aiṃ Śrīṃ Hrīṃ, obeisance to Ādhāraśakti; obeisance to Prakṛti; obeisance to Maṇḍūka; obeisance to Kamaṭha; obeisance to Pṛthivī; obeisance to Sudhāmbudhi.

"Obeisance to Maṇidvīpa; obeisance to Cintāmaṇigṛha; obeisance to Ratnavedikā; obeisance to Maṇidvīpa. Thus, above and above in all directions, [he offered] obeisance to the various hosts of sages, obeisance to the various Vedas. On the right shoulder, obeisance to Dharma; on the left shoulder, obeisance to Jñāna; on the left thigh—

Salutation to Vairāgya (Dispassion) on the right thigh; salutation to Aiśvarya (Sovereignty) on the right side of the abdomen; salutation to Adharma (Unrighteousness) on the right back; salutation to Ajñāna (Ignorance) on the left back; salutation to Avairāgya (Non-dispassion) on the left side of the abdomen; salutation to Anaiśvarya (Lack of sovereignty) on the left thigh;
again, from above upwards, salutation to Śeṣa at the heart; salutation to Padma (the Lotus).
Salutation to the petals consisting of *prakṛti*; salutation to the filaments consisting of *vikṛti*;
salutation to the pericarp adorned with the fifty seed-syllables; above that, salutation to the solar disc (*sūryamaṇḍala*);
salutation to the lunar disc (*somamaṇḍala*); salutation to the fire disc (*vaiśvānaramaṇḍala*); *saṃ*, salutation to *sattva*; *raṃ*.
Salutation to Rajas; salutation to Tamas; *Āṃ*, salutation to the Self (*ātman*); *Aṃ*, salutation to the Inner Self (*antarātman*);

*Paṃ*, salutation to the Supreme Self (*paramātman*); *Hrīṃ*, salutation to the Self of Knowledge (*jñānātman*). Upon the petals: salutation to Vāmā; salutation to Jyeṣṭhā; salutation to Raudrī; salutation to Ambikā; salutation to Icchā; salutation to Jñānā.

Salutation to Kriyā, salutation to Kubjikā, salutation to Citrā, salutation to Viṣaghnikā, salutation to Aparā (Aiṃ), salutation to Parā (Aiṃ Aiṃ), salutation to Sadāśiva Mahāpreta Padmāsana (Hasauṃḥ), salutation to Śivamañca. Thus ends the Pīṭhanyāsa.
57) Then, one should meditate on the Root Goddess in the center of the lotus of one’s own heart:
Oṃ! She has the luster of the rising sun, wears a crown of the moon, possesses lofty breasts, and is endowed with three eyes.

I worship Bhuvaneśī, whose face is smiling, and who displays the gestures of granting boons, fearlessness, and protection [or who holds the gestures of granting boons, the goad, the noose, and fearlessness].
Thus, having meditated on the form of Mūladevī, worshipped her with mental offerings (mānasopacāra), performed the fire-oblation (homa) and other rites according to one's capacity,
and contemplated the Kāmakalā, one should meditate upon Śrī Bhuvaneśvarī in her previously described form above that [Kāmakalā] and seat her upon one’s own left side.

Now, regarding the placement of the arghya vessel: having prepared on one's left side a mandala consisting of a square with an outer circle, within which is a triangle, which in turn is situated within a hexagon;
and having further fashioned on the ground to one's right a mandala consisting of a triangle, a circle, and a bindu.
There, having worshipped the foundational power (ādhāra-śakti) and placed the support (ādhāra) there,

one should place upon it a vessel such as a conch that has been purified with the Astra-mantra and filled with water using the Hṛdaya-mantra; then, having invoked the sacred waters (tīrtha) therein and worshipped them with perfumes and other offerings while reciting the Praṇava (Oṃ).

Having worshipped with the digits of the sun, moon, and fire, one should display the *dhenumudrā* and worship with one's own mantra; this is the general procedure. With that water from the general *arghya*, having sprinkled the mandala prepared on one's left side, one should perform the worship of the pedestal (*pīṭhapūjā*) there in the sequence beginning with the foundational power (*ādhāraśakti*).

Having washed the base with "namaḥ" and placed it upon the mandala, one should worship it with the mantra: "Oṃ raṃ, obeisance to the fire-mandala consisting of ten kalās. Then, having washed the water-pot (kalaśa) with the mantra "phaṭ," filled it with the causal substance (kāraṇa), adorned it with red garlands and other ornaments, and established it with the thought that it is the Goddess herself, [one should worship] with "aṃ..."

Having worshipped with "Oṃ, obeisance to the solar orb consisting of twelve kalās," and having worshipped in the center of the substance with "Oṃ Saḥ, obeisance to the lunar orb consisting of sixteen kalās," one should protect it with "Phaṭ," veil it with "Huṃ," gaze upon the substance with the root mantra, sprinkle it with water while saying "Namaḥ," and [finally] with the root mantra.
Having smelled the substance and offered a flower into the pitcher, one should recite the mantra that removes the curse:
"The Supreme Brahman alone is eternal, consisting of both the gross and the subtle; by that [truth], I destroy your sin of killing a Brahmin, which has arisen from the hair. (1)
O Goddess, born from the solar disc, arisen from the abode of Varuṇa, composed of the seed-syllable Amā— may [this person] be liberated from the curse of Śukra.
If the *praṇava* is the seed of the Vedas and consists of the bliss of Brahman,
by that truth, O Goddess, may it remove your sin of killing a Brahmin.

Thus one should recite three times: "Oṃ aiṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ vrāṃ vrīṃ vrūṃ vraiṃ vrauṃ vraḥ, obeisance to the Goddess Surā, who is liberated from the curse of Brahmā; svadhā. Thus three times. "Oṃ aiṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ krāṃ krīṃ krūṃ kraiṃ krauṃ kraḥ, O Sure, release [her] from the curse of Kṛṣṇa."
p. 58) *mocaya amṛtaṃ srāvaya srāvaya svāhā*—recite this three times. Then: *oṃ aiṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ śāṃ śīṃ śūṃ śaiṃ śauṃ śaḥ sure śukraśāpaṃ mocaya mocaya amṛtaṃ srāvaya*.

"srāvaya svāhā"—thus three times; "oṃ haṃsaḥ śuciṣad vasur antarikṣasaddhotā vedisad atithir duroṇasat | nṛṣad varasad ṛtasad vyomasad abjā gojā ṛtajā adrijā ṛtaṃ bṛhat"—thus three times. Holding the jar with his hand, he should recite these mantras.
Then, having meditated upon Ānandabhairava and the vowels there in the manner previously described, one should worship them with their respective mantras:
"Oṃ ha sa kṣa ma la va ra yūṃ, vauṣaṭ to Ānandabhairava," and "Oṃ sa ha kṣa ma la va ra yīṃ, vauṣaṭ to Surādevī. Having worshipped them separately with these two mantras, [one should proceed].

Having satisfied [the deities], one should then draw the *mātṛkā-cakra* in three rows, turning clockwise, in the midst of the substances—namely, *aṃ* (16 times), *kaṃ* (16 times), and *thaṃ* (16 times). Having thus drawn the *śakti-cakra*, one should write *haṃ* and *kṣaṃ* in its center;
by means of their immersion (*samāveśa*), one should contemplate nectar (*amṛta*) in the midst of the substances.

Having rendered [the substance] nectarine by means of the Dhenu-mudrā, and having held the vessel while reciting the syllable *vaṃ*— the seed-syllable of nectar— and the root-mantra eight times; then, between oneself and the Śrī-cakra,
having drawn a mandala consisting of a triangle, a hexagon, a circle, and a square, one should worship within the square.
Having worshipped with "Oṃ, salutation to Pūrṇagiri-pīṭha; salutation to Uḍḍīyāna-pīṭha; salutation to Kāmarūpa-pīṭha;

salutation to Jālandhara-pīṭha," one should worship the six limbs (ṣaḍaṅga) within the hexagon. Then, having worshipped the front, right, and left [corners] of the triangle with the three parts of the root mantra, one should worship Ādhāraśakti and the others in the center.

Having worshipped [the vessel] and placed the tripod within the triangle, one should sprinkle it with the water of the general *arghya* while reciting "Namaḥ," and worship it with sandalwood paste and unbroken rice grains in hand. Having worshipped it with "Oṃ Raṃ,
obeisance to the fire-mandala consisting of ten kalās," one should worship [the individual kalās] with "Yaṃ, obeisance to Dhūmrārcis" and "Raṃ..."

Having worshipped with: *ūṣmāyai namaḥ* (salutation to Ūṣmā), *laṃ jvalinyai namaḥ* (salutation to Jvalinī), *vaṃ jvālinyai namaḥ* (salutation to Jvālinī), *śaṃ visphulliṅginyai namaḥ* (salutation to Visphulliṅginī), *ṣaṃ suśriyai namaḥ* (salutation to Suśrī), *saṃ surūpāyai namaḥ* (salutation to Surūpā), *haṃ kapilāyai namaḥ* (salutation to Kapilā), *laṃ havyavāhāyai namaḥ* (salutation to Havyavāhā), and *kṣaṃ kavyavāhāyai namaḥ* (salutation to Kavyavāhā); then [one should touch] the vessel with *phaṭ*.
Having washed [the vessel] with the mantra and placed it upon a triangle, one should worship it with:
"Oṃ, obeisance to the solar orb consisting of twelve kalās. Then: "Kaṃ Bhaṃ, obeisance to Tapinī;
Khaṃ Baṃ, obeisance to Tāpinī; Gaṃ Phaṃ, obeisance to Dhūmrā; Ghaṃ Paṃ, obeisance to Marīcī; Ḍaṃ Naṃ..."
Having worshipped with: *caṃ* salutation to Jvālinī; *chaṃ* salutation to Ruci; *jaṃ* salutation to Suṣumṇā;
*jhaṃ* salutation to Bhogadā; *ñaṃ* salutation to Viśvā; *ṭaṃ* salutation to Bodhinī;
*ṭhaṃ* salutation to Dhāriṇī; and *ḍaṃ* salutation to Kṣamā.

Having drawn a triangle, a circle, and a hexagon, and having worshipped them with the mantra both in its entirety and in its individual parts, one should recite the seed-syllable *vaṃ* (the seed of Varuṇa), the root-mantra, and the Mātṛkā in reverse order; then, filling three parts with the substance and one part with water, and having placed perfumes and other offerings therein, [one should offer] *oṃ saḥ somamaṇḍalāya*.
Having worshipped with "Obeisance to the one whose self consists of sixteen digits," [one worships the vowels]: *aṃ* obeisance to Amṛtā; *āṃ* obeisance to Mānadā;
*iṃ* obeisance to Pūṣā; *īṃ* obeisance to Tuṣṭi; *uṃ* obeisance to Puṣṭi; *ūṃ* obeisance to Rati;
*ṛṃ* obeisance to Dhṛti; *ṝṃ* obeisance to Śaśinī; *ḷṃ* obeisance to Candrikā; *ḹṃ* obeisance to Kānti.
Oṃ *eṃ*, salutation to Jyotsnā;
Oṃ *aiṃ*, salutation to Śrī; Oṃ, salutation to Prīti; Oṃ *auṃ*, salutation to Aṅgadā; Oṃ *aṃ*, salutation to Pūrṇā.

Having worshipped with "Aḥ, obeisance to Pūrṇāmṛtā," one should draw the triangle wheel (cakra) starting from the 'a-katha' letters as before upon the substance; having worshipped the triangle with the three sections of the root mantra and worshipped the six limbs (ṣaḍaṅga) within the hexagon,
one should invoke the sacred waters (tīrtha) with "O Gaṅgā, O Yamunā," and so forth, and [invoke] Ānandabhairava and Bhairavī.

Having worshipped with their respective mantras, one should worship the five jewels (pañcaratna) as follows: "Glūṃ, obeisance to the jewels of the sky (gaganaratna) in the east; Slūṃ, obeisance to the jewels of heaven (svargaratna) in the south; Glūṃ, obeisance to the jewels of the mortal world (martyaratna) in the west; Plūṃ, obeisance to the jewels of the netherworld (pātālaratna) in the north; Nlūṃ, obeisance to the jewels of the serpents (nāgaratna) in the east."

Having worshipped the first vessel, then having placed the second and subsequent vessels upon the mandalas in front, one should veil them with "Hūṃ," transform them into nectar by means of the *dhenu-mudrā* with "Vaṃ," perform the three claps of the fingers (*tālatraya*),
the snapping of the fingers (*choṭikā*) to bind the directions, and cover the vessel with the *matsya-mudrā*.

Having recited the root mantra seven times over that [first vessel], one should contemplate the consecrated vessel—beginning with the second—as being in the form of the Goddess, each with its own respective mantra. Then, having obtained the permission of the Goddess, they should place eleven vessels near the jar: the Guru-vessel, the Śakti-vessel, the Bhoga-vessel, and the Svapātra (one's own vessel).

Having established these vessels— the Yoginī vessel, the Baṭuka vessel, the Vīra vessel, the Bali vessel, the Pādya vessel, the Arghya vessel, and the Ācamanīya vessel— and having filled them with the substance for chewing (carvaṇa),
one should take a drop from the Śrīpātra using the Tattvamudrā while reciting: *ha sa kṣa ma la va ra yūṃ*.

Having offered libations three times with "I satisfy Ānandabhairava; obeisance," and having offered libations three times at the end of the *pādukā* mantra with "I satisfy the venerable [Name]ānandanātha’s *śrīpādukā*;
obeisance," and likewise having satisfied the supreme guru, the supreme preceptor, and the supreme elder, then—

Having offered libations three times with the nectar from the Śrīpātra, reciting at the end of the root mantra: "I satisfy the venerable Bhuvaneśvarī—along with her weapons, her vehicle, her retinue, her mudrās, and her attendants;
obeisance"—and having once again adorned the jar with perfumes, garlands, and other offerings, one should meditate upon it as the form of the Goddess, consisting of nectar.
One should meditate upon the jar. Thus ends the procedure for the worship of the jar.

Then, upon the seat arranged atop the lion-throne, one should perform the worship of the pedestal (*pīṭhapūjā*) as before: *oṃ aiṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ*, salutation to the Support-Energy (*ādhāraśakti*), salutation to the Root-Nature (*mūlaprakṛti*), salutation to Maṇḍuka, salutation to Kamaṭha, salutation to Śeṣa, salutation to the Earth, salutation to the Ocean of Nectar (*sudhāmbudhi*).

Salutations to Maṇidvīpa; salutations to Kalpavana; salutations to Cintāmaṇigṛha; salutations to Ratnavaidikā; salutations to the pedestal inlaid with various jewels; salutations to the hosts of various sages in the cardinal directions;
salutations to the hosts of various Siddhas; salutations to Dharma; salutations to Jñāna; salutations to Vairāgya.
Salutation to Sovereignty; salutation to Non-sovereignty; salutation to the central bulb;
salutation to the stalk; salutation to the lotus; salutation to the petals consisting of primordial nature (*prakṛti*);
salutation to the filaments consisting of transformation (*vikṛti*); salutation to the pericarp adorned with the seed-syllables of the fifty Mothers.
In the center of that: *Aṃ* salutation to the solar disc (*sūryamaṇḍala*); *Saḥ* salutation to the lunar disc (*somamaṇḍala*);
*Raṃ* salutation to the disc of Vaiśvānara; *Saṃ* salutation to Sattva; *Raṃ* salutation to Rajas; *Taṃ* salutation to Tamas;
*Āṃ* salutation to the Self (*ātman*); *Aṃ* salutation to the Inner Self (*antarātman*); *Paṃ* salutation to the Supreme Self (*paramātman*); *Hrīṃ*.
Salutation again to the one whose nature is knowledge (*jñānātman*). On the petals: salutation to Vāmā; salutation to Jyeṣṭhā;
salutation to Raudrī.
Salutation to Ambikā; salutation to Icchā; salutation to Jñānā; salutation to Kriyā; salutation to Kubjikā;
salutation to Citrā; salutation to Viṣaghnikā; *aiṃ* salutation to Aparā; *aiṃ* salutation to Parā;
*sarvatrah-sauṃḥ* salutation to the throne of Sadāśiva Mahāpreta.
Having worshipped the pedestal with the mantra "Obeisance to Śivamañca," one should place the Śrīcakra upon the pedestal:
one should draw an eight-petaled lotus on the outside surrounded by sixteen petals,
and in the center of the pericarp, a most beautiful hexagon.
One should practice the underground chamber (bhūgṛha) in that same manner; thus one should extract the wheel (cakra).
And in another opinion:
[it consists of] a point (bindu), a triangle, and a union with six corners (rasakoṇa).
This Śrīcakra, adorned with a circular petal of the Nāga [the eight-petaled lotus] and marked by three circles of sixty-four petals and the Bhūgṛha (Earth-house),
is dear to the Goddess of the Universe.
Having thus established the Śrīcakra and having offered some red flowers and water upon it,
one should worship the Pīṭha-śaktis: in the cardinal directions, *Āṃ* Ajayāyai namaḥ, *Īṃ* Vijayāyai namaḥ,
*Ūṃ* Ajitāyai namaḥ, *Ṛṃ* Aparājitāyai namaḥ, *Ḷṃ* Nityāyai namaḥ, *Aiṃ* Vilāsinyai namaḥ, *Auṃ*.
"Oṃ, salutation to Dogdhrī; salutation to Aghorā. In the center, salutation to Maṅgalā Hrīṃ. Having thus worshipped the pedestal (pīṭha), one should meditate upon Śrī Bhuvaneśvarī as described:
"Oṃ, [I meditate on her] who has the brilliance of the rising sun, who wears the moon as a crown, whose breasts are full, and who is endowed with three eyes."
I worship Bhuvaneśī, whose face is smiling and who displays the gestures of granting boons, bestowing fearlessness, and dispelling dread.

Having meditated thus, one should bring the Goddess from one's own heart into the handful of flowers by means of the seed-syllable *Yam*, the seed of air, through the left nostril; having invoked her there, one should pray:
"Oṃ! O Queen of Gods, easily accessible through devotion, accompanied by your retinue!"
O Goddess, as long as I shall worship you, so long remain here.

At the end of the root mantra: O Śrīmat-Śrī-Maheśvara, together with your vehicle, retinue, weapons, ocean [of attendants], and all your equipment—thus, be present here, be present here! Thus, be firmly established here, be firmly established here! Thus, accept, accept my worship accompanied by all ritual offerings, svāhā!

Having thus displayed the nine mudrās beginning with the invocation (āvāhana), and having offered a flower upon the seat, one should then perform the consecration of the vital breaths (prāṇapratiṣṭhā) by forming the lolling tongue mudrā (lelihānamudrā) over the Śrīcakra.
Oṃ āṃ hrīṃ kroṃ yaṃ raṃ laṃ vaṃ śaṃ ṣaṃ saṃ haṃ saḥ.
The vital breaths (prāṇas) of the illustrious Śrī Bhuvaneśvarī are here, her vital breaths are here; her life-force (jīva) is established here. || 21 || || 21 ||
All the sense-faculties are situated here; they are situated here. || 21 ||

Having performed the installation of the vital breaths (*prāṇapratiṣṭhā*) with the mantra: "May speech, mind, skin, eyes, ears, tongue, nose, and life-breath come here itself and remain happily for a long time, Svāhā," one should place a flower on the seat, perform the binding of the directions (*digbandhana*),
veil [the deity], effect the ritual of the limbs (*sakalīkaraṇa*), and perform the rite of supreme transformation (*paramīkaraṇa*), [concluding] with the *dhenu* and *yoni* mudrās.

Having displayed the Śakti-mudrā, and having displayed the mudrās of the boon-granting gesture, fearlessness, the book, the rosary, the knowledge-goad, the bow, the arrow, the skull-garland, and so forth, one should then,
with the Puṣpahasta-mudrā and the nectar from the Śrīpātra, [worship] her together with her weapons and her vehicle.

"Obeisance, I satiate the illustrious Śrī Bhuvaneśvarī, together with her retinue, together with the ocean, together with the enclosure, accompanied by the illustrious Śrī Maheśvara-Bhairava. Having thus satiated [her] three times upon the *pīṭha*, one should again, at the end of the root mantra, satiate her three times, saying: "Obeisance, I satiate the sandals of the illustrious Śrī Bhuvaneśvarī. Now...

One should perform the sixteen-fold ritual service (*ṣoḍaśopacāra-pūjā*). At the end of the root mantra: "This water for the feet (*pādya*) is offered to the venerable Śrī Bhuvaneśvarī, together with the venerable Śrī Bhairava; *namaḥ* to the feet. [Offer] the water for the feet at the feet. At the end of the root mantra: "This water of honor (*arghya*)—*svāhā* to the head. [Offer] the water of honor at the head. At the end of the root mantra: "This water for sipping (*ācamanīya*)—*svāhā* to the root. [Offer] the water for sipping at the root. At the end of the root mantra: "This honey-mixture (*madhuparka*)—*svadhā*. [Offer] the honey-mixture at the root.
Having bathed [the deity] well with "This bathing water, obeisance to the entire body" and so forth at the mouth and the end of the root mantra,
and having wiped the limbs with a clean silk cloth, one should then [offer] variegated silken garments, saffron, musk, sandalwood, vermilion, a crown, earrings, garlands, and so forth upon the image.
Then, having offered the fragrance with the mudrā formed by the tips of the middle, ring, and thumb fingers, reciting the root mantra at the end with "this fragrance, namaḥ";

then, having offered the flowers with the mudrā formed by the tips of the thumb and forefinger, reciting the root mantra at the end with "these flowers, vauṣaṭ"; and then, having consecrated the incense vessel with "phaṭ" and placed it before [the deity].
Touching [the bell] with the index finger of the left hand, at the end of the root mantra, offer incense with "I present incense; *namaḥ*," and having offered water,
then worship the bell with perfumes and other offerings using the mantra "Oṃ jagaddhvani mantramātaḥ svāhā," while ringing the bell with the left hand.
Lifting the incense vessel with the middle finger, ring finger, and thumb of the right hand while reciting the Gāyatrī and the root mantra:
*Oṃ, born from the essence of the forest tree, rich in fragrance, the most excellent scent.*
May this incense, worthy of being smelled by all the gods, be accepted.
At the end of the root mantra,

one should offer incense to the glorious Śrī Maheśvara, together with his vehicle, retinue, weapons, ocean-like [attendants], equipment, coverings, and the goddess. Then, having placed a lamp-vessel in front, one should perform the sprinkling (prokṣaṇa) as before.
Having performed the worship, touching the lamp-vessel with the middle finger of the left hand,
one should offer the lamp as before, saying "I offer the lamp," while sprinkling water with the right hand;
then, sounding the bell as before, one should place the right hand between the middle and ring fingers.
Holding the lamp-vessel with the thumb and showing it while reciting the root *gāyatrī*:
(p. 62) *Oṃ suprakāśo mahādīpaḥ sarvatra timirāpahaḥ* || 1 ||
May this lamp, whose light is both internal and external, be accepted.

Thus, as before, one should illuminate the Goddess with the mantra "I offer the lamp; obeisance" (*iti pūrvavad dīpaṃ nivedayāmi namaḥ*). Then, having fashioned a *caru* (sacrificial oblation) in the shape of the moon upon an eight-petaled lotus made with saffron in a vessel of leaves or similar material, and having placed a single lamp in the center of the vessel and eight lamps on the eight petals, one should worship it with: *Śrīṃ Sauṃḥ Glūṃ*.

Having worshipped the vessel with the mantra *slūṃ mlūṃ plūṃ nlūṃ sauṃ śrīṃ śrīṃ ratnaiśvaryai namaḥ* and having worshipped it again with the root mantra (*mūla*), then, sounding the bell with the left hand and lifting the bowl with the right hand up to the forehead while reciting the root mantra nine times—
O Goddess, composed of nine aspects and joined with all the goddesses who are mistresses of the wheels,
accept this *ārārtika* for my accomplishment.

Thus, with the *cakramudrā*. Then, having placed various food offerings (*naivedya*) into a vessel made of gold or other materials, one should veil them with "Hūṃ," transform them into nectar with the *dhenumudrā* while reciting "Vaṃ," and mutter the root mantra seven times. While touching the food-offering vessel with the thumb of the left hand, at the end of the root mantra—
O Supreme Goddess, accept this divine, well-prepared supreme rice-offering (paramānna), contained in a golden vessel, prepared in five ways and endowed with the six flavors.
"I offer this food offering (naivedya) to Śrī Bhuvaneśvarī; obeisance.

Then, with the right ring finger and thumb, one should release the food-offering vessel. Having again given water for sipping (ācamanīya), one should offer betel-leaf (tāmbūla) mixed with camphor and other ingredients, saying "I offer [this]," as before, for all [the deities].

In the center, the offering of water (utsarga) should be performed. Then, having thrice satiated the Goddess with the nectar from the Śrīpātra using the Tattvamudrā, one should display the previously mentioned mudrās and likewise display the Yonimudrā: Kṣobhiṇī at the heart, Drāviṇī at the mouth, Ākarṣiṇī between the eyebrows, and Vaśinī on the forehead.
Having displayed the *yonimudrā*, which consists of the five *mudrās* beginning with *āhlādinī* at the *brahmarandhra*,
and then, with palms joined in reverence (*kṛtāñjali*), having obtained permission by saying, "O Śrī Bhuvaneśvarī, I shall worship your enclosures (*āvaraṇas*"),
one should begin the worship of the enclosures: in the center of the pericarp (*karṇikā*), [one recites] *oṃ aiṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ hṛllekhāyai namaḥ*.

In the east: *aiṃ* homage to Gaṅgā; in the south: homage to Raktā; in the north: *iṃ* homage to Karālikā; in the west: homage to Mahocchuṣmā—this is the first enclosure (*prathamāvaraṇa*). In the southeast: *oṃ hrāṃ* homage to the heart; in the southwest: *oṃ hrīṃ* *svāhā* to the head; in the northwest: *oṃ hrūṃ*.

To the tuft (śikhā), Vaṣaṭ, in the northeast; Oṃ Hraiṃ, to the armor (kavaca), Huṃ, at the front part; Oṃ Hrauṃ, to the three eyes (netratraya), Vauṣaṭ, in the cardinal directions; Oṃ Hraḥ, to the weapon (astra), Phaṭ, in the center. [Recite] the root mantra again. Then, in the six corners: in the east, obeisance to Brahmā together with Gāyatrī; in the southwest...
Salutation to Viṣṇu accompanied by Sāvitrī in the northwest; salutation to Rudra accompanied by Sarasvatī in the northeast (p.
salutation to Kubera accompanied by Lakṣmī in the southeast; [salutation] in the west.
Salutation to Madana accompanied by Rati in the northeast; salutation to Vighnarāja accompanied by Puṣṭi [in the northeast];
salutation to Śaṅkhanidhi and salutation to Padmanidhi on the two sides of the hexagon. Again, in the filaments starting from the southeast:
in the southeast, *oṃ hrāṃ* to Hṛdayaśakti; in the northeast, *oṃ hrīṃ*.
Oṃ, homage to the Power of the Head (Śiraḥ-śakti) in the northwest; Oṃ hrūṃ, homage to the Power of the Crest (Śikhā-śakti) in the southwest;

Oṃ hraiṃ, homage to the Power of the Armor (Kavaca-śakti) in the southeast; Oṃ hrauṃ, homage to the Power of the Eyes (Netra-śakti) in the cardinal directions; Oṃ hraḥ, homage to the Power of the Weapon (Astra-śakti) in the center—[with] the Root Mantra (mūla). This is the second enclosure. Then:
In the eight petals starting from the east: Oṃ Aiṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ, obeisance to Anaṅgakusumā;
obeisance to Anaṅgakusumāturā; obeisance to Anaṅgamadanā; obeisance to Anaṅgamadanāturā; obeisance to Bhuvanapālā; obeisance to Gaganavegā; obeisance to Śaśirekhā.
"Salutation to Gaganarekhā," with the root mantra in the center—this is the third enclosure. Then, having worshipped [the deities] on the sixteen petals starting from the east:
"The wise declare that the direction between the worshipper and the one being worshipped is called the East."

Oṃ aiṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ. Salutation to Karālī; salutation to Vikarālī; salutation to Umā; salutation to Sarasvatī; salutation to Śrī; salutation to Durgā; salutation to Uṣā; salutation to Lakṣmī; salutation to Śruti; salutation to Smṛti; salutation to Dhṛti; salutation to Śraddhā; salutation to Medhā.
"Obeisance to Mati, obeisance to Kānti, obeisance to Āryā; in the center is the root mantra"—thus is the fourth enclosure.
Then, outside of the sixteen petals: *Oṃ aiṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ*, salutation to Anaṅgarūpā;
salutation to Anaṅgamadanā (2); salutation to Madanāturā (3); salutation to Bhuvanavegā (4);
salutation to Bhuvanapālinī (5); salutation to Sarvamadanā (6); [salutation] to Anaṅgavedanā.
Salutation! || 7 || Salutation to Anaṅgamekhalā! || 8 || "The root [mantra] in the center"—thus ends the fifth enclosure.
Then, outside of that: Oṃ Aiṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ, obeisance to Brāhmī. (1) Obeisance to Māheśvarī. (2)
Salutation to Kaumārī. || 3 || Salutation to Vaiṣṇavī. || 4 || Salutation to Vārāhī. || 5 || Salutation to Indrāṇī.

|| 6 || Salutation to Cāmuṇḍā. || 7 || Salutation to Mahālakṣmī. || 8 || In the center is the root mantra; then outside of that: Oṃ Aiṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ, salutation to Asitāṅgabhairava. || 1 || [Salutation] to Rurubhairava.
Homage! || 2 || Homage to Caṇḍabhairava! || 3 || Homage to Krodhabhairava! || 4 ||
Salutation to Unmattabhairava. (5) Salutation to Kapālabhairava. (6) Salutation to Bhīṣaṇabhairava.
(7) Salutation to Saṃhārabhairava. (8) In the center, the root mantra; thus ends the sixth enclosure.
Then, in the middle of the square: Oṃ aiṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ, obeisance to Indra (1). Obeisance to Agni (2).
Salutation to Dharmarāja. || 3 || Salutation to Nairṛta. || 4 || Salutation to Varuṇa. || 5 ||

Salutation to Vāyu || 6 || Salutation to Kubera || 7 || Salutation to Īśāna || 8 || Salutation to Brahmā in the northeast; salutation to Viṣṇu in the southwest; in the center, the root mantra—thus is the seventh enclosure.
Then, outside of that: Oṃ aiṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ, obeisance to Indra-śakti || 1 || Obeisance to Agni-śakti || 2 ||
Salutation to the power of Yama. || 3 ||

Salutation to the Śakti of Nairṛta. || 4 || Salutation to the Śakti of Varuṇa. || 5 || Salutation to the Śakti of Vāyu. || 6 || Salutation to the Śakti of Kubera. || 7 || Salutation to the Śakti of Īśāna. || 8 || Salutation to the Śakti of Brahmā.
Homage! || 9 || Homage to the Vaiṣṇava Śakti! || 10 || In the center—homage to the Vara-mudrā! || 1 ||
Salutation to Abhayamudrā. || 2 || Salutation to Japamālā. || 3 || Salutation to Pustakā. || 4 ||

In the center is the Root [Mantra]; this is the ninth enclosure (*navamāvaraṇa*). Then, within the subterranean chamber (*bhūgṛha*): Oṃ Aiṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ, obeisance to Vajraśakti (1). Obeisance to Śaktiśakti (2). Obeisance to Daṇḍaśakti (3). Obeisance to Khaḍgaśakti (4). Obeisance to Pāśaśakti (5). Obeisance to Aṅkuśaśakti (6). Obeisance to Gadāśakti (7).

*Namaḥ* || 7 || Salutation to the Trident-Power (*triśūla-śakti*). || 8 || Salutation to the Lotus-Power (*padma-śakti*). || 9 || Salutation to the Discus-Power (*cakra-śakti*). || 10 || In the center is the Root-Mantra; this is the tenth enclosure (*daśamāvaraṇa*). Then, outside of that: *Oṃ aiṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ*, salutation to Airāvata, salutation to the Ram, salutation to the Buffalo, salutation to the Preta, [salutation] to the Crocodile (*makara*).

Salutation to the deer, salutation to the man, salutation to the bull, salutation to the swan, salutation to Garuḍa, and salutation to the lion in the center. Then, outside of that: Oṃ Aiṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ, salutation to Airāvata-Śakti, salutation to Meṣa-Śakti, salutation to Mahiṣa-Śakti, salutation to Preta-Śakti.
Salutation to Makara-Śakti; salutation to Mṛga-Śakti; salutation to Nara-Śakti;

salutation to Vṛṣa-Śakti; salutation to Haṃsa-Śakti; salutation to Garuḍa-Śakti; salutation to Siṃha-Śakti. This is the eleventh enclosure (āvāraṇa). Then, according to the previous sequence: Oṃ Aiṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Ādityāya.
Salutation to Soma; salutation to Bhauma; salutation to Budha; salutation to Guru; salutation to Śukra;

salutation to Śanaiścara; salutation to Rāhu; salutation to Ketu in the center; then outside of that: *Oṃ Aiṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ*, salutation to the power of Āditya (*āditya-śakti*); salutation to the power of Soma (*soma-śakti*); salutation to the power of Bhauma (*bhauma-śakti*).

Salutation to the power of Mercury; salutation to the power of Jupiter; salutation to the power of Venus; salutation to the power of Saturn; salutation to the power of Rāhu; salutation to the power of Ketu in the center—thus is the twelfth enclosure.

Then, having worshipped and offered libations with the root mantra (mūla) in the center— reciting *oṃ aiṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ vāṃ vaṭukāya namaḥ* in the east, *yāṃ yoginībhyo namaḥ* in the south, *kṣāṃ kṣetrapālāya namaḥ* in the west, *glauṃ gaṇapataye namaḥ* in the north, and *huṃ sarvabhūteśvarāya namaḥ* in the northeast— one should then worship the enclosure (*āvaraṇa*).
One should meditate [on them]: Hṛllekhā and the others are to be worshipped, possessing a radiance equal to the five elements,
holding the gestures of granting boons, the noose, the goad, and fearlessness, and adorned with immeasurable ornaments.
Gāyatrī and Brahmā hold a staff, a water-pot, and a rosary;
Śaṅkha and Cakra and Gadā and Padma hold a conch, a discus, a mace, and a lotus; Sāvitrī and Viṣṇu wear yellow garments;
and Sarasvatī and Maheśvara hold an axe, a rosary, and a hand in the gesture of granting fearlessness.

Kubera stands holding a jewel-pitcher and a jeweled casket in his pot-bellied hands; he wears yellow garments and embraces Mahālakṣmī—who holds a lotus—in his right arm with her seated upon his lap, while his left arm rests around her. He holds an arrow, a noose, and a goad in his [other] hands, wears red garlands and robes, and holds sweetmeats in his hand.
Embracing Rati with his right hand while holding an utpala lotus with his left, he—holding a goad and a noose in his hands—[presses] the vulva of his beloved with his hand.

Digambara Vighneśa is red in color and holds a jar filled with honey-wine (*mādhvīka*) in his *puṣkara* hand, while holding a cup in the other; Puṣṭi, who embraces him, is also red in color and naked, intoxicated with wine, holding a cup in her left hand, touching Gaṇeśa’s *liṅga* with the other, and holding a blue lotus.
Anaṅgarūpā and the others, however,
held in their lotus-like hands a wine-cup, a palm-leaf fan, betel, a bright umbrella, a chowrie, a parrot, and flowers.

Having performed the meditation on the worship of the enclosures (āvaraṇapūjādhyāna) beginning with "blazing with various ornaments," one should then worship the Divine Lineage (divyaugha), the Siddha Lineage (siddhaugha), and the Human Lineage (mānavaugha) individually within the three triangles arranged in three rows. Furthermore, having worshipped and gratified [the deities] in the Bindu with the root mantra, one should perform the five mudrās.
Then, having displayed [the offering], one should offer a handful of flowers with the *puṣpāñjali* mantra:

*oṃ yaddattaṃ bhaktimātreṇa patraṃ puṣpaṃ jalaṃ phalam | niveditaṃ ca naivedyaṃ tadgṛhāṇānukampayā ||* "Oṃ! Whatever leaf, flower, water, fruit, or offered food has been given through mere devotion, please accept that out of compassion."
Having thus offered five handfuls of flowers (*pañcapuṣpāñjali*), one should perform the fire-oblation (*homa*) with whatever substances are available, accompanied by other verses.
Having drawn and visualized the *cakra* either in the fire or in water, one should offer oblations with "To Prāṇa, Svāhā! To Apāna, Svāhā! To Vyāna, Svāhā!
To Udāna, Svāhā! To Samāna, Svāhā! and so forth, followed by "Oṃ Hrāṃ, to the Heart."

Having offered the six-limbed oblations beginning with "namaḥ svāhā," and having performed the fire-offerings for the retinue and the root goddess as described in their respective manuals, one should perform the homa with the Thousand Names, worship the Goddess, and ask for her forgiveness:
Oṃ! For those whose feet have stumbled upon the ground, the ground itself is the support;
for me, who have committed offenses against you, you alone are my refuge. (1)
A servant indeed commits an offense at every step;
who else in this world, save for a master, can endure it? (2)
Thousands of offenses are committed by me day and night;
O Mother, forgive all of this in my presence and before you. 3.
I do not know the invocation, I do not know the dismissal;
I do not know the nature of worship—O Supreme Goddess, you alone are my refuge! || 4 ||
In deed, thought, or speech, there is no other refuge for me;
O Supreme Goddess, protect me as you move within all beings! 5.
The Goddess is both the giver and the enjoyer; the Goddess is this entire world.
The Goddess is victorious everywhere; she who is the Goddess is indeed myself. (6)

Whatever may be deficient in syllables, whatever may be deficient in words or phonemes, and whatever may be lacking in measure or mantra—O Goddess of Gods, you ought to forgive it; for whose mind has not faltered? (7)
O Goddess of the gods! O Supreme Sovereign! Whatever has been deficient in substance, deficient in ritual action, or deficient in mantra—forgive all that out of your grace, O Goddess! || 8 ||
Whatever action I perform while awake, dreaming, or in deep sleep—may all that become worship unto You; salutations to Śivā, the source of prosperity! || 9 ||
Whatever I do from morning until evening, and from evening until morning, O Source of the Universe, may that be an act of worship unto You. (10)
Forgive me, O Goddess of the lords of gods, you who are the very essence of mantra;
may my devotion to your lotus feet be eternal and unwavering. (11)

Having thus asked the Goddess for forgiveness, and having again removed the *nirmālya* (remnants of the offering) and worshipped the Goddess once more, he should dismiss her into his own heart. Taking a handful of flowers, he should recite:
"Oṃ, go, go to the supreme abode, your own place, O Supreme Goddess!"
Wherein even the gods, beginning with Brahmā, do not know that supreme state.
Having thus offered a handful of flowers upon the pedestal, one should take the flower from the pedestal with the *saṃhāramudrā* [gesture of withdrawal]:
Oṃ, stay, stay in the supreme abode, your own place, O Supreme Goddess!
Therein, where all the gods beginning with Brahmā abide, [so may you] abide within my heart.

Having recited this, touching a flower to his heart, smelling it, he should place it upon his head. Then, having prepared a mandala in the northeast and worshipped with "Vāṃ, obeisance to Vaṭuka," [he should recite]: "Oṃ Aiṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ, come, come, O son of the Goddess, Lord Vaṭuka, radiant with a mass of tawny matted locks, three-eyed, flame-mouthed!"
"Destroy, destroy all obstacles! Accept, accept this *bali* offering together with all ritual services, *svāhā*!

Having offered the *bali* to Īśāna and Baṭuka with this mantra using the combination of the thumb and ring finger, one should draw a mandala in the south-east, worship it with "Oṃ, obeisance to the Yoginīs," and [offer] *oṃ aiṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ*.

Whether above the cosmic egg in heaven or in the expanse of the sky, on the surface of the earth, in the partless realm, or in the netherworld, in fire, in water, in wind, or wherever else one may be situated;
or having established oneself in sacred fields, seats, and secondary seats, with incense, lamps, and other offerings—
May the goddesses, who are always worshipped by the lords of heroes, protect us with their auspicious power through this rite of the bali offering.

Having offered the *bali* to the Yoginīs in the southeast corner with the mantra *yāṃ yoginībhyaḥ hūṃ phaṭ svāhā* using the gesture of the little finger and the thumb, [he should then offer it] in the southwest: *Oṃ aiṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ kṣāṃ kṣīṃ kṣūṃ kṣaiṃ kṣauṃ kṣaḥ, O Guardian of the Site and Field! Fulfill, fulfill all desires, together with the *ali* and *bali*!*
Having formed a mandala in the northwest corner with the mantra "baliṃ gṛhṇa gṛhṇa svāhā" and having worshipped it, [one should recite]:
"Śrāṃ gāṃ gīṃ gūṃ gaiṃ gauṃ gaḥ, O Gaṇapati, bestower of boons, bring all people under my control; accept this worship and offering, svāhā! using the elephant-trunk mudrā.

Having offered the *bali* to Gaṇapati with the words "one should offer the *bali*," and having prepared a mandala between the northeast (Īśāna) and the other [direction], one should offer the *bali* to all beings (*sarvabhūta*) with the mantra: "Oṃ Aiṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ, to all obstructors and to all beings, Huṃ Phaṭ Svāhā. Thereafter, one should also offer the *bali* of goat and other such offerings. Then—

Having meditated on the Guru at the head and the chosen deity (iṣṭadevatā) at the heart, having performed the recitation (japa) according to one's capacity, and having performed the breath control (prāṇāyāma), the [recitation of the] seers (ṛṣi) and so forth, and the six-limbed assignment (kara-ṣaḍaṅga-nyāsa), one should take water and say:
"Oṃ! You are the protector of that which is most secret; accept this recitation performed by us."
O Goddess, O Maheśvarī, may success be mine through your grace!
Having thus offered the fruit of the recitation, consisting of radiant light, into the left hand of the Goddess,
and having recited the armor (*kavaca*), the thousand-name hymn (*sahasranāma-stotra*), and so forth; and having prostrated with the eight limbs (*sāṣṭāṅga-praṇipāta*), circumambulated her,
and performed the salutation of the vessel (*pātra-vandana*) together with the initiates (*sāmayika*s);—
May all practitioners rejoice; may detractors perish.
May the state of Śambhu be mine, and may the Guru be forever gracious.

Having recited this and other verses of the *Śāntistotra*, having prepared a mandala in the northeast (īśāna), and having placed the remains of offerings (*nirmālya*) and so forth in the northeast while reciting "Oṃ, obeisance to the Goddess Dwelling in the Remains of Offerings (*Nirmālyavāsinī*"), one should take water and [recite]: "Oṃ Aiṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ!
From this moment, by virtue of my life-force, intellect, body, and authority over dharma, in the states of waking, dreaming, and deep sleep, through mind and speech..."
"Whatever has been thought by my actions, my two hands, my feet, my belly, and my genitals; whatever has been spoken;

and whatever has been done—all that, in its entirety, is mine, and let it be offered at the lotus-feet of Śrī Bhuvaneśvarī, svāhā! Having thus poured water at the front [of the vessel] with this mantra, one recites: "Oṃ tat sad brahma."
Having recollected [this], one should dwell at ease.

Thus ends the manual for the daily worship of Śrī Bhuvaneśvarī, within the *Daśavidyā-rahasya* of the *Śrī Rudrayāmala Tantra*. Saṃvat 1943, on Sunday, the 9th day of the bright fortnight of the month of Śrāvaṇa.
May there be prosperity! May there be auspiciousness!
Now, the armor: Om, salutation to Śrī Gaṇeśa. Of this Śrī Bhuvaneśvarī mantra, Śakti is the seer (ṛṣi) and Gāyatrī is the meter (chandaḥ).

Bhuvaneśvarī is the deity, *haṃ* is the seed-syllable (*bīja*), *īṃ* is the power (*śakti*), and *raṃ* is the peg (*kīlaka*). My application (*viniyoga*) is in this recitation for the sake of attaining my desired goal. Salutation to Śakti-Ṛṣi on the head; salutation to Gāyatrī-chandas on the face; salutation to the deity Śrī Bhuvaneśvarī on the heart; salutation to the seed-syllable *haṃ* on the private parts; salutation to the power *īṃ*.

*Raṃ* at the two feet, *kīlakāya namaḥ* on all limbs. *Oṃ hrāṃ* to the two thumbs, *namaḥ*; *hrīṃ* to the two index fingers, *namaḥ*; *hrūṃ* to the two middle fingers, *namaḥ*; *hraim* to the two ring fingers, *namaḥ*; *hrauṃ* to the two little fingers, *namaḥ*; *hraḥ* to the palms and backs of the hands, *namaḥ*. *Hrāṃ*.

Having performed the ritual placement (*nyāsa*) with "Hṛdayāya namaḥ," "Hrīṃ Śirase svāhā," "Hrūṃ Śikhāyai vaṣaṭ," "Hraiṃ Kavacāya huṃ," "Hrauṃ Netratrayāya vauṣaṭ," and "Hraḥ Astrāya phaṭ," one should meditate thus:
Oṃ! [I meditate on her] who possesses the brilliance of the rising sun, who wears a crown of moons, whose breasts are full, and who is endowed with three eyes.
I worship Bhuvaneśī, whose face is smiling and whose hands display the gestures of granting boons, the goad, the noose, and protection.
The Goddess said: "O Lord of Gods, whatever Vidyās have been revealed by Bhuvaneśī—all of them have been heard and mastered; now I desire to hear them."
O Mahādeva! Please recount that armor (kavaca) named Trailokyamaṅgala which was previously mentioned; it is supremely pleasing to me.
Īśvara said:
O Pārvatī, listen; I shall speak—attend with care—to the armor named Trailokyamaṅgala, which is the very embodiment of mantras. (3)
O Goddess, this consists of the perfected knowledge that bestows all sovereignty;
by reciting and retaining it, a mortal becomes a possessor of the sovereignty of the three worlds. (4)
The seer (ṛṣi) of this Trailokyamaṅgala armor is Śiva; the meter (chandas) is Virāṭ; and the deity (devatā) is Bhuvaneśvarī, the sustainer of the world. || 5 ||
The application for the sake of dharma, artha, kāma, and mokṣa has been proclaimed.
May the seed-syllable *hrīṃ* protect my head, and may Bhuvaneśī protect my forehead. (6)
Aiṃ, may she protect my right eye; Hrīṃ, may she protect my left eye;
Śrīṃ, may Maheśvarī, whose self consists of three syllables, protect my right ear.
May Aiṃ always protect my left ear; may Ghrāṇa protect me always.
May the Goddess Hrīṃ protect my face, and may Aiṃ protect my tongue.
May Vāk Tripurā, whose nature consists of three syllables, protect the throat; may she who is of the nature of Parā protect it constantly.
May Śrīṃ protect the shoulders, and may Hrīṃ always protect the arms. (9)
Klīm, may Tripureśānī, the bestower of sovereignty over the three cities, protect my two hands;
Śrīm (Ām), may she protect my heart, and Hrīm, may she always protect my middle region. || 10 ||
KROṂ—may she protect the region of the navel; may the three-syllabled Bhuvaneśvarī, the bestower of all seeds, protect [the heart].
May Śaṅkhinī, the bestower of life to all, protect the back; may Sarvavaśaṃkarī protect it. || 11 ||
Hrīṃ! May she protect my secret place; salutations to the Blessed Lady! May Māheśvarī always protect my hips and the pair of my knees with joy.
May Annapūrṇā always protect [me] with "svāhā"; may she protect the two feet;
may the seventeen-syllable mantra protect the entire body of Annapūrṇā. 13.
Tāra, Māyā, Ramā, and Kāma—this supreme mantra of twenty syllables, consisting of sixteen syllables followed by these, may she who resides in my head protect me at all times. (14)
“Tāraṃ durge yugaṃ rakṣiṇi svāhā”—this ten-syllable mantra;
may Jayadurgā, dark as a rain cloud, always protect me from the east. || 15 ||
This supreme [goddess], consisting of the seed-syllable *māyā* and so forth, as well as the ten-syllabled [mantra], is Jayadurgā;
she who has the luster of molten gold—may she protect me from fire. 16.
The supreme mantra consisting of eight syllables— *tāraṃ hrīṃ durgāyai namaḥ*—
may she who bears the conch, discus, bow, and arrows protect me from the south. (17)
May the supreme Mahiṣamardinī, whose essence is gold and wealth, who destroys the demon Mahiṣāsura, protect me always in the southwest. 18.

*Māyā Padmāvatī Svāhā*—may she always protect me in the west. [She is proclaimed as having seven syllables; Padmāvatī, seated upon a lotus, may she always protect me in the west. *Māyā Pāśāṅkuśapuṭā Pāhi Parameśvarī Svāhā*. [She is called *Māyā*, O Supreme Goddess.]
Svāhā. || 19 ||
The thirteen-syllable [mantra], mounted on a horse, may she protect [the practitioner] in the northwest;
Sarasvatī, with five arrows, O eternally moist one, O you who flow with passion! || 20 ||
May the three-syllabled Nityā Svāhā always protect me from the north. Then may the bride [or the wise one] constantly guard with *tāra*, *māyā*, *kavaca*, and *khe*. || 21 ||
Huṃ kṣeṃ hrīṃ phaṭ—may this twelve-syllabled Great Vidyā, the bestower of all things, protect me always in the northeast corner along with Tvaritā and the others. || 22 ||
Aiṃ Klīṃ Sauṃḥ! May Bālā protect me constantly from the region above; may Bhairavī Bālā, ending with the Bindu (Hsauṃ), protect me always upon the earth.
Thus, this meritorious armor has been told to you—the supreme auspiciousness of the three worlds, more essential than the essence itself, the embodiment of the flood of great vidyās. (24)
For by the constant recitation of this, even Kubera became the lord of wealth;
and by reciting and retaining it, all the gods, beginning with Indra, attained their status. (25)
Being masters of all accomplishments, they shall attain all sovereign powers.
Having offered eight handfuls of flowers, one should recite [the mantra] once with the root mantra alone. || 26 ||
He shall obtain the fruit of worship performed for an entire year; for by making her—who is otherwise indifferent—pleased, Kamalā becomes permanently established in his home.
And eloquence shall dwell in the mouth of that virtuous soul who bears this [mantra] named *Trailokyamaṅgalā*; this is the truth, the truth, there is no doubt.
Having donned this supreme armor, which is most meritorious, he too shall become the best among the virtuous;
endowed with all sovereign powers, he shall be a conqueror of the three worlds. (29)
A man [should apply it] on the right arm and likewise a woman on the left arm;
having become possessed of many sons, even a barren woman obtains a son. (30)
Weapons such as the Brahmāstra and others do not cut that person who, without knowing this armor, recites the mantra of Bhuvaneśvarī. (31)
Having fallen into extreme poverty, he shall soon meet his death.
Thus ends the *Bhuvaneśvarī-kavaca*, named *Trailokyamaṅgala*, within the dialogue between Pārvatī and Īśvara in the *Śrī Rudrayāmala Tantra*.
The Thousand Names of Śrī Bhuvaneśvarī.
Homage to Śrī Gaṇeśa.
The Goddess said:
O God of gods, O Mahādeva, you who are proficient in all the scriptures!
You who bear the skull-topped staff and the khaṭvāṅga, and who are smeared with the ashes of the funeral pyre! || 1 ||
The primordial, eternal Prakṛti, who is concealed in all scriptures—this is the meritorious thousand names of her, the illustrious Bhuvaneśvarī. (2)
"Tell me, O Mahādeva! How may the Goddess be propitiated?
Īśvara said:
"Well asked, O Mahādevī! This is indeed for the benefit of practitioners."
She who is the eternal, primordial nature, hidden in all the scriptures;
by the mere remembrance of whom one is liberated from all sins. (4)
From the propitiation of her, one becomes liberated while living;
of her, I shall indeed relate the thousand names in brief.

Oṃ. Of this *Sahasranāmastotra* of the illustrious Bhuvaneśvarī, Dakṣiṇāmūrti is the seer (*ṛṣi*), the Paṅkti is the meter (*chandaḥ*), the primordial Śrī Bhuvaneśvarī is the deity (*devatā*), Hrīṃ is the seed-syllable (*bīja*), Śrīṃ is the power (*śakti*), Klīṃ is the pin (*kīlaka*), and its application (*viniyoga*) is in my recitation for the sake of the attainment of virtue, wealth, desire, and liberation.
The primordial Māyā, the supreme Śakti, Śrīṃ Hrīṃ Klīṃ Bhuvaneśvarī; she who is the world, the creator of the world, the one to be attained, Bhavānī,
and the bringer of existence.
Rudrāṇī, devoted to Rudra, and likewise Satī, the beloved of Rudra;
Umā, Kātyāyanī, Durgā, Maṅgalā, and Sarvamaṅgalā. || 7 ||
Tripurā, the Supreme Sovereign; Tripurā, the beloved of Sundarī;
the Delighter, the Enchanting One, the Auspicious Rāmā, who performs the work of Rāma. || 8 ||
Brāhmī, Nārāyaṇī, Caṇḍī, Cāmuṇḍā, Muṇḍanāyikā, Māheśvarī, Kaumārī, Vārāhī, and Aparājitā. || 9 ||
Mahāmāyā, with disheveled hair, is Mahātripurasundarī;
she is beautiful, radiant, red in color, and clothed in red garments. (10)
Red-eyed and clad in red garments, she is most beautiful with her seeds of blood;
her limbs are sprinkled with red sandalwood, and she is ever fond of red flowers.
Kamalā, Kāminī, and Kāntā, she is ever beloved by the god of love.
Lakṣmī is fickle, with tremulous eyes; she is restless, impetuous, and dear to him.
Bhairavī is the remover of fear and the destroyer of great terror;
she is the terrifier, the most formidable, the slayer of fear, and the annihilator of fear.
In cremation grounds, in the wilderness, and in difficult places, she is remembered as the destroyer of fear;
she is Jayā, Vijayā, Jayapūrṇā, and the bestower of victory.
She is Yamunā, Yāmunā, Yāmyā, born of Yamunā [or the portion of Yama], and beloved by Yama;
she is the mother of all, the one to be born, the destroyer of people, and the increaser of people. || 15 ||
She is Kālī, Kapālinī, Kullā, Kālikā, and Kālarātrikā;
she dwells in the heart of Mahākāla and possesses the form of Kālabhairava.
She holds a skull and a khaṭvāṅga staff, and she wields a noose and a goad;
she is both fearless and fearful, as well as the destroyer of fear.
She is the bestower of great terror, and likewise she has a hand that grants boons.
Gaurī, fair-limbed, bright, and of golden complexion, she is the bestower of victory. || 18 ||
Ugrā, Ugraprabhā, Śānti, Śāntidā, and Aśāntināśinī; likewise Ugratārā, Ugrā, Nīlā, and Ekajaṭā. (19)
Hāṃ Hāṃ Hūṃ Hūṃ [in the form of a swan], likewise Tārā, and Siddhikālikā;
Nīlatārā, Vāgīśī, and likewise Nīlasarasvatī. || 20 ||

The Gaṅgā is Kāśī, she is the virtuous and the truthful; likewise, she consists of all sacred fords (tīrtha). She is the embodiment of sacred fords, meritorious through sacred fords, the giver of sacred fords, and the servant of sacred fords. || 21 ||
She is the giver of merit, the embodiment of merit, and the illuminator of meritorious fame;
she is the time of merit, the abode of merit, and likewise beloved by those who possess merit.
Tulasī, Totilā, Rādhikā, the one dear to Rādhana;
Satyā, Asatyā, Satyabhāmā, Rukmiṇī, the beloved of Kṛṣṇa. (23)
Devakī, the mother of Kṛṣṇa; Subhadrā of auspicious form; Manoharā; likewise Saumyā; Śyāmāṅgī; and Samadarśanā. || 24 ||
Of terrible form and terrible splendor, appearing both fierce and lovely;
a maiden, a young girl, small, yet assuming the form of a maiden. || 25 ||
A young woman in the form of a maiden, colored by the essence of youth;
with full breasts and a slender waist, she is mature, middle-aged, and afflicted by old age.
Extremely aged, having the form of a pillar, with moving limbs, she is restless and fickle;
she is Lāṅgalī, Cañcalā, Vegā, the Mother of the Gods (Devamātā), and the embodiment of the gods; she is auspicious, the performer of the work of the gods, and possesses divine form. || 27 ||
Diti is the mother of the gods, the daughter of Dakṣa, the eternal mother of all;
she is fond of drink, the giver of drink, the sacrificer, the protector,
and one who delights in protecting.
She who eats fish, she who devours meat, and she who eats nectar, beloved by the people; she who is an ascetic,
she who performs penance, she who is to be heated by penance, and she who bestows the perfection of austerity.
She who partakes of the sacrificial oblation, she who consumes the oblation, she who dwells in the offerings to gods and ancestors;
she who bears the Yajurveda, she who brings fulfillment, she whose limbs are the sacrifice,
and she who is beloved by the sacrifice.
Dakṣā, Dākṣāyaṇī, Durgā, Dakṣayajñavināśinī,
Pārvatī, Parvataprītā, and likewise Parvatavāsinī. || 31 ||

She is golden, a celestial palace, of the nature of gold; she is Menā, the venerable and beautiful one. She dwells on Kailāsa, she is liberated (or white), and she delights in the playful sports with Śarva (Śiva).
She possessed beautiful limbs, a lovely form, a fine mouth, and a radiant countenance;
she was the very beauty of her cheeks adorned with swinging earrings, wearing shimmering ear-ornaments. || 33 ||
Seated upon a great lion-throne, adorned with golden ornaments,
wearing golden armlets and golden decorations, she possesses a radiance equal to ten million suns.
Her radiance is like that of the rising sun; her form is adorned with vermilion;
she takes the form of barley and of red lac, and she assumes the appearance of red sandalwood. (35)
Koṭarī, Koṭarākṣī, Nirlajjā, Digambarā, Pūtanā, Bālamātā, and Śūnyālayanivāsinī. || 36 ||
She dwells in the cremation ground, she is the Void, she resides in the heart and at the crossroads;
she is the slayer of Madhu and Kaiṭabha, and the destroyer of the demon Mahiṣāsura.
She is the destroyer of Niśumbha and Śumbha, the annihilator of Caṇḍa and Muṇḍa;
she is named Śivā, she is of the form of Śiva, the messenger of Śiva, and the beloved of Śiva.
Bestower of auspiciousness, she who dwells upon the chest of Śiva, Śarvāṇī, the performer of auspicious deeds,
Indrāṇī, the daughter of Indra, the princess, and the beloved of the gods.
Modest by nature and virtuous in character, she is a noble woman who adorns her family;
though born of a great lineage and free from desire, she is shameless and yet the ornament of her kin. (40)
She is of noble birth, the daughter of a noble family, and likewise adorned by her lineage;
she possesses infinite and boundless forms, and she is the destroyer of infinite asuras.
Laughing through her union with Śiva, she bestows the desired bliss;
she has serpent-limbs, is adorned with serpents, and wears a necklace of serpents. || 42 ||
Dharaṇī, Dhāriṇī, and Dhanyā, who bestows great siddhi;
likewise Ḍākinī, Śākinī, Rākinī, and Hākinī. (43)
Bhūtā, Pretā, Piśācī, and Yakṣiṇī, who is worshipped by Dhanada;
Dhṛti, Kīrti, Smṛti, Medhā (or Mahāmedhā), Tuṣṭi, Puṣṭi, Umā, and Ruṣā (or Uṣā). || 44 ||

She is the consort of Śaṅkara, the consort of Śambhu, the Fish-goddess, Rati, Prīti, she who is afflicted by love, the goddess Anaṅgamadanā, and she who is distressed by the passion of the bodiless god. || 45 ||
Bhuvaneśī, Mahāmāyā, as well as Bhuvanapālinī, Īśvarī, she who is dear to Īśvara, and she whose ornament is Candraśekhara. || 46 ||
The Goddess, who brings joy to the mind, resides within the minds of people;
she is formless, yet possesses many forms, and while being the essence of consciousness, she is all forms.
Likewise, Śivā is the bestower of bliss. || 47 ||
She is infinite in form, eternal, and likewise the bestower of infinity;
she is Nandā, the embodiment of bliss, and likewise the illuminator of bliss.
She is eternal bliss, eternally imperishable, and the bestower of joy upon practitioners;
she is the woman, the youthful maiden, the auspicious one, the bringer of prosperity, and the radiant one.
Radiant like the moon and sun, she who protects like the sun;
she who is Nārasiṃhī, Hayagrīvā, and the destroyer of Hiraṇyākṣa. || 50 ||
She is Vaiṣṇavī, a devotee of Viṣṇu, and dwells within the Śālagrāma;
she is known as the four-armed, the eight-armed, and the thousand-armed.
The primordial Kātyāyanī is eternal, the first of all, the bestower of everything;
she is the goddess consisting of all moonlight, auspicious and consisting of all the Vedas.
The Goddess consists of all the gods; in ancient times, she consisted of all the worlds.
The Goddess is the deluder of all and the bringer of all the worlds under her control.
She is the queen, the one who delights, the passion, colored by the loveliness of her body;
she is the actress, the beloved of the dancer, the cunning woman, and likewise the one who subdues the crafty.
Mahāmāyā, the great deluder, who utterly bewilders great beings;
she is fond of offerings, delights in meat, and is always a lover of honey and flesh.
Intoxicated by honey, she is the Mādhavikā flower, possessing the form of Madhu and Mādhava;
she consists of day, she consists of night, she is the twilight, and her essential nature is the junction. || 56 ||
She is the form of Time, subtle in form, the subtle one, and the most subtle;
she is the form of the lunar days (tithi), the form of the days of the week (vāra), and likewise the form of the lunar mansions (nakṣatra). || 57 ||
The Goddess consists of all beings and dwells within the five elements;
she is of the nature of emptiness, has the form of emptiness, is established in emptiness, and is the Paralyzer.
The goddess who moves through space, who dwells in the wheel of light,
who is the abiding form of the planets, is Rudrāṇī, born from the wheel [or: born from Rudra and the others].
[arising] || 59 ||
She bestows the perfection of asceticism upon the seers, the sons of Brahmā, and those who uphold their vows;
she is Arundhatī, Gāyatrī, and Sāvitrī, whose form is truth.

Abiding on the funeral pyre, having the form of the funeral pyre, she bestows the accomplishment of the mind; abiding in the corpse, having the form of the corpse, she dwells within the enemy of the corpse.
She who dwells in the wheel of sound; [g: she who dwells in the wheel of corpses]. || 61 ||
The Yoginī who is the embodiment of yoga, who removes the impurities of yogins, the highly gracious Great Goddess, the daughter of Yamunā, the bestower of liberation. 62.
Stainless, pure, and immaculate, she is the purity of being who bestows victory;
she is the Great Knowledge, the Great Illusion, the Enchantress, and the Enchantress of the Universe.
The Goddess who accomplishes all tasks, who dwells within every undertaking;
she is the fierce Raudrī, the performer of both what is to be done and what is not to be done, the bringer of the great dissolution.
She is both the distinction between female and male and yet indivisible; she is the divider and the destroyer of division.
She possesses all forms, consists of all things, and is the embodiment of non-dual bliss.
Pracaṇḍā, Caṇḍikā, Caṇḍā, the destroyer of the fierce Asura; Sumastā, Bahumastā, and Chinnamastā, the destroyer of life.
Formless and yet multiform, possessing manifold forms while being of the nature of consciousness; possessing many weapons and yet weaponless, she strikes down all weapons.
She is the meaning of the scriptures and the discourse of the scriptures; she speaks various meanings of the scriptures.
She delights in the treatises on poetry and dwells within the ornaments of poetry.
She is the knower of tastes, the organ of taste, the tongue; she is the delight of flavors and the lover of tastes.
She is endowed with manifold wonders and sports in various flavors.
She is formless and yet possesses her own essential form; she is deformed and yet beautiful in form. She is unmanifest and yet has a manifest form;
she is the universal form and the possessor of form. Likewise, she is the state of form, the individual soul, and the one rich in the possession of various guises, assuming diverse appearances.
The Goddess, wearing various guises, is established in diverse appearances;
she is misshapen, crooked, black, and Kālikā, whose form is dark. (71)
Mahālakṣmī is the bestower of fortune, endowed with all auspicious marks;
residing in the house of Kubera, she is the embodiment of wealth and the giver of riches.
The goddess is the bestower of various jewels, residing within fragments of gems;
she is the abode of color, the form of color, and is eternally composed of all colors.
She is to be described as having the form of the syllable Oṃ, as the primordial one, and as having the form of the light of the sun;
she is the goddess who liberates from saṃsāra and bestows victory in battle.
Jayarūpā, Jayākhyā, Yajinī, Jayadāyinī, Māninī, Mānarūpā, and Mānabhaṅgapraṇāśinī. || 75 ||
She is the venerable one, fond of honor, wisdom, proud, and the bestower of honor;
she is the practitioner, the non-practitioner, the unattainable, the achiever, and she who is fond of spiritual practice.
She is declared to be the immobile and the mobile, subtle and fond of the restless;
she bestows prosperity, has the form of prosperity, grants success, and is the giver of success.
She who brings security and auspiciousness, she who causes universal delusion, she who is colored with passion and she who bestows all desires. || 78 ||
She is the delight of the bhaga and the liṅga, she who dwells within the bhaga and the liṅga;
she whose form is the bhaga, whose splendor is the bhaga, and whose form is the liṅga, the possessor of the liṅga. || 79 ||
The song of the vulva is great joy; the song of the linga is great bliss.
