She is self-arisen, worshipped by the youth Kusuma; she is self-arisen, filled with flowers [or: possessed of the art of flowers].
She is the Self-Existent One, she whose form is flowers, the Self-Existent One who loves blossoms;
she is the one whose well is semen, the Great Well, and she who dwells in the flow of semen.
She who abides in semen, who possesses semen, who is semen, and who is worshipped by those who worship semen;
she whose eyes are desire, who takes forms at will, the Yoginī, and the dweller in the sacred seats (pīṭha). || 82 ||
The Goddess consists of all sacred seats (pīṭha) and dwells in the worship of those seats;
the Goddess holds a rosary and carries a drinking vessel. || 83 ||
She holds a trident and has a trident in her hand; she holds a noose and has the form of a noose;
she likewise wields a sword and a mace, as well as all types of weapons.
She is Bhavānī, who bestows liberation from worldly existence;
she is to be meditated upon, she is auspicious, she is clever, she is pleased by the clever, and she is worshipped by the four-faced Brahmā.

She is to be honored by the gods, worshipped by the gods, and worthy of worship by all; she is the sovereign of the gods, the mother, appearing in the form of people, and the captivator of the hearts of men. 86.
She who wears matted locks, she whose hair is bound, she of beautiful hair, she who binds her hair;
she is non-violence, the hater, the one who is hated, and the destroyer of all hatred. 87.
She who expels, she who incites hatred, she who paralyzes, and she who deludes; she whose syllables are sweet,
she who sports, she who creates the marks of playful sport, and she who brings about all forms.
And she who produces the act of spitting. || 88 ||
She is all-knowing and the performer of all deeds; she consumes all and is the slayer of the enemies of the gods.
She is all-formed and all-peaceful, and she is the very form of the life-breath of all beings.
The Goddess is the cause of creation and maintenance, as well as the bringer of dissolution;
she is the bewildered one, the virtuous one, and the fierce one, assuming manifold forms.
O Goddess of gods, O Maheśvarī, whatever has been mentioned and whatever has not been mentioned—whatever is seen, O Goddess, all that is Bhuvaneśvarī. 91.
Thus, O Great Goddess, the thousands of names of the illustrious Bhuvaneśvarī have been told to you; their fruit is now being declared.
O beloved, he who recites this upon rising in the morning, as well as at midnight,
and likewise during the forenoon, midday, and evening, O favorite of Hara— (93)
Having recited it here or there with devotion, success is attained without a doubt;
whether one recites it, causes it to be recited, hears it, or causes it to be heard likewise. (94)
Everything that he desires in his mind shall become true, especially on the eighth, the fourteenth, or the ninth lunar day. || 95 ||

On the transit [of the sun] occurring on a Saturday or a Tuesday, which is endowed with all auspiciousness, whoever recites the *Thousand Names of the Goddess* with supreme devotion, (p. 80) [attains the fruit]. || 96 ||
And Bhuvaneśvarī establishes her presence within his body;
O Goddess, his task shall then be accomplished, and not otherwise by any means.
In a cremation ground or even in a remote wilderness, in an empty house or at a crossroads;
likewise at a crossroads with a single liṅga, or in the region of Meru. || 98 ||
In the midst of water, in the midst of fire, in battle, or for the sake of pacifying a village— or when life itself is in peril—
one should recite the thousand names after having chanted the mantra a thousand times.
And likewise, O Goddess, one should worship Bhuvaneśvarī with incense, lamps, and the like, as well as with offerings of bali and various kinds of food offerings (naivedya). (100)

Having worshipped according to the rules, recited the mantra, and praised [the deity] with the Thousand Names, the practitioner attains accomplishment before long; there is no doubt in this matter. || 101 ||
The Goddess Bhuvaneśvarī will always be pleased with him who has written [her mantra] on birch bark using saffron and red sandalwood. (102)
Likewise, having drawn [the mantra] with gorocanā and other substances on an auspicious lunar day and under a favorable asterism, the best of practitioners should write it on his right arm. (103)
O Pārvatī, one should maintain [this practice] with supreme devotion as the form of the Goddess;
O Maheśānī, for such a person, success will be attained without delay. 104.
In battle, or even in the royal court, he shall be victorious everywhere;
even deities come under his control, so what need be said of humans and the like? (105)

O Pārvatī, one who recites this or causes it to be recited with devotion to the Goddess undoubtedly effects the paralysis of spells, the solidification of water, and even the cessation of the movement of wind and fire.
Having enjoyed excellent pleasures here in this age [kalau], and having composed extensive treatises on the meaning of poetry [or:
having mastered difficult poetic works], the practitioner shall at the end attain the status of a Gaṇa of the Goddess and obtain liberation. || 107 ||
O Goddess of the gods, he attains all his goals; of this there is no doubt.
[This applies] even to one with deficient limbs, one with redundant limbs, to a rogue, or to the disciple of another. 108.
O Maheśānī, it must never be given, even at the cost of one's life,
to a disciple who lacks purity of mind, O Maheśvarī; [it should be given] only to one who is humble and endowed with devotion.
This king of hymns should be bestowed; it shall grant all accomplishments.
Having written it, one should wear it on the body; for such a person, suffering does not arise. (110)
O Maheśvarī, this King of Hymns (Stavarāja) of Bhuvaneśvarī has thus been told to you; O Goddess, this is the Thousand Names of Bhuvaneśī.
O Pārvatī, this should not be given to just anyone, except to a disciple;
it is as beautiful as the best of celestial trees, and is to be served exclusively by those who have attained accomplishment.
If a person recites this always with an undistracted mind,
having obtained all enjoyments in this world, he goes at the end to the presence of Śiva for liberation, forever accompanied by kinnaras.
being praised || 112 ||
Thus ends the hymn titled "The Thousand Names of Bhuvaneśvarī" in the venerable Rudrayāmala Tantra.
May there be prosperity.
Salutations to Śrī Gaṇeśa.
Now begins the hymn of one hundred and eight names of Śrī Bhuvaneśvarī. The Lord said:
The goddess who causes great delusion, the beautiful one, the sovereign of the world;
she is the single-syllabled, the sole mantra, the solitary leader of the worlds. || 1 ||
Of one form and of great forms, possessing both gross and subtle bodies,
she is the seed-form, the Great Power who increases victory in battle.
She is the one of great delight, of great power, the Yoginī who destroys sin;
she is the eightfold perfection, the embodiment of the arts, the Vaiṣṇavī, and Bhadrakālī. || 3 ||
The Great Goddess, who loves devotion, assumes the forms of Hari, Brahmā, and others;
she is the form of Śiva, the form of Viṣṇu, the form of Kāla, and she dwells in bliss.
She is ancient and of the nature of merit; she is Pārvatī, the increaser of virtue.
She is Rudrāṇī, Pārvatī, and Indrāṇī, whose body forms half of Śaṅkara’s own.
The great goddess Nārāyaṇī is the queen, the source of all auspiciousness;
she possesses the thirty-eight kalās, beginning with the letter 'A' and ending with the letter 'Kṣa'.
The seventh is the triple-guṇa woman who brings about the birth of the body; she is the agent of creation and dissolution, pervading all things until the end of the kalpa.
She is the one possessing all powers, the Great Power, Śarvāṇī, the Supreme Goddess;
she is Hṛllekhā, the Goddess Bhuvanā, who is devoted to the great poets.
Salutations to Śivā, the peaceful one, O Śāṅkarī, Sovereign of the World, who consists of will, knowledge, and action, and possesses the eightfold qualities beginning with atomization (aṇimā).
She was the embodiment of the Vedas and their auxiliary sciences, exceedingly subtle, and possessed of a physical form;
she was a knower of time, a knower of Śiva, and wholly devoted to the Śaiva dharma.
She who exists in the interval of time, whose form is time, the sustainer of life for all perceptions;
she who possesses the most excellent sword, who holds the khaṭvāṅga staff, and who bears the supreme trident.
Formless and multiform, the Leader who brings the world under her sway;
Fearless and the Protector of the World, the Wielder of the Pināka bow and the Sustainer of the Nagas. (12)
Vajraśakti, Mahāśakti, Pāśatomaradhāriṇī, the eighteen-armed goddess Hṛllekhā, and likewise Bhuvanā. (13)
Holding a sword, possessing a magnificent form, situated in the midst of the moon, sun, and fire—thus is this hymn of one hundred and eight names spoken by Ramanatha. (14)
It pacifies all sins, wards off all misfortunes, causes the destruction of all enemies, and always increases victory. || 15 ||
It bestows longevity, nourishment, protection, and fame; it grants sovereignty over the states of the immortals and other realms, and removes even a fraction of the impurities of the soul.
Thus ends the "One Hundred and Eight Names of Bhuvaneśvarī" from the Śrī Rudrayāmala Tantra.
Saṃvat 1943, Phālguna badi 10, Thursday.
Salutations to Śrī Gaṇeśa.
Now begins the *Śrībhuvaneśvaryaṣṭaka*.
The Goddess said:
O Lord, O most excellent Śrī Bhairava, O compassionate one, O you who are affectionate toward your devotees!
If I am dear to you, then speak the hymn to Bhuvaneśī.
Īśvara said:
Listen, O Goddess! I shall proclaim the auspicious eight names of Bhuvaneśī, by the mere knowledge of which the three worlds shall become blessed. (2)

Oṃ, I bow to the support of the universe, the Mistress of the World, the beloved of Bhava, who bestows both worldly enjoyment and liberation, who is beautiful, enchanting, and the bringer of auspiciousness. || 3 ||
O Goddess! You are Svāhā, you are Svadhā; you are the sacrifice, the mistress of sacrifice;
you are the protector, the dispeller of darkness, devoid of both the pervaded and the pervader.
You are the support, you are the sacrifice, you are knowledge and the object of knowledge, the supreme state;
you are Śiva, you are Viṣṇu himself, you are the supreme, imperishable Self.
You are both cause and effect; you are Lakṣmī and you are the consumer of oblations (Agni); you are the Moon, you are the Sun, you are Time, you are the Creator, and you are the Wind.
You are Gāyatrī, you are Sāvitrī, you are Māyā, and you are the beloved of Hari;
you alone are the Supreme Power (Parāśakti), and you alone assume the form of the Guru.
You are Time, you are beyond all parts; you alone are the prosperity of the worlds.
O embodiment of compassion! You are every action and the cause of everything.
O fair-faced one, this octet belongs to the primordial Bhuvaneśī;
that mortal who, with a joyful mind and with faith, recites it at the three junctions of the day, [attains the fruit].
By the power of this hymn, the supernatural attainments (siddhis) come under his control, prosperity remains within his home, and kings submit to his will. (10)
(85) Ghosts, spirits, piśācas, and other such beings, as well as the planetary grahas, do not look toward that direction.
Whatever desire the practitioner, with a joyful mind, may long for— || 11 ||
O fair-faced one, he attains each of those [goals] through the grace of Bhuvaneśī;
there is no hymn equal to this in the three worlds. (12)

This [hymn] bestows all prosperity and is the purifier of purifiers. O fair-faced one, when this excellent hymn is accomplished, all riches come under one's control through the grace of Bhuvaneśī. 13.
Thus ends the Śrībhuvaneśvaryaṣṭaka in the venerable Rudrayāmala Tantra.
Saṃvat 1943, Phālguna, dark fortnight, tenth day, Thursday.
Now begins the hymn of the thousand names of the venerable Bhuvaneśvarī, beginning with the letter *bha*.

Oṃ. Of this mantra-hymn of the thousand names of the venerable Bhuvaneśvarī, Sadāśiva is the seer (*ṛṣi*), Anuṣṭubh is the meter (*chandaḥ*), Bhuvaneśvarī is the deity (*devatā*), Lajjā is the seed-syllable (*bīja*), Kamalā is the power (*śakti*), and Vāgbhava is the pin (*kīlaka*).
The application is in the recitation for the accomplishment of all goals.
Oṃ! O Bhuvaneśī, worshipped by the world, Bhavānī, destroyer of fear;
you who are the form of existence, the bliss of existence, and the one who carries us across the ocean of worldly existence. || 1 ||
Arising from existence, delighting in existence, and removing the burden of existence;
she whose face is auspicious, whose eyes are auspicious, whose form is auspicious, is the medicine for existence. || 2 ||
She possesses auspicious limbs, auspicious hair, and is the liberator from the bonds of worldly existence;
she sits upon an auspicious seat, wears auspicious garments, and is adorned with auspicious ornaments. || 3 ||
She whose form is the *bhaga*, who is the bliss of the *bhaga*, the mistress of the *bhaga*, she who is garlanded with *bhagas*;
she who is the knowledge of the *bhaga*, the divine lady (*bhagavatī*), she who is moistened by the *bhaga*, and the bringer of the *bhaga*.
She whose source is the womb, she who sports in the womb, she who is rich in the womb, she who is auspicious through the womb;
she whose play is the womb, she who is delighted by the womb, she who is the perfection of the womb, and the sovereign of the womb. || 5 ||
She whose abode is the *bhaga*, who exerts energy through the *bhaga*, who resides in the *bhaga*, who nourishes the *bhaga*;
she who is the festival of the *bhaga*, the knowledge of the *bhaga*, the mother of the *bhaga*, and she who is established in the *bhaga*.
She is the power of fortune, the treasure-house of fortune, the worship of fortune, and the desire for fortune;
she is the sleep of fortune, the sovereign of fortune, the one to be adored by fortune, and the beauty of fortune.
She whose lines are the vulva, whose affection is the vulva, who increases the affection of the vulva;
she who is the sister, who resides in the seed of the vulva, and who delights in the enjoyment of the vulva. || 8 ||

She whose conduct is the *bhaga*, who is the support of the *bhaga*, whose form is the *bhaga*, and who has the *bhaga* as her refuge; she who has the *bhaga* as her flower, who protects the glory of the *bhaga*, and who dwells within the flower of the *bhaga*. || 9 ||
Bearing a beautiful form, auspicious, adorned with auspicious flowers, possessing auspicious grace, wearing an auspicious garland—O lady of auspicious limbs, O auspicious beauty! (10)
She whose conduct is auspicious, whose play is auspicious, whose eyes are auspicious, who destroys what is inauspicious;
she whose limbs are auspicious, whose speech is auspicious, whose radiance is auspicious, and who is adorned with the vulva (bhaga). || 11 ||
She possesses modesty worthy of the noble, she is a river of the noble, she dwells in the enjoyments of the noble;
she has the breasts of the noble, the face of the noble, and is a noble assembly that dispels fear.
The Mistress of devotion, the creator of devotion, she who bestows grace upon devotees;
the giver of devotion, the mother of devotion, and the increaser of the bliss of devotees. || 13 ||
She who loves devotion, who delights in devotion, who sports in the state of devotion;
she whose character is devotion, whose play is devotion, who is the mistress of devotion, and the protector of devotion. || 14 ||
She is the knowledge of devotion, the knowledge for the devotee, devotion itself, and that which delights in devotion;
she is the path of devotion, the love of devotion, and the one who accomplishes the means of devotion. || 15 ||
She who is to be accomplished through devotion, she who is to be accomplished by devotees, the friend of devotion, the sovereign of existence;
the science of warriors, the bliss of warriors, the abode of warriors, and the form of warriors.
She who is honored by warriors, she who dwells among warriors, she who resides in the quarters of warriors;
she who is the sister of warriors, she whose form is that of a warrior, and she who increases the form of a warrior. || 17 ||
She is the mistress of warriors and the queen of warriors; she is the beautiful one who partakes in the state of warriors.
Through her love for warriors and according to the conduct of warriors, she bestows grace upon them.
She who is to be worshipped by warriors, who is to be understood by warriors, who delights the awakening of warriors;
she who is to be served by warriors, the best of warriors, who is to be honored by warriors, and who awakens warriors. || 19 ||
Bhaṭakīrti, Bhaṭakalā, Bhaṭapā, Bhaṭapālinī, Bhaṭaiśvaryā, Bhaṭādhīśā, Bhaṭekṣā, and Bhaṭatoṣiṇī. || 20 ||
The mistress of warriors, the mother of warriors, the increaser of the fortune of warriors;
the sustenance of warriors, the union with warriors, and the increaser of the joy of warriors. || 21 ||
She is the mistress of fortune, the mother of fortune, the abode of fortune, and the embodiment of fortune;
she is contemplation, skilled in all states of being, the giver of existence, and the increaser of existence.
She whose form is existence, whose essence is existence, who dwells within other states of being;
she who is the sprout of existence, the digit of existence, and the resident of the abode of existence. || 23 ||
Supported by existence, she abides within existence as a distinct state;
she is the prosperity of existence, the accomplishment of existence, the origin of existence, and that which manifests through existence. (24)
She whose abode is existence, who is intent on existence, and who is devoted to the means of existence;
she is the Mistress of existence, accessible through existence, established in existence, and proud of existence. || 25 ||
She is the future, the delight of existence, the goddess of speech, and the sovereign lady of the land of Bhārata;
she is the river Bhāgīrathī, the fortunate one, the one who brings about the rise of fortune, and the creative art.
She is the refuge of fortune, composed of fortune, fortunate herself, and the bestower of the fruits of fortune;
she is the conduct of fortune, the essence of fortune, the stream of fortune, and the giver of fortune.
She is the mistress of fortune, the treasure-trove of fortune, the fortunate one, and the excellent mother of fortune;
she is the glance of fortune, the name of fortune, the giver of fortune and fortune itself, and the mother of fortune.
She is the examination of fortune, the mind of fortune, the beginning of fortune, and she who dwells in the midst of fortune;
she possesses the voice of a sister, she has brothers, she is the mother of brothers, and she is the protector of her brothers.
She who dwells in her brothers, she who is well-disposed toward her brothers, she who is like a bee, she who is the mother of bees;
she who has the form of a Bhilla, she who possesses the nature of a Bhilla, she who resides among the Bhillas, and she who protects the Bhillas.
Bhillamātā, Bhilladhātrī, Bhillinī, Bhillakeśvarī, Bhillakīrti, Bhillakalā, and Bhillamandaravāsinī. || 31 ||
She is the play of the Bhillas, the sport of the Bhillas, worshipped by the Bhillas, and beloved by the Bhillas;
she is the daughter-in-law of the Bhillas, the daughter of the Bhillas, the wife of the Bhillas, and the nourisher of the Bhillas. || 32 ||
The granddaughter of the Bhillas, the assembly of the Bhillas, she who dwells among the scouts of the Bhillas;
she who is worshipped by the Bhillas, the speech of the Bhillas, the mother of the Bhillas, and the dispeller of the fear of the Bhillas. (33)
She who abides in fear, she who is the mother of those in fear, she who is fear itself, she who destroys fear;
she who bestows fear, she who removes fear, she who sports with the form of fear through fear.
She who is the abode of fear, the pacifier of fear, she who dwells in the place of fear;
she who follows the way of fear, the essence of fear, the observer of fear, and the remover of fear. || 35 ||
Bhīmeśī, mother of Bhīma, Bhīmā, dwelling in the terrible; Bhīmeśvarī, delighting in the terrible, Bhīmāṅgī, and protector of the terrible. || 36 ||
She whose roar is terrifying, whose lute is terrifying, who increases terrifying sovereignty;
she who is the assembly of the terrifying, the mother of the terrifying, and who delights in terrifying lore. || 37 ||
She is the bestower of terrible prowess, she who dwells in terrible prowess;
she is the goddess who causes terrible joy, and she who sports in terrible joy. || 38 ||
She who instructs in fearlessness, she who is eternal, she who bestows formidable fortune;
she who is formidable accomplishment, she who is formidable prosperity, and she who increases formidable devotion. (39)
She who dwells in the formidable, she who bestows formidable boons, she who teaches formidable dharma;
the sovereign of Bhīṣma, the sustainer of Bhīṣma, and the awakener of the awakening of Bhīṣma. || 40 ||
She is the glory of Bhīṣma, the mother of Bhīṣma, the instructor of Bhīṣma’s knowledge;
she resides in Bhīṣma, she is the scorcher of Bhīṣma, the mistress of Bhīṣma, and the savior from Bhīṣma. || 41 ||
She whose play is formidable, whose character is formidable, who dwells on the banks of the Bhīṣma;
she who has the Bhīṣma as her refuge, who grants formidable boons, and who increases the joy of the Bhīṣma. || 42 ||
She is the mistress of the worlds, the one who brings bliss to the worlds;
she dwells upon the earth, her form is the earth, and she is the remover of the earth's burden.
She who abides in enjoyment, she who bestows enjoyment, she who is enjoyment, she who dwells in enjoyment, she whose form is enjoyment;
she who is the mistress of enjoyment, she who grants enjoyment, she whose form is the very nature of enjoyment. || 44 ||
She who dwells upon serpents, the mistress of serpent-lords, whose form has the appearance of a serpent;
she who is a female serpent, whose abode is the serpents, and who bestows bliss upon the serpents. || 45 ||
She is the mistress of beings, the mother of beings, abiding in beings, and possessing the form of beings;
she is the sovereign of beings, her play is in the realm of beings, and she always assumes the guise of beings. 46.
The giver of beings, she whose hair is beings, the sustainer of beings, the Great Sovereign;
she who moves among beings, the consort of beings, and the dweller in the world of beings. || 47 ||

She is the accomplishment of beings, the supernatural power of beings, and she who dwells in the bliss of beings; she is the glory of beings, the fortune of beings, and the increaser of the good fortune of beings. || 48 ||
She is worshipped by the elements, she is the delight of the elements, she is the one who dispels ignorance regarding the elements;
she is the granddaughter of the elements, the daughter of the elements, the wife of the elements, and the sovereign mistress of the elements.
She who dwells in all beings, who delights in all beings, the mistress of all beings, the protector of all beings;
the mother of kings, resembling a king, and the bestower of sovereignty upon kings. || 50 ||
She is the activity of kings, beloved by kings, and the increaser of the majesty of kings;
she is the sister of kings, the mother of kings, the granddaughter of kings, and likewise their daughter-in-law.
She is the fame of kings, the policy of kings, and the increaser of the fortune of kings;
she is the activity of kings, the play of kings, and she dwells upon Mount Mandara, the king of mountains.
Worshipped by kings, to be propitiated by kings, increasing the enjoyments of kings,
taking refuge with kings, the artifice of kings, and wielding the scepter of royal curiosity. (53)
She who abides in ornaments, the mistress of ornaments, the ornament itself, and she who wears ornaments;
she who is the mistress of the dharma that is the substratum of ornaments, and she whose form has the appearance of ornaments. || 54 ||
She is the abode of the conduct of the lords of the earth, adorned with the conduct of the lords of the earth;
she is the composition of the conduct of the lords of the earth, embellished by the conduct of the lords of the earth. || 55 ||
She is the sovereign of the dharma of earthly conduct, she is the performer of earthly conduct, she is one whose character is earthly conduct, and she is devoid of earthly conduct. || 56 ||
Established in the increase of royal conduct, she bestows the increase of royal conduct;
she effects royal conduct and grants the fruits of royal conduct. || 57 ||
She is the mistress of the king’s conduct and actions; she bestows the king’s conduct and actions;
she resides within the body of the king’s conduct; she is the one who performs the king’s conduct and actions. || 58 ||
Established in the perfection of royal conduct, she bestows the perfection of royal conduct;
she possesses the qualities of royal conduct and upholds royal conduct. (59)
She is the wave of bliss for kings, she who takes the form of the sovereign of kings;
she is the foundation of the king's policy, and she dwells in the station of the king.
She is the goddess residing in the station of the king, the bestower of boons upon the king;
she is the wave of bliss from medicine, whose very form is the bliss of medicine.
The queen Bheṣajānanda, the bearer of Bheṣajānanda, the mistress of the activity of Bheṣajānanda, and the bestower of Bheṣajānanda. || 62 ||
She is the healer, the medicine, the root, and she who dwells in the abode of medicine;
she possesses the form of the Lord of Medicine and bestows the siddhis of the Lord of Medicine.
She is the Mistress of Medicine and the Sovereign of Dharma; she bestows the activity of the Lord of Medicine.
She is the Mistress of the activity of the Lord of Medicine and she whose very nature is the action of the Lord of Medicine.
The mother of the Lord of Medicines, the protectress of the Lord of Medicines;
the architect of the Lord of Medicines, the auspiciousness of the Lord of Medicines. || 65 ||
Dwelling in the midst of the medicinal forest, she is the guardian of the medicinal forest;
she is the science of medicine, the medicine itself, and the bestower of desired medicines. || 66 ||
Abiding in medicine, mistress of medicine, increaser of the joy of medicine;
Bhairavī, whose conduct is that of Bhairava, and whose form has the appearance of Bhairava. || 67 ||
Skilled in the practice of Bhairava, adorned with the practice of Bhairava, she is Bhairavā, the mistress of Bhairava, and the bestower of the bliss of Bhairava. || 68 ||
She whose nature is the bliss of Bhairava, she who possesses the form of the bliss of Bhairava, she who is skilled in the bliss of Bhairava, and she who is the temple of the bliss of Bhairava. (69)
She knows the reality of Bhairavānanda, is devoted to Bhairavānanda,
is skilled in Bhairavānanda, and bestows the discipline of Bhairavānanda.
She who abides in the joy of Bhairava’s bliss, she who bestows the joy of Bhairava’s bliss, the queen of Bhairava’s bliss, and she who is garlanded with the joy of Bhairava’s bliss. (71)
She who bestows the intellect of Bhairava-bliss, she who is the Mother of Bhairava-bliss, the progenitor of the support of Bhairava, and the protectress of the support of Bhairava. || 72 ||
She whose form is the support of Bhairava, she who possesses the form that is the support of Bhairava;
she who is the accumulation of the support of Bhairava, she who is the certainty regarding the support of Bhairava. || 73 ||
She is the knower of the reality that is the support of Bhairava; she is the giver of the reality that is the support of Bhairava.
She is the mistress of the tantra which has Bhairava as its refuge; she is the mantra-practitioner who has Bhairava as her refuge. (74)
The arrangement has Bhairava as its support, it is colored by the support of Bhairava;
it is the definitive determination of the support of Bhairava, and it is replete with the support of Bhairava. || 75 ||
She who determines the refuge of Bhairava, she who upholds the refuge of Bhairava;
she whose nature is the awakening of Bhairava-bliss, she who brings about the awakening of Bhairava-bliss. || 76 ||
Established in the awakening of Bhairava-bliss, she bestows the awakening of Bhairava-bliss;
she grants the boon of Bhairavī-sovereignty and is the giver of Bhairavī-sovereignty. || 77 ||

The architect of Bhairava’s sovereignty, the increaser of Bhairava’s sovereignty, the abode of the perfection of Bhairava’s sovereignty, and the bestower of the perfection of Bhairava’s sovereignty. (78)
She is the sovereign perfection of Bhairavī’s power, she whose form is the sovereignty of Bhairavī;
she is the excellent path of Bhairavī’s sovereignty, and she who possesses the sublime radiance of Bhairavī’s sovereignty.
Established in the increase of Bhairava’s sovereignty, she bestows the increase of Bhairava’s sovereignty;
she is skilled in Bhairava’s sovereignty and grants the desires of Bhairava’s sovereignty. 80.
(92) Easily attained through the sovereignty of Bhairavī, she is the bestower of the sovereignty of Bhairavī;
she is radiant with the sovereignty of Bhairavī, and her transformation is the sovereignty of Bhairavī. || 81 ||
She possesses the majesty, sovereignty, and discipline of Bhairava; she is the knower of the majesty and sovereignty of Bhairava;
she is the greatness of the majesty and sovereignty of Bhairava; she is the one who takes pride in the majesty and sovereignty of Bhairava.
She is devoted to the sovereignty of Bhairavī, created by the sovereignty of Bhairavī;
she is the Mistress of Enjoyment, the Mother of Enjoyment, the Abode of Enjoyment, and the Protector of Enjoyment. || 83 ||
She who is the play of enjoyment, the sport of enjoyment, the mistress of enjoyment, the increaser of enjoyment;
she whose limbs are enjoyment, the delighter in enjoyment, and she who moves within the conduct of enjoyment. || 84 ||
She who is the locus of enjoyment, the possessor of enjoyment, the enjoyer, and whose form is enjoyment;
she who is the sprout of enjoyment, the ordainer of enjoyment, and she who dwells in the support of enjoyment. || 85 ||
Bhogāmbikā, who delights in enjoyment, who bestows the accomplishment of enjoyment;
she who dwells in food, who is devoted to eating, and who grants the bliss of eating. || 86 ||
She is the wave of bliss in eating, she who sports within the act of eating;
she is the majesty of the bliss of eating, and she bestows the enjoyment of the bliss of eating. 87.
She is the arrangement of the joy of eating, she is gladdened by the joy of eating;
she is skillful in the etiquette of eating, and she is adorned by the etiquette of eating. || 88 ||
She is one whose conduct in eating is practiced, whose conduct in eating is refined, who is perfected in the conduct of eating, and who is endowed with the conduct of eating. || 89 ||
Established in the conduct of eating, she is the giver of the manner of eating;
she is the glory of the conduct of eating, and she is the expansion of the conduct of eating. || 90 ||
She who delights in the practice of eating, she who protects the practice of eating, she who is the doe of the practice of eating, and she who devours the practice of eating. || 91 ||

She who bestows happiness through the practice of eating, she who is fond of the practice of eating, she whose essence is the delicious taste of food, and she who is beautiful through the consumption of food. 92.
She whose conduct consists of food and nourishment, who is restless for food and nourishment;
she whose wealth is the taste of food, and who is fond of the taste of food. || 93 ||
Satisfied with the taste of food, devoted to the taste of food, following the good path of the taste of food, and taking refuge in the taste of food. || 94 ||
Delighting in the tasting of food, intent upon the tasting of food;
she whose syllable is *bhaukṣa*, the sovereign of *bhaukṣa*, whose form consists of the syllable *bhauk*. || 95 ||
She who abides in the syllable BHAUḤ, whose beginning is the syllable BHAUḤ, and who dwells in the station of the syllable BHAUḤ;
she who utters the sound BHAṂ, who possesses the radiance of light, who is the essence of light, the mistress of ashes, and whose form is ash. || 96 ||
Bhaṅkārā, Bhañcanā, Bhasmā, Bhasmasthā, Bhasmavāsinī; Bhakṣarī, Bhakṣarākārā, and Bhakṣarasthānavāsinī. || 97 ||
She who is rich in food, the mistress of food, whose form is sustenance, whose nature is ash;
she who dwells on the mountains, the mistress of the mountains, the mountain-dweller, and the sovereign of the mountains. || 98 ||
She who delights in the joy of the mountains, she who protects the joy of the mountains, she who generates the joy of the mountains, and she who dwells within the joy of the mountains. || 99 ||
She is the delight of the joy of the mountains, protected by the joy of the mountains;
she possesses the majesty of the joy of the mountains, and is the abode of the joy of the mountains. 100.

The sovereign of all who delight in the mountains, the mother of all who delight in the mountains, the queen of those who delight in the mountains, and the bestower of joy upon those who delight in the mountains. || 101 ||
She is the mistress of dharma for the lord of the mountains, she whose nature is the joy of the mountain-dweller;
she is the mistress of dharma for the lord of the mountains, the bestower of spiritual accomplishments upon the lord of the mountains.
She is the mistress of the lord of mountains and the wife of the lord of mountains;
she is devoted to the lord of mountains and is praised by the lord of mountains.
She abides by the conduct of the Lord of Mountains, she bestows the conduct of the Lord of Mountains;
she is the mistress of the fortune of the Lord of Mountains, she is the beloved wife of the Lord of Mountains. 104.

She who abides in the mind of the Lord of Mountains, she who bestows the intellect of the Lord of Mountains, she who grants boons to the Lord of Mountains, she who is saluted by the Lord of Mountains. || 105 ||
She is to be propitiated by the Lord of the Mountains; she is worshipped by the Lord of the Mountains.
She is the Mistress of Destruction, composed of destruction, abiding in destruction, and having the form of destruction.
She who is unbroken by destruction, whose delight is in dissolution, who is worshipped through dissolution, who protects through dissolution;
she who possesses dissolution, whose play is dissolution, and who revels in the enjoyment of dissolution. || 107 ||
She resembles the stage of a dramatic performance; she dwells upon the stage of a dramatic performance;
she consumes the dramatic performance; she is rooted in the dramatic performance; she ordains the enjoyment of the dramatic performance. || 108 ||
She who rests upon dissolution, whose seed is dissolution, the sovereign of the sprout from the seed of dissolution;
she who is the wonder of the mechanism of dissolution, likewise the sovereign of the mechanism of dissolution. (109)
She who abides in the delusion of the mechanism of destruction, she who delights in the mechanism of destruction;
she who abides in the investigation of the mechanism of destruction, she who investigates the mechanism of destruction. || 110 ||

She who is the bliss of the essence of the churning machine, the sovereign of the essence of the churning machine, she who tastes the essence of the churning machine, and she who abides in the essence of the churning machine. || 111 ||
She who is the support for the essence of the mechanism of destruction, she who is the refuge for the essence of the mechanism of destruction;
she whose form is like that of the daughter of the Mountain-King (Pārvatī), she who possesses the form of the daughter of the Mountain-King.
The mistress of yoga, daughter of the mountain; the protectress of the daughter of the mountain;
the majesty of the daughter of the mountain; she who wears the daughter of the mountain as a garland. 113.
She is the consort of the Lord of the Mountain’s son, she possesses the form of the Mountain’s daughter,
she is the abode of the perfection of the Mountain’s son, and she bestows the perfection of the Mountain’s son.
She is the mistress of the state of the Son of the Mountain; she is the one who brings about the state of the Son of the Mountain.
She dwells in the enjoyment of the Son of the Mountain; she is the giver of that which is to be enjoyed by the Son of the Mountain. 115.
She who enjoys the son of the Mountain King, she who sports with the son of the Mountain King;
she who is auspicious, most auspicious, the bringer of auspiciousness, and the beloved of Bhava.

She is the state of being and the state beyond being, known as existence; she is the radiance of light, the end of fear, the brilliance and the state beyond brilliance, established in splendor, the light of lights, and like the sun.
She who dwells in the sun, the mistress of the sun, she who increases the sovereignty of the sun, she who generates bliss for the sun, and she who bestows bliss upon the sun. || 118 ||
She is the greatness of Bhāskarānanda, the source-mother of Bhāskarānanda, the sovereign power of Bhāskarānanda, and the mistress of Bhāskarānanda. 119.
The excellent path of Bhāskarānanda, the beautiful radiance of Bhāskarānanda, the accumulation of Bhāskarānanda, and that which was fashioned by Bhāskarānanda. (120)
Established in the system of Bhāskarānanda, she bestows the system of Bhāskarānanda;
she abides in the midst of the rising of Bhāskara, and she dwells within the center of Bhāskara’s rising.
Abiding in the splendor of the rising sun, she possesses the brilliance of the rising sun;
she is adept in the conduct of the Sun-god and is the moonlight of the Sun-god’s way of life.
Supreme among those who follow the conduct of Bhāskara, she is the Caṇḍikā of Bhāskara’s conduct;
supreme among those who follow the conduct of Bhāskara, she has reached the further shore of Bhāskara’s conduct. (123)
Established in the liberation of Bhāskarācāra, she bestows the liberation of Bhāskarācāra;
established in the perfection of Bhāskarācāra, she bestows the perfection of Bhāskarācāra. || 124 ||
She whose support is the feet of Bhāskara, she who rests upon the feet of Bhāskara;
she who is the mistress of the mantras of Bhāskara’s conduct, she who is the minister of Bhāskara’s conduct. 125.
She who knows the conduct of Bhāskara and is the mistress of his wealth; she who is adorned by the conduct of Bhāskara;
she who is the sovereign of dharma supported by Bhāskara; she who upholds that which is supported by Bhāskara.
She is the fashioner of the support for the Sun, she is protected by the support of the Sun;
she performs the actions of the support of the Sun, and she bestows the fruits of the actions of the Sun.
She whose form is the support of Bhāskara, she who possesses the form that is the support of Bhāskara;
she who is the beloved mistress of the support of Bhāskara, she who is the lover of the support of Bhāskara. || 128 ||
She is the mistress of the rays supported by the sun; she possesses the rays supported by the sun.
She is the mistress of the dharma supported by the sun; she is the effulgence supported by the sun. || 129 ||
She who resides in the foundational wheel of Bhāskara, she who possesses the foundational wheel of Bhāskara;
she who is the mistress of the field of Bhāskareśvara, she who dwells within the field of Bhāskareśvara. || 130 ||
The mother of Bhāskareśvara, the protectress of Bhāskareśvara;
the sovereign of all for Bhāskareśvara, the night of Bhāskareśvara. || 131 ||
Bhāskareśvarasadbhīmā, Bhāskareśvarasannibhā, Bhāskareśvarasupathā, and Bhāskareśvarasuprabhā. || 132 ||
The youthful consort of Bhāskareśvara, the beautiful lady of Bhāskareśvara;
the sovereign mistress of the form of Bhāskareśvara, she who possesses the very form of Bhāskareśvara. || 133 ||
Bhāskareśvaramitreśī, Bhāskareśvaramantriṇī, Bhāskareśvarasānandā, and Bhāskareśvarasāśrayā. || 134 ||

She who resides in the painting of Bhāskareśvara, she who bestows the painting of Bhāskareśvara, she who is the mistress of the painting of Bhāskareśvara, and she who possesses the painting of Bhāskareśvara. || 135 ||
She who abides in the fortune of Bhāskareśvara, she who bestows the fortune of Bhāskareśvara;
she who is the mistress of the fortune of Bhāskareśvara, she who is the creative power of Bhāskareśvara. || 136 ||
Bhāskareśvarakīrtīśī, Bhāskareśvarakīrtinī,
Bhāskareśvarakīrtisthā, and Bhāskareśvarakīrtidā. || 137 ||
The compassion of Bhāskareśvara, the creator of Bhāskareśvara;
the speech of Bhāskareśvara, the Gāruḍī of Bhāskareśvara. || 138 ||
She resides within the body of Bhāskareśvara; she bestows the body of Bhāskareśvara.
She abides in the sound of Bhāskareśvara; she is the resonant voice of Bhāskareśvara. || 139 ||
She whose command is Bhāskareśvara, she who sounds as Bhāskareśvara;
she who resides in the treasury of Bhāskareśvara, she who bestows the treasury of Bhāskareśvara. 140.
She is the treasury-lordess of Bhāskareśvara, the giver of the treasury of Bhāskareśvara;
she abides as the power of Bhāskareśvara and is the bestower of the power of Bhāskareśvara. || 141 ||
She who is pleased by Bhāskareśvara, she who delights Bhāskareśvara;
she who is the mistress of the field of Bhāskareśvara, she who protects Bhāskareśvara. || 142 ||
Established in the yoga of Bhāskareśvara, she bestows the yoga of Bhāskareśvara;
she is the sovereign of the yoga of Bhāskareśvara and the yoginī of Bhāskareśvara. || 43 ||
Bhāskareśvarapadmeśī, Bhāskareśvarapadminī, Bhāskareśvarahṛdbījā, and Bhāskareśvarahṛdvarā. (44)

She whose womb is the heart of Bhāskareśvara, she whose radiance is the heart of Bhāskareśvara, she who resides in the intellect of Bhāskareśvara, and she whose true nature is that of Bhāskareśvara. (45)
She is the true speech of Bhāskareśvara; she is the excellent consort of Bhāskareśvara;
she is established in the kingdom of Bhāskareśvara; and she is the bestower of the kingdom of Bhāskareśvara. 146.
She is the sovereign of the realm of Bhāskareśvara, the nourisher of Bhāskareśvara;
she is established in the knowledge of Bhāskareśvara and is the bestower of the knowledge of Bhāskareśvara.
She is Bhāskareśvarajñāneśī, she who goes to Bhāskareśvara;
she is Bhāskareśvaralakṣeśī, she who is marked by Bhāskareśvara. || 148 ||
Washed by Bhāskareśvara, protected by Bhāskareśvara, stationed on the sword of Bhāskareśvara, and given by the sword of Bhāskareśvara. 149.
Bhāskareśvarakhaḍgeśī, Bhāskareśvarakhaḍginī, Bhāskareśvarakāryyeśī, and Bhāskareśvarakāminī. || 150 ||
Established in the body of Bhāskareśvara, they are the gift of the body of Bhāskareśvara;
established in the eye of Bhāskareśvara, they are by means of the eye of Bhāskareśvara. (151)
Her navel resembles the sun; she is worshipped by Bhāskareśvara;
she is the pacifier of the killing of an embryo and the destroyer of the sin of destroying an embryo. || 152 ||
She is the pacifier of the poverty of the fetus, the destroyer of diseases of the fetus, the alleviator of the sorrow of the fetus, and the warder-off of the defects of the fetus. || 153 ||
She who pacifies the distress of the embryo, she who destroys the delusion of the embryo;
she who dwells within the ocean of existence, she who is the mistress of the ocean of existence, and she who destroys the fear of the ocean of existence. || 154 ||

She who brings about the crossing of the ocean of existence, she who increases the happiness within the ocean of existence, she who accomplishes the purpose within the ocean of existence, and she who is the treasure-house of compassion for the ocean of existence. (155)
She quiets the time of the ocean of existence; she bestows boons upon the ocean of existence;
she is the place of refuge for those within the ocean of existence; she abides as the object of devotion for those within the ocean of existence. 156.
She has the form of devotion to the ocean of existence; she is the act of devotion to the ocean of existence;
she is the conduct of devotion to the ocean of existence; she is the sprout of devotion to the ocean of existence. || 157 ||

She who finds bliss in worshipping the ocean of existence, she who is the sovereign of worshipping the ocean of existence, she who possesses the lordship of worshipping the ocean of existence, she who is the mistress of the act of worshipping the ocean of existence. 158.

Success in devotion to the ocean of existence, delight in devotion to the ocean of existence, constancy in devotion to the ocean of existence, and vigilance in devotion to the ocean of existence. (159)
Sunk in devotion to the ocean of existence, she removes the fear of birth within that ocean of existence;
her devotion to the ocean of existence is desirable, for it is the very essence of devotion to the ocean of existence. 160.
She is the glory of worshiping the ocean of existence, she is performed through worshiping the ocean of existence;
she is the eternal bestower of auspiciousness upon the ocean of existence, she is the giver of auspiciousness within the ocean of existence. 161.
She is the entirety of bliss within the ocean of existence; she is the complete perfection within the ocean of existence;
she is the total accomplishment within the ocean of existence; she is the entire treasure-trove within the ocean of existence. 162.
She is the essence of all that is within the ocean of existence; she is the bestower of all goals within the ocean of existence;
she is the formless embodiment of the dwelling within the ocean of existence; she is the very shape of the dwelling within the ocean of existence.
The worthy ones have their existence within the ocean of becoming; they are submerged by the waters of the ocean of becoming;
they possess the form of passion for the ocean of becoming; and they are afflicted by the intoxication of the ocean of becoming. 164.
She is the Mistress of Passion within the ocean of existence, the Sovereign of Passion within the ocean of existence;
she is the fashioner of fortune within the ocean of existence, and the constant bestower of fortune within the ocean of existence. (165)
She is the time that bestows fortune upon the ocean of existence; she is filled with the fortune of the ocean of existence;
she is devoted to the fortune of the ocean of existence; she is permeated by the fortune of the ocean of existence. 166.
She is the movement of fortune within the ocean of existence, she is the accumulation of fortune within the ocean of existence;
she is the excellent path to fortune within the ocean of existence, and she is the bestower of excellent fortune within the ocean of existence.
She who knows the ways of fortune within the ocean of existence; she who bestows the wisdom regarding the fortune within the ocean of existence;
she who is the sovereign over the ways of fortune within the ocean of existence; she who is the river of the ways of fortune within the ocean of existence. 168.

Skilled in the enjoyments of the ocean of existence, bestowing the enjoyments of the ocean of existence, dense with the fortunes of the ocean of existence, and entwined with the enjoyments of the ocean of existence. (169)
She is the Gandhārī of the enjoyments in the ocean of existence, strung together with the enjoyments of the ocean of existence;
she is the exquisite flavor of the enjoyments in the ocean of existence, and she possesses a great longing for the enjoyments of the ocean of existence.
She is the knot of enjoyments in the ocean of existence, the yoginī of enjoyments in the ocean of existence;
she is the tongue of enjoyments in the ocean of existence, and she is adorned with the splendor of enjoyments in the ocean of existence. || 171 ||
She is the splendor of the enjoyments of the ocean of existence, she is expanded by the enjoyments of the ocean of existence;
she is the bestower of the boons of the enjoyments of the ocean of existence, and she is praised by the enjoyments of the ocean of existence. || 172 ||
Skilled in the enjoyments of the ocean of existence, adorned by the enjoyments of the ocean of existence;
the mother who brings about the piercing of the ocean of existence, the protector of the piercing of the ocean of existence. || 173 ||

The arrangement of the divisions of the ocean of existence, protected by the divisions of the ocean of existence, determined by the divisions of the ocean of existence, and free from desire for the divisions of the ocean of existence. || 174 ||
She is the architect of the diverse structures of the ocean of existence; she is established upon the various divisions of the ocean of existence;
she destroys the multitudes of the diverse realms within the ocean of existence; she delights in the multitude of those very divisions. 175.
She is the mistress of the karma that shatters the ocean of existence, she whose actions shatter the ocean of existence;
she is the mistress of auspiciousness, the mother of the auspicious, the auspicious one herself, and the dweller in the auspicious.
Bhadreśvarī, Bhadravatī, Bhadrasthā, Bhadradāyinī;
Bhadrarūpā, Bhadramayī, Bhadradā, and Bhadrabhāṣiṇī. || 177 ||
She whose ears are auspicious, she whose appearance is auspicious, the auspicious mother, the one whose abode is auspicious;
she whose actions are auspicious, she whose arts are auspicious, the auspicious one, and she who increases what is auspicious. || 178 ||
She who delights in auspicious play, who possesses auspicious arts, who desires auspicious pastimes,
who brings about auspiciousness, who is devoted to the auspicious, whose limbs are auspicious, and who is the minister of the auspicious. (179)
She is auspicious knowledge and inauspicious knowledge; she is auspicious speech and the speaker of auspiciousness.
She bestows blessings upon kings, she is the sovereign, the creeper of the earth, and the sustainer of the world.
She is the enjoyment of kings, the splendor of kings, the hope of kings, and the bestower of royal form;
she is the appearance of kings, the delight of kings, the fortune of kings, and the supreme well-being of kings. 181.
She is the policy of kings, the prosperity of kings, and the fear of kings; she is the source of terror, the wave of bliss for the world, and the beauty of worldly bliss. 182.
She who brings about the bliss of existence, she who increases the bliss of existence, she who delights in the bliss of existence, and she who bestows the bliss of existence. || 183 ||
She who generates worldly bliss and whose very form is worldly bliss—
for him who recites this hymn every day, endowed with devotion— 184.
Being endowed with devotion to the guru and intent upon the service of the guru, he should have his senses conquered, speak the truth, and keep his mouth filled with betel. || 185 ||
By day, by night, and at the junction of dawn and dusk, he becomes the Supreme Lord;
by the mere recitation of this hymn, a king will certainly be brought under one's control. 186.
The wise one is himself Hara in all tantras among all the scriptures, having practiced [the teachings] from the mouth of the guru and remaining in the presence of the guru. (187)
He who recites or even hears [this] at the junctions of time (saṃdhyā) in sacred places of Śiva, in an empty house, or at a crossroads, is a yogi; of this there is no doubt. || 188 ||
One should give away all one's possessions as a sacrificial fee, including even one's wife and sons; then, with a mind free and at ease, one should recite this hymn of praise. (189)
O Goddess, one who is devoted to this hymn is undoubtedly the very form of Hara;
whoever should always recite or even listen to it with a single-minded focus. (190)
He shall be long-lived, happy, and eloquent; there is no doubt that his speech will be such.
By remaining devoted to the feet of the Guru, he will become beloved by women. (191)
O beloved, like a wise preceptor who is wealthy, virtuous, illustrious, and intelligent, one should become dear to all and always worship this hymn. (192)
O Goddess, the accomplishment of mantras is as if held in his very hand; of this there is no doubt.
He shall attain the status of Kubera, for all supernatural powers (siddhis) are indeed subject to him. (193)

And whatever woman has lost her son, or is afflicted by misfortune; whether she be barren, or one whose children are like crows (a "crow-barren" woman), or a woman whose offspring die in infancy. || 194 ||
O Great Goddess, those who are destitute of wealth and grain, and who are overwhelmed by disease and grief—by them this [mantra] should indeed be written upon birch bark. 195.
It should be worn on the left arm; by that, it will bestow happiness.
Thus, she who was tormented by suffering went again and again. (196)
In an assembly, in calamity, in verbal dispute, in danger from an enemy, in battle with the fourfold army, and likewise in every kind of misfortune or affliction; || 197 ||
By remembering this, auspicious doubts depart to a great distance.
This should not be given to the disciple of another, nor to one who lacks devotion, nor to a wicked person.
O Queen of the Gods, one should not give [this] to a hypocrite, one of evil conduct, or a miser;
rather, one should give it to a disciple who is peaceful, humble, and self-controlled.
For one who is devoted, endowed with tranquility, and intent upon the worship of Rāja, it is impossible to describe [the merit] even in thousands of future births. || 200 ||
O sweet-spoken one, even Brahmā previously described to Viṣṇu the greatness of this mere hymn, even with hundreds of millions of mouths.
Even now, O Supreme Goddess, this has been told to you out of affection;
it must be kept secret from those who are bound by ignorance (paśus) and should never be disclosed.
Thus ends the hymn of the thousand names beginning with the letter *Bha*, dedicated to Bhuvaneśvarī, within the dialogue between Īśvara and Pārvatī in the Great Ocean of Tantras.
[Now follows] the Hymn to the Heart of Śrī Bhuvaneśvarī.
The Goddess said:
O Blessed One, speak that hymn which accomplishes all desires, by the mere hearing of which nothing else remains to be heard. (1)
O Brahmin, if you would show me favor and if you have affection for me, then tell me of that which is pure upon this earth.
Īśvara said:
Listen, O Goddess, I shall proclaim the heart-mantra of Bhuvaneśvarī, which accomplishes all desires and bestows fame; it is a hymn that grants renown. (3)

Oṃ. Of this mantra of the Śrī Bhuvaneśvarī-hṛdaya-stotra, Śakti is the seer (ṛṣi), Gāyatrī is the meter (chandaḥ), Bhuvaneśvarī is the deity (devatā), the letter *ha* is the seed-syllable (bīja), the letter *ī* is the power (śakti), and the letter *ra* is the pin (kīlaka). Its application (viniyoga) is for the purpose of attaining all desired objects of the mind through recitation.

Oṃ hrīṃ, salutation to the heart (hṛdayāya) 1; Oṃ śrīṃ, svāhā to the head (śirase) 2; Oṃ aiṃ, vaṣaṭ to the crest-lock (śikhāyai) 3; Oṃ hrīṃ, huṃ to the armor (kavacāya) 4; Oṃ śrīṃ, vauṣaṭ to the three eyes (netratrayāya) 5; Oṃ aiṃ, phaṭ to the weapon (astrāya). Thus is the ritual placement of the six limbs beginning with the heart (hṛdyādi-ṣaḍaṅga-nyāsa).

Oṃ hrīṃ, salutation to both thumbs (1); Oṃ śrīṃ, salutation to both index fingers (2); Oṃ aiṃ, salutation to both middle fingers (3); Oṃ hrīṃ, salutation to both ring fingers (4); Oṃ śrīṃ, salutation to both little fingers (5); Oṃ aiṃ, salutation to the palms and backs of the hands (6). Thus.
The ritual placement upon the limbs (karanyāsa).
Then one should meditate upon the Yoga-born Yoginī, the mother of the creators beginning with Brahmā,
the life-sustainer of the gods, whose fierce-limbed body is the blazing supreme light of victory.
Holding a conch, a discus, an arrow, and a bow in her four lotus-like arms—
she who is primordial Māyā, the most distinguished, the source of the worlds of Bhava and Bhavabhū, and the ground that bears the burden of the earth.

We worship that Śrī Bhuvaneśvarī, by whose command the unborn Lord of Śrī creates this entire universe beginning with the sky as if it were his own legitimate offspring, and by whom Bhava maintains and destroys it at its end.

We worship that Śrī Bhuvaneśvarī, who brings joy to the people of the world, who is known as Jayā, who is illustrious, whose source is the excellent sacrifice of the yantra, and who has conquered the vast expansion created by immeasurable enemies.

When Hari had fallen asleep at the end of the three worlds, the Creator was born from the lotus arising from His navel; we worship that Śrī Bhuvaneśvarī, upon whose feet he rested when the world was blind with darkness.
We worship that Śrī Bhuvaneśvarī, whose birth is not found anywhere, nor is there any continuous existence for her here, nor is there any cessation of all karma for her.

We worship that Śrī Bhuvaneśvarī, whose mind is fierce with the casting of side-glances, who has bestowed her wealth, whose heart is moist with compassion, and who grants the desired object to those with true devotion.
We worship that Śrī Bhuvaneśvarī, who is the fierce Kālī from whom the birth of the world arose, who sustains it in its midst, and who devours it all at the end. 10.
We worship that Śrī Bhuvaneśvarī, by whom the individual soul perceives no dream during the state of deep sleep, yet awakens to experience some dream while in the waking state. 11.

We worship that venerable Bhuvaneśvarī, who is independent; for by obtaining her side-long glances, which are like buds throbbing with compassion, the Siddhas do not find poetic skill or even lordship in any single place.
We worship that Śrī Bhuvaneśvarī, whose compassionate glances cause the lotus of her blossoming face to radiate within the heart, while her rays flash forth in every direction.
We worship that Śrī Bhuvaneśvarī, by whom [her devotees], adorned with tilakas following their passion, their limbs overflowing with ancient love, and being utterly fearless, remain ever joyful. 14.
We worship that Śrī Bhuvaneśvarī, before whom Hari, Viriñci, Hara, and Īśitā stand as protectors, their pride broken by her grace, and who always desires their favor. 15.

Those who chant the mantra whose first syllable is *manu* (ma), which has *hara* (ha) situated in fire (*ra*), and which is joined with the moon of the left ear (*va*), are indeed highly praised; we worship that venerable Bhuvaneśvarī. 16.
May that venerable Bhuvaneśvarī, whose heart is ever moist with the essence of love, be gracious to me—she by whose compassionate glance those who worship her feet become like Kubera. (17)
This hymn to Bhuvaneśvarī is easy to recite with joy, always to be well-served by the virtuous;
it bestows happiness, destroys the taints of the Kali age, and is praiseworthy for those who listen well or recite it.
Whoever, with a concentrated mind, should recite this heart-essence of a hymn—
The goddess Bhuvaneśvarī, being pleased, shall become the bestower of his desires.
It bestows wealth, long life, merit, and a virtuous mind, as well as steadfast devotion to the gods and especially devotion to the guru. (20)
On the full moon day, on the fourteenth day, and especially on a Tuesday,
this hymn should be recited with effort in the temple of the deity.
The fruit of this hymn shall be attained by reciting it anywhere at all;
one whose body is purified should always recite it in all sacred places of the Goddess of Gods.
Thus ends the Hṛdayastotra of Śrī Bhuvaneśvarī, within the Bhuvaneśvarī-paṭala of the Nīlasarasvatī-tantra, in the dialogue between the Śrī Devī and the Lord.
Now begins the Śrībhuvaneśvarī Stotra:
I praise Ambikā, the cause of the universe, who is composed of bliss, who is the manifest embodiment of the Word-Brahman (Śabdabrahman), for the sake of attaining all prosperity. (1)
O Mother! Having praised you— the primordial mother of all, the bestower of bodies upon the lotus-born Brahmā, Viṣṇu, and Śiva,
and the cause of the creation, maintenance, and destruction of the three worlds— I purify my speech with it.

O Daughter of the Mountain King! You alone are indeed the cause of the possession of power by the God who is the enemy of Manmatha, who assumes the forms of earth, water, fire, the best of winds, the Hotṛ priest, the moon, and the sun.
O Mother, I understand that very reason for the preeminence of the triple-streamed Gaṅgā, who is worshipped by all the gods:
that she constantly revolves within the matted locks of Śambhu, which are purified by the pollen of your lotus feet.

The lord of the digits (the moon) delights the night-lily, but no other sun delights the day-lotus, nor any other; yet who else has the power for this supreme act of gladdening in a single instance? You, however, cause the entire universe to rejoice through your own vision.
Even now you possess the fresh youth of all the worlds; though the daughter of the King of Mountains, you are exceedingly tender.
Though the mother of the Triple Veda, you have never been fully beheld. O Gaurī, you are the object of meditation, yet you do not stand within the path of the mind.

O Mother of the worlds! Those who, having attained after a long time this human birth so difficult to obtain, and having further acquired proficiency in their own senses, do not worship you—having climbed to the very top of the ladder, they fall once again. [Those who do not worship you with sandalwood paste mixed with camphor powder and cool water, nor with flowers of fragrant scent...]
For indeed, O Bhavānī! those who rule over all the worlds, being filled with longing, worship you; they truly become renowned. 8.
Having entered the central path of the first lotus and fashioned the universe like the sleeping king of serpents,
she assumes the shimmering grace of a circle of lightning-streaks, bursting through five lotuses as she pervades them all.

O Mother, Consort of Maheśvara! Those whose bodies have been sprinkled by the nectar-like essence flowing from You along that path, and who have thereby regained their way home—may they never again enter a womb. May You never flash within the hearts of such as these. 10.

O Gaurī! With my mind, I meditate upon your form—possessing a face made beautiful by the weight of dangling earrings, with full and sloping breasts and a slender, rounded waist; and whose hands are adorned with the lotus, the rosary for meditation, and the water-pot.
Having established myself in yoga, having conquered the six internal enemies, and having restrained the host of senses within a tranquil mind...
O Bhuvaneśvarī! Yogis behold you, whose beautiful face is adorned with hands holding a noose, a goad, and granting the gestures of fearlessness and boons. 12.

Being consecrated by four jars of nectar turned clockwise, which resemble molten gold, and holding two beautiful lotuses in your two hands, you yourself become Padmā, bestowing the boons of fearlessness and prosperity. 13.

O Goddess Bhavānī! You are Durgā, having ascended the king of beasts with your creeper-like arms—eight in number, bearing various formidable weapons—and possessing the luster of a blade of dūrvā grass, you surpass the wings of the enemies of the immortals. 14.

I repeatedly remember the young Pulinda woman—her face radiant with droplets of water from the summer heat, a necklace fashioned from *guñjā* berries, clad in yellow silk, possessing a dark luster, intoxicated by the languor of love—and who was followed by swans whose gait and tinkling anklets were seen from afar, like embodied words of meaning accompanying her. Followed by swans whose gait and tinkling anklets were seen from afar, as if by embodied words of meaning; [and] the young Pulinda woman, whose face was beautified by sprays of water from the summer heat, who had fashioned a necklace from *guñjā* berries, who wore yellow garments, who possessed a dark splendor, and who was intoxicated by the languor of the god of love.
O Consort of Śrīkaṇṭha! I place upon my head your two feet, which resemble two lotuses with well-formed stalks rising upward. 16.

O Bhavānī! I bow to your two auspicious calves, which are being gazed upon by the bull-bannered Lord Śiva with eyes untroubled by satiety as if he were looking at them with both his own eyes, having uprooted his eye on the forehead,
and which are tremulous with intense passion.
I remember your thighs, which surpassed the pride of an elephant’s trunk in both girth and softness;
they were like two pillars provided by your youth to support the weight of your hips.
And your hips and breasts, their strength already fully developed, shall soon be further expanded together by your youth as it passes beyond childhood.

O friends, having discerned your form through the play of the line of body hair, may your waist flash within the center of my heart—filled with the waters of loveliness by your fresh youth, as if it were a tender sprout offered by Youth to quench the fire of Kama’s eye in Shiva;
O Goddess, may I never forget that which has entered your navel. 20.
Even while the Lord bears ashes that betray his residence [in the cremation ground], those two breasts of yours, smeared with saffron paste,
recall the frontal globes of an intoxicated elephant rising from a bath— globes momentarily visible with foam and reddened by vermilion.
O Mother, may those two arms of my enemy— beautiful with streams of radiant luster flowing from throats that are too long,
fashioned like two long nooses by the hand of his servant to seize me by the neck— not transgress the path of my memory.

O Daughter of the Mountain King! Having contemplated your neck—neither too long, stealing the grace of fashioned conch shells, resplendent with various ornaments, and endowed with enchanting qualities—I never reach satiety.
[I likewise contemplate] your eyes that are exceedingly long, your noble forehead, and the lines of your cheeks slightly blossoming with a gentle smile.
O Mother! he who repeatedly remembers your face with its bimba-red lips and high, long nose—he alone has truly been born.

O Goddess, for him who with his mind perceives your mass of hair—which is like a digit of the moon covered in frost and indistinguishable from a swarm of bees hovering over abundant fragrant flowers—the ancient bond falls away of its own accord. (25)
That mortal here who, with a perpetually moist inner soul, recites this hymn of the illustrious ones— which is the ripening of sacred learning and virtuous conduct—
becomes a vessel for the highest prosperity, characterized by the fortune of royal crowns bowing at his feet.
For a long time. || 26 ||
Thus ends the Śrībhuvaneśvarīstotra in the Śrīrudrayāmala Tantra.
Now begins the Śrībhuvaneśvarīkramacandrikā in the ritual manual (paddhati) of Śrī Pṛthvīdhara Ācārya.
Śrīḥ.
I salute the Guru, the manifestation of consciousness, whose form is supreme bliss.
By means of his own self-luminosity, he sets forth this great *Bhuvaneśī-krama*.
Then, having risen during the *brāhma-muhūrta*, the practitioner (*mantrin*), having meditated upon the lotus feet of the venerable Guru upon his own head, should offer this prayer of salutation:
"We offer our word of homage to Śiva, whose form is the bliss of the infinite ether, who is moist with compassion, and who has assumed the form of the Guru. (2)
I salute the venerable Bhuvaneśvarī, who resides upon the seat of erotic passion, and who is the supreme creeper sprouting from the seed known as self-luminous reflective awareness. 3.

Having risen during the *brāhma-muhūrta*, [one should meditate] upon Him in the pure lunar orb of consciousness within the white lotus at the aperture of Brahmā (*brahmarandhra*), appearing like crystal and displaying the gestures of granting boons and fearlessness.
He is embraced by his consort, who stands upon his left lap and holds a long blue lotus; he is adorned with three eyes and possesses a red spear. || 5 ||
One should remember him with a serene face and peaceful countenance, preceded by his name;
having recollected his two feet, which consist of red and white light.
One should visualize the Guru and the Guru’s wife as the God and the Goddess,
reciting the *pādukā* mantra according to the instruction of one's own Guru.
One should worship with the offerings of fragrance and so forth, accompanied by their respective mudrās.

For example: *Laṃ*, to the one whose self is Earth, whose self is the Supreme Self, whose self is the primordial nature of the subtle element of fragrance, to the venerable Guru-Nātha, I offer fragrance; [this is done] with the two little fingers (*kaniṣṭhā*). *Haṃ*, to the one whose self is Space...

I offer a flower to the two thumbs for the venerable Guru-nātha, who is the Supreme Self (paramātman), whose nature is the subtle element of sound (śabdatanmātra-prakṛti). I offer incense to the two index fingers for the venerable Guru-nātha, who is the Supreme Self, whose nature is the subtle element of touch (sparśatanmātra-prakṛti), and who is of the nature of air (vāyavyātman).

*Raṃ*, to the Self of Fire, the Supreme Self, the Self of the primordial nature of the subtle element of form, to the venerable Guru-Nātha, I offer a lamp in the middle fingers. *Vaṃ*, to the Self of Air, the Supreme Self...

With the two ring fingers: "I offer the food offering (naivedya) to the venerable Guru-Nātha, whose nature is the subtle element of taste. With the hollowed palms joined together: "I offer betel (tāmbūla) to the venerable Guru-Nātha, whose nature is Śakti, whose nature is the Supreme Self (Paramātman), and whose nature is all the subtle elements (sarva-tanmātra). Thus, with these ritual services (upacāra).

Having fully worshipped the illustrious Guru-nātha, one should pray: "O Lord of the World! Whatever I do from morning until evening, and from evening until morning, may that be an act of worship unto You."

Having prostrated before one's own guru according to the aforementioned method, preceded by his name—for example: "Aiṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ, I worship the consciousness of Amukānandanātha, or the venerable *śrīpādukā* joined with the *śakti*; obeisance"—and having thus paid homage:
Heramba, Kṣetrapāla, Vāgiśa, and likewise Vaṭuka;
the venerable Guru, Nātha, Ānanda, Bhairava, and the supreme Bharavī.
Having thus recited the hymn to the Guru’s sandals in this sequence:
"To that direction, this handful of flowers is perpetually cast, made resonant by the humming of bees and double-tongued insects."
Wherein the Blessed One, the sovereign of gurus and the eternal witness to the drama of the universe's arising and dissolution, remains awake.

Having thus paid homage with the five mudrās, one should meditate upon the root mantra (mūlavidyā). As follows: One should contemplate one's own deity from the base up to the aperture of Brahmā (brahmarandhra), resembling ten million suns in brilliance and as cooling as ten million moons.
Having meditated for some time with a firm posture and one-pointed concentration upon that [light] which shines like the rising sun, one shall become happy as long as one breathes.
Having meditated upon the root-vidyā according to the method thus stated, one should perform the mental recitation (saṃkalpa) of the ajapā. It is as follows:

Of this venerable ajapā-gāyatrī mantra, Haṃsa is the seer (ṛṣi), Paramahaṃsa is the deity (devatā), Avyakta-gāyatrī is the meter (chandas), Haṃ is the seed-syllable (bīja), Saḥ is the power (śakti), So’haṃ is the pin (kīlaka), and Praṇava is the essence (tatva).

"Nāda is my place, the udātta accent is my tone, and white is my color; for the sake of destroying all my sins and for the sake of attaining the realization of my own true nature, I shall perform today, within this day and night, the recitation of the Ajapā Gāyatrī twenty-one thousand six hundred times in the form of inhalation and exhalation."

Having formed the resolve with the mantra "I am He" (*haṃsaḥ so'ham*), one should perform breath control (*prāṇāyāma*), purification of the hands (*karaśuddhi*), and the ritual placement of the six limbs (*ṣaḍaṅganyāsa*). [Thus: *hsāṃ* to the heart, the essence of the sun, *namaḥ* on the two thumbs. (p. 107)

Hsīṃ, to the one whose self is Soma, svāhā to the head, on the two index fingers; hsūṃ, to the one whose self is the stainless (nirañjana), vaṣaṭ to the crest-lock (śikhā), on the two middle fingers; hsaiṃ, to the one whose self is the non-manifest (nirābhāsa), huṃ to the armor (kavaca), on the two ring fingers; hsaiṃ, to the one whose self impels the bodiless and subtle (atanusūkṣmapracodayātmane), vauṣaṭ to the three eyes, on the two little fingers; hsaḥ.

The six-limbed ritual (*ṣaḍaṅga*) is performed with "Phaṭ" for the weapon (*astra*) directed toward the palms and the backs of the hands, [recited] over the Self whose nature is the awakening of the unmanifest. Now, the meditation (*dhyāna*):
one should meditate upon oneself as being of the nature of Śiva, joined with the two wings known as Fire and Moon.
Remembering "Haṃsa" as that which goes out with the sound *sa* and enters with the sound *ha*, one realizes "So 'ham" (I am He) through the absence of the consonants.
Having withdrawn the two wings, one should contemplate oneself in the form of an egg;

having meditated upon the Supreme Self in the form of the syllable *Oṃ*, practicing the *Tāra* [mantra], [one visualizes]: *Oṃ*. The *ādhāra-cakra* is the locus of the earth, red in color, four-petaled, consisting of four syllables, and endowed with four powers: *vaṃ*.

*Śaṃ ṣaṃ saṃ*. In the center of that [mandala], one should worship Gaṇeśa together with Siddhi and Buddhi. Regarding the *majapā-japa* performed on the previous day: it consists of twenty-one thousand six hundred recitations, including the six hundred [recitations] performed in the center with the perfected mantra *haṃsaḥ so'ham* for the sake of the Great Elephant-faced One, whose nature is the Supreme Brahman.

I offer this; obeisance! Then, at the Svādhiṣṭhāna-cakra, the seat of fire, which is yellow in color and possesses six syllables—namely *baṃ bhaṃ maṃ yaṃ raṃ laṃ*—in the center of its lotus pericarp, one should perform [the recitation] six thousand times (*ṣaṭsahasram*) with the perfected mantra "Haṃsaḥ So’ham" for the sake of Śrī Brahmā, whose nature is the Supreme Brahman.

I offer the Ajapā-japa together with Sāvitrī; obeisance! Then, the Maṇipūra-cakra is located at the navel; it has ten petals, is dark green in color, and consists of ten syllables: ḍaṃ, ḍhaṃ, ṇaṃ, taṃ, thaṃ, daṃ, dhaṃ, naṃ, paṃ, phaṃ. In its center, one recites "Haṃsaḥ So'ham" six thousand times (6,000).

I offer this Ajapā-japa, performed with the perfected mantra, to Viṣṇu, who is the very nature of the glorious Supreme Brahman, accompanied by Lakṣmī; obeisance! Now, the Anāhata-cakra is located in the heart region; it has twelve petals, is white in color, and consists of the twelve syllables: *kaṃ khaṃ gaṃ*.

Ghaṃ ṅaṃ caṃ chaṃ jaṃ jhaṃ ñaṃ ṭaṃ ṭhaṃ. In the midst of these, the *ajapājapa* performed with the perfected mantra "haṃsaḥ so'ham" (six thousand times, 6000), I offer this *ajapājapa* to Rudra, who is the nature of the venerable Supreme Brahman, together with Gaurī; salutations! Now, the Viśuddha-cakra.

The throat center has sixteen petals and is the color of crystal; it possesses the sixteen vowels: aṃ, āṃ, i, īṃ, u, ūṃ, ṛṃ, ṝṃ, ḷṃ, ḹṃ, eṃ, aiṃ, oṃ, auṃ, aṃ, aḥ. In its center, one thousand (1000) repetitions of the perfected mantra "haṃsaḥ so'ham" constitute the *ajapājapa* for the sake of the one whose nature is the glorious Supreme Brahman.

I offer the *ajapājapa* to the individual soul (*jīvātman*), accompanied by the creative power of the Lord; obeisance! Now, the *ājñācakra*, located between the eyebrows, having two petals, the color of lightning, and two syllables—*haṃ* and *kṣaṃ*—in the center of the pericarp of the lotus, [the recitation] is performed with the perfected mantra *haṃsaḥ so’ham* one thousand times.
Having offered [the prayer] with "I offer the ajapā-japa to the venerable Supreme Brahman, accompanied by the supreme Śiva and Śakti; obeisance," one should perform the same on the following day.
Having thus performed the morning rites, having bid farewell to the Guru in his own place, and having bowed to the earth, one should go outside.
Namely:
O Goddess Samudramekhalā, whose breasts are the circle of mountains! (p. 108)
Salutations to you, the consort of Viṣṇu; forgive my touch of your feet.

Having thus paid homage with the two hollowed palms, one should go outside. O Dear One! I shall now describe the daily ritual for those whose minds are intent on the propitiation of the Mantra; one should rise every day at the time of dawn.
Having restrained his senses, he should go a long distance outside his own village;
having observed a pure spot that is fertile and free of grass,
he should cover that area with grass and summon fresh earth.
Having fetched that water from the sacred bathing place (tīrtha), one should fill a large vessel with it.

For example: having taken a large vessel full of water and some earth, and having set it down on the ground after first pouring out some water, one should divide the earth into three parts; then, taking one part for the purification of urine, one part for the purification of feces, and one part for...

Having divided the vessels into three parts for the purpose of cleansing the hands, feet, and so forth, one should void excrement while facing south. Therein, the formal resolve (*saṃkalpa*) is as follows:
"May the sages, gods, piśācas, yakṣas, and rākṣasas depart."
I shall perform the rite of purification for all the hosts of ancestors and spirits.
Having spoken thus and struck the three *tāla* sounds, one should uncover the head with a cloth and perform the evacuation of waste.
In the morning, facing north, or at night, facing south, one should then rise and perform the purification (*śauca*).
Then one should utter "May the spirits depart" and perform the triple clapping of the hands;
having respectfully taken earth in the measure of a large myrobalan fruit.
Purification should be performed with diligence until the odor and the stain have been removed.
In that regard, the rule for purification is as follows: one application of clay on the penis, three on the hand, and two on both hands together is prescribed;
one should apply one application each on the two feet—this is proclaimed as the purification for urination.
Thus is the purification after urination.
Five applications of clay are prescribed for the anus, ten for the hands, and seven for both together;
one should apply it three times to the feet—this is declared to be the purification of the anus.
Thus concludes the purification after voiding excrement. Thereafter, one should discard mouthfuls of water. Regarding this, the rule is:
one becomes pure through four, eight, three, and six mouthfuls of water respectively.
Upon passing urine, voiding excrement, after eating, and even upon the emission of semen.
This is its meaning:

one should discard four mouthfuls of water after urinating, eight after defecating, three after eating, and six after the emission of semen. Having thus performed the rules for purification, the procedure for cleaning the teeth follows:
O beloved! One should collect a tooth-stick made from mango, campaka, jambu, apāmārga, or similar trees, or from the jātī tree or the badara.
In that regard, the prayer is:
"O Lord of the Forest, grant us long life, strength, fame, luster, progeny, cattle, wealth, prosperity, wisdom, and intelligence."
