Having thus petitioned the lord of the forest, and having taken a tooth-stick (dantakāṣṭha) measuring eighteen, twelve, nine,
or six finger-breadths, one should consecrate it sixteen times with this mantra: *Oṃ namo bhagavate maṇibhadrāya yajñasenādhipataye kili kili svāhā*.

Having purified the teeth along with the tongue by means of the mantra *klīṃ kāmadevāya namaḥ*, one should wash the mouth three times with the root mantra (*mūla*). Then, taking the materials for bathing and reciting the *prātaḥsmaraṇa* and other prayers, one should go to a body of water such as a river and bathe. It is as follows:

Having washed the hands and feet and performed the ritual sipping of water (ācamana), one should make the formal resolve (saṃkalpa): "Having proclaimed the lunar date and other details, for the sake of the destruction of all my sins and for the attainment of the grace of the deity, I shall perform the bath. Therein, first is the clay bath: beginning from the feet with the root mantra...

Having thus performed the clay-bath (mṛttikā-snāna) by [cleansing] from the knees up to the knees, from the knees up to the navel, from the navel up to the chest, from the chest up to the throat, and from the throat up to the crown of the head;
then, having performed the Vedic bath ending with the Aghamarṣaṇa rite, one should perform the Tantric bath. It is as follows:
Oṃ hrīṃ, I purify the principle of the self (ātmatattva), svāhā; Oṃ hrīṃ, I purify the principle of knowledge (vidyātattva), svāhā;

Oṃ hrīṃ, I purify the principle of Śiva (śivatattva), svāhā. Having wiped [the mouth] twice and touched the nose, the two eyes, the head, and the right ear once, one should thus perform the ritual sipping of water (ācamana).
The method of bathing is twofold, distinguished as external and internal.
Among these, first is the internal bath:
O Pārvatī, the internal bath is exceedingly secret.
I shall speak for the sake of destroying existence and for the attainment of the group of five.
Having recollected the three rivers from within the midst of the three feet,
one should contemplate the flowing stream of Being-Consciousness-Bliss as the object of one's meditative realization.
For yogins, the means to liberation for men arises from mere remembrance;
therefore, one should contemplate oneself as being bathed by that [remembrance] for the sake of the pacification of all mental states.
The *iḍā* is renowned as the Gaṅgā, and the *piṅgalā* as the river Yamunā;
Sarasvatī is to be known as being between them—that is remembered as Prayāga.
Having thus completed the internal bath through the sequence of meditative cultivation, one should perform the external mantra-bath as follows:
facing the eastern direction, one should supplicate the earth and the Guru with these two mantras:
O Goddess! You always provide sustenance and nourishment for all beings;
by that truth, protect me and release me from my bonds, O Upholder!
That which has the form of an unbroken circle pervades all that is moving and unmoving.
Salutation to that venerable Guru by whom that state has been revealed.

Having paid homage to these two, standing in water reaching the navel, one should draw a triangle, a hexagon, an eight-petaled lotus, a sixteen-petaled lotus, and a square within the water using the little finger; then, having written the root-syllable in the center of the triangle, [one should invoke] the holy water from the solar orb with the goad-mudrā: *aiṃ* to the heart.
Having drawn [the water] with the mantra "namaḥ" and having cast it into the sacred site (tīrtha), one should invoke the presence of that sacred site there. The mantra is:
"O Ravi! O God, O Divākara! By the truth that the sacred sites within the belly of the universe have been touched by your rays, grant me the sacred site!"
O Gaṅgā, Yamunā, Godāvarī, Sarasvatī! O Narmadā, Sindhu, Kāverī! Be present in these waters.
"O Gaṅgā, Yamunā... [and so forth]. O beautiful one, I invoke that Goddess here for the purpose of bathing. Come, O Gaṅgā! Salutations to you, who are endowed with all sacred fords (tīrthas)."

"Oṃ aiṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ, O Tīrthaśakti, who consists of all bliss, come, come, svāhā!"—with this mantra and the Aṅkuśa mudrā, one should perform the union, and then display the following mudrās: 1. Āvāhanī (invocation), 2. Sthāpanī (installation), 3. Sannirodhinī (confinement), 4. Avaguṇṭhanī (veiling), 5. Sammukhīkaraṇī (facing toward), 6. Dhenu (the cow), and 7. Yoni (the source). These are they.
Having displayed the seven mudrās, one should perform the six-limbed rite (*ṣaḍaṅga*) as follows: *Oṃ hrāṃ* to the heart, *namaḥ* with both thumbs; *hrriṃ* to the head...
Svāhā! Salutation to the two index fingers. Hrūṃ! Vaṣaṭ to the crest-lock; salutation to the two middle fingers.
Hraiṃ! Huṃ to the armor; salutation to the two ring fingers. Hrauṃ! Vauṣaṭ to the eyes;
salutation to the two little fingers. Hraḥ! Phaṭ to the weapon; salutation to the palms and backs of the hands.

Having thus performed the six-limbed rite (*ṣaḍaṅga*), covering [the head] with both hands and consecrating it seven times with the root mantra, and having recited the Amṛteśvarī mantra seven times and meditated upon her, one should sip water (*ācamana*) and bathe. It is as follows: *Oṃ hrīṃ klīṃ āṃ, O Immortal One, O Source of Nectar, O Mistress of Nectar, O Showerer of Nectar, cause nectar to flow forth!* (*amṛte amṛtodbhave amṛteśvari amṛtavarṣiṇi amṛtaṃ srāvaya*).

srāvaya sāṃ jūṃ jūṃ saḥ amṛteśvaryai svāhā | O Bhavānī! I meditate upon you, the Mistress of Nectar (Amṛteśvarī), who satisfies all that moves and is stationary with the flood of your outpouring nectar-rays, for the sake of the pacification of worldly existence.
Meditating upon the inner power that proceeds from the foundation to the aperture of Brahma,
one should perform an internal bath with its shower of nectar.
Having meditated according to the method thus described, and having submerged and emerged, one should perform the sprinkling (*mārjana*) seven times with the root mantra.

Then, one should perform the *aghamarṣaṇa*. It is as follows: taking water in the palm of the right hand, consecrating it seven times with the root mantra while recollecting it as being of the nature of consciousness (*cid-rūpa*), and [using] the left hand with the *saṃghaṭṭa* mudrā—

Having consecrated [the disciple] three times on the head with the root-mantra (*mūlavidyā*), one should collect the remaining water with the *iḍā* [channel], cleanse the internal channel, and expel the turbid matter, which resembles soot, through the *piṅgalā* [channel]. Then, visualizing a diamond-stone (*vajraśilā*) on the left side, one should cause [the disciple] to strike it against the diamond-stone situated in the left portion while reciting the mantra "huṃ phaṭ. Thereafter—
Having sprinkled [the disciple] three times on the head with the *yonimudrā* using the root mantra (*mūla*), one should sprinkle him three times on the heart and the two arms.
Then, having again sprinkled him three times on the head with the *yonimudrā* using the root mantra, one should sprinkle him three times on the heart and the two arms.
Then follows the water libation (*jalatarpaṇa*). Having performed the water libation with the words, "I offer libations to those deities," [one recites]: *oṃ aiṃ hrīṃ*.
Having offered libations three times with the mantra, "Śrīṃ, I satiate the Śrīpādukā of Ambā Bhuvaneśvarī," one should go outside.

Having put on two washed garments that have been sprinkled with water while reciting the Mūlamantra, and having performed the ritual sipping of water (ācamana), one should apply sacred ash (vibhūti). It is as follows:
Having washed his hands and feet, he should sip water with the root-mantra; then he should put on new and pure upper garments and sacred threads.
Having first performed the ash-bath, one should then apply the triple mark (tripuṇḍra).
Thereafter, sitting properly upon kuśa grass, one should perform the ritual dusting (uddhūlana) in the prescribed sequence.
O Goddess, one should perform the smearing of all limbs from head to foot with fresh white moist ashes, using either the Praṇava or the Śiva-mantra.
Then one should fashion the Tripuṇḍra, which is also called Triyāyuṣa.
For example: having placed the sacrificial offering in the left hand and covered it with the right hand, one recites: "O Jātavedas, let us press the Soma for you; burn away the wealth of the enemy.
May he carry us across all difficulties as Agni carries us across a river with a boat, beyond all misfortunes. (Ṛgveda 1.7.6).
p.
112) With the Gāyatrī [Oṃ bhūrbhuvaḥ svaḥ | We meditate upon that excellent splendor of the divine Savitṛ; may he impel our intellects]: with the Tryambaka [Oṃ tryambakaṃ yajāmahe...].
Fragrant, the increaser of nourishment—may I be released from death like a cucumber from its stalk, yet not from immortality. 3.60 I am Agni; by birth I am Jātavedas.
Ghee is my eye, nectar is in my mouth. I am the light, the threefold measurer of the realm of space, the unaging.
I am Dharma, named Havir. [18.66] Do not harm us in our offspring, nor in our descendants, nor in our life-span;
do not harm us in our cows, nor in our horses. O Rudra, do not slay our heroic men who are wrathful against us. Bearing oblations, we invoke you forever. [16.16] The triple-life-span of Jamadagni.

[“Oṃ, the triple longevity of Jamadagni, the triple longevity of Kaśyapa; that triple longevity which is among the gods—may that triple longevity be ours. With this [mantra], one should apply the ashes while reciting: “Fire is ash, wind is ash, water is ash, earth is ash, space is ash; indeed, all this is ash. These are the eyes of the mind.”

They become ashes. Then, having consecrated them seven times with the root mantra: "Īśāna" [Oṃ Īśānaḥ sarvavidyānām īśvaraḥ sarvabhūtānām | Brahmādhipatir brahmaṇo’dhipatir brahmā śivo me astu sadā śivom || 38 || 8].
Having placed ashes on the head, [one should recite]: "To Tatpuruṣa... [Oṃ tatpuruṣāya vidmahe | mahādevāya dhīmahi | tanno rudraḥ pracodayāt || 38 | 7 ||] ...on the face, [and recite]: "To Aghora...
[Oṃ aghorebhyo'tha ghorebhyo ghoraghoratarebhyaḥ | sarvebhyaḥ sarvaśarvebhyo namaste].

"Be unto those who have the form of Rudra" (38.6); thus at the heart, for Vāmadeva: "Oṃ, salutation to Vāmadeva, salutation to the Eldest, salutation to the Best, salutation to Rudra, salutation to Time, salutation to the Maker of Parts, salutation to the Maker of Strength" (38.4); thus at the secret place, for Sadyojāta.

"Oṃ, I take refuge in Sadyojāta; salutations, salutations indeed to Sadyojāta! In every existence, in non-existence, and beyond existence—O Bhava, protect me! Salutations to the source of existence! (38.3). With this mantra, one applies it to the feet.
Again, having placed ashes on the head with the root-vidyā, one applies them to the mouth with the root-mantra, to the chest with the root-mantra, and to the thighs with the root-mantra.
One should bathe with the root mantra on the shanks, with the root mantra on the feet, and with the root mantra on all the joints.
Having rubbed [the area] with the thumb and drawn a triangle with the little finger,
and having written the seed-syllable of Bhuvaneśvarī in its center, one should consecrate it seven times with the root mantra using the thumb.

Having circumambulated [the head], one should say "Oṃ, obeisance to the Blazing Fierce One" (oṃ dīptacaṇḍāya namaḥ) and draw a line across the middle of the forehead with the middle and ring fingers; thus,
the Blessed Brahmā resides in the forehead and Havyavāhana (Fire) in the heart.
Pūṣan is at the navel, the shoulders, and the throat;
Rudra and Āditya are in the left and right arms; likewise, Prabhañjana is in the middle of the wrists.
At the base of the left [arm] is Vāmadeva, and in the middle is he who has the luster of the moon;
the Vasus are at the wrist, and Hari is remembered to be at the back.
In the head is the Self, Mahādeva, the Supreme Self, Sadāśiva;
in all the limbs are the guardians of the directions, the Śaktis, the groups of Mothers, and so forth.
And may all the gods protect [you] during the sprinkling with the Vibhūti.
Now, the characteristics of the Tripuṇḍra: If it be circular, there will be disease; if it be too long, there is a loss of ascetic merit.
A wise man should wear the Tripuṇḍra with a measurement equal to the width of two eyes.
Having understood this, one should perform the ash-bath (bhasmasnāna) according to the prescribed rule;
or alternatively, one may apply it to all limbs using only the root-mantra (mūlavidyā).
Thus ends the procedure for the bath and wearing of the *vibhūti*.

Now, the procedure for the twilight rites (*sandhyā*) is described. Having first performed the Vedic twilight rite as prescribed in one's own *śākhā*, one should commence the Mantra-twilight rite. It is as follows: *Oṃ hrīṃ, I purify the principle of the self; obeisance.*

Svāhā! Oṃ hrīṃ, I purify the principle of knowledge (vidyā-tattva), obeisance, svāhā! Oṃ hrīṃ, I purify the principle of Śiva (śiva-tattva), obeisance, svāhā! Having thus performed the sipping of water (ācamana), having wiped [the mouth] three times and touched once the two nostrils, the two eyes, and the head.
One should touch the heart and the right ear; this is the manner of sipping water (ācamana).
One should perform breath control (*prāṇāyāma*) with the root mantra. Then, one should perform the six-limbed ritual (*ṣaḍaṅga*), namely the assignment of the five limbs (*aṅgapañcaka-nyāsa*):
*oṃ hrāṃ hṛdayāya namaḥ* [to the thumbs] *namaḥ*; *oṃ hrīṃ śirase svāhā* [to the index fingers] *namaḥ*; *oṃ hrūṃ śikhāyai vaṣaṭ* [to the middle fingers] *namaḥ*; *oṃ hraiṃ*...

*Kavacāya hūṃ*—*namaḥ* to the two ring fingers; *Oṃ hrauṃ netratrayāya vauṣaṭ*—*namaḥ* to the two little fingers; *Oṃ hraḥ astrāya phaṭ*—*namaḥ* to the palms and backs of the hands. Thus is the six-limbed ritual (*ṣaḍaṅga*). Now follows the assignment of the five limbs (*aṅgapañcakanyāsa*): *Oṃ hrīṃ hṛllekhāyai namaḥ* on the head.

Having performed the ritual placement (*vinyāsa*) thus: *Oṃ hraṃ* to Gaganā, salutation to the mouth; *Oṃ hraiṃ* to Raktā, salutation to the heart; *Oṃ hrauṃ* to Karālikā, salutation to the secret place; *Oṃ hraḥ* to Mahocchuṣmā, salutation to the two feet. Then, [placing] *Oṃ hrīṃ* to Śiva, salutation to the right hand; *Oṃ hrāṃ* to Śakti, salutation to the left hand. Then, in the water...
Having fashioned a triangular and hexagonal *yantra*, one should draw the sacred water (*tīrtha*) from the solar orb with the *aṅkuśa-mudrā* while reciting "Aiṃ,
obeisance to the heart," and having cast it into the vessel, one should display the seven mudrās beginning with the invocation (*āvāhana*) as previously described, and then summon the sacred waters.
O Gaṅgā, Yamunā, Godāvarī, Sarasvatī, Narmadā, Sindhu, and Kāverī! Be present in these waters.

Then, having taken water in the palm of the right hand and covered it with the left hand, one should empower it seven times with the root mantra; then, taking that water in the left hand, [one sprinkles] with the water dripping from the joints of the fingers.

Having cleansed one's own head with the ten syllables beginning with *ya*— namely *yaṃ raṃ laṃ vaṃ śaṃ ṣaṃ saṃ haṃ laṃ kṣaṃ*— together with the root-mantra (*mūlavidyā*), and having discarded that water, one takes up fresh water as before and [cleanses] with the *sparśa* consonants from *ka* to *ma* (*kaṃ khaṃ gaṃ ghaṃ ṅaṃ caṃ*...).
Having drunk water accompanied by the root mantra (*mūlavidyā*)— namely *chaṃ jaṃ jhaṃ ñaṃ ṭaṃ ṭhaṃ ḍaṃ ḍhaṃ ṇaṃ taṃ thaṃ daṃ dhaṃ naṃ paṃ phaṃ baṃ bhaṃ maṃ*— and having taken other water as before,
[one should consecrate it] with the sixteen vowels together with the bindu (*aṃ āṃ iṃ īṃ uṃ ūṃ ṛṃ ṝṃ*).

Having again purified one's own head with the syllables *ḷṃ ḹṃ eṃ aiṃ oṃ auṃ aṃ aḥ* together with the root-mantra (*mūlavidyā*), one should take that water in the right hand; then, by means of the root-mantra, having drawn the water through the left nostril (*iḍā*)— the channel flowing toward the lunar orb— using the practice of inhalation (*pūraka*), one should wash the internal channels.

Having entered through that [nostril], one should expel the wave of darkness, which has the luster of collyrium, along with the personification of sin (*pāpapuruṣa*) through the right nostril— the *piṅgalā* channel carrying the solar orb— by means of the practice of exhalation (*recaka*),
using the weapon-mantra *ślīṃ paśu huṃ phaṭ* while forming a circle with the hand on the left side.
Or he may strike it against the ground. Then, rising up, he should offer three *arghyas*. As follows:
*Aiṃ kāmeśvarīṃ vidmahe hrīṃ bhuvaneśvarīṃ dhīmahi tannaḥ śaktiḥ pracodayāt*.
"To the venerable Bhuvaneśvarī, who dwells within the rising sun, I offer this *arghya*; obeisance."

Having thus offered the three *arghya* oblations, one should satiate the *Gāyatrī* mantra as many times as possible according to one's capacity. Again, having performed the ritual sipping of water (*ācamana*) as before, one should perform three breath-controls (*prāṇāyāma*) with the root mantra, execute the ritual placement (*nyāsa*) as previously described, and meditate upon the *Gāyatrī*.
Then, while reciting [the mantra], one should contemplate the Great Goddess (*Maheśānī*), radiant as saffron, within the *ādhāra*.
At midday, one should contemplate her, resembling the moon, within the lotus of the heart.
And one should meditate upon Him in the center of the head, possessing the splendor of the dark Tamāla tree.

Having meditated thus and having recited the previously mentioned Gāyatrī one hundred and eight times, and having again performed the six-limbed placement (*ṣaḍaṅganyāsa*) and meditation, one should offer the recitation with the mantra "guhyātiguhyam" to the deity who pervades the six paths (*ṣaḍadhvan*). In this manner, at each of the three times of day mentioned, one should perform the rites beginning with sprinkling (*mārjana*) and ending with the water offering (*arghya*). Then:

After the morning twilight ritual (saṃdhyā), one should perform the worship of the Sun (saurapūjā). It is as follows: having drawn a square mandala on the ground with cow dung, and having fashioned an eight-petaled lotus there with red sandalwood paste, one should install the Lord of the Day (the Sun) in the center together with the *māyā* seed-syllable (*hrīṃ*), and having installed Soma and the other deities upon the petals, one should worship them.

Namely: *hrīṃ* salutation to Sūrya in the center; on the petals: *hrīṃ* salutation to Soma, *hrīṃ* salutation to Bhauma, *hrīṃ* salutation to Budha, *hrīṃ* salutation to Guru, *hrīṃ* salutation to Bhārgava, *hrīṃ* salutation to Mandā, *hrīṃ* salutation to Rāhu, and *hrīṃ* salutation to Ketu.

Having worshipped and placed sandalwood, unbroken rice grains, and flowers into the *arghya* vessel, and having performed the six-limbed ritual (*ṣaḍaṅga*) with the *māyā* seed-syllable (*hrīṃ*) repeated six times, one should meditate upon the Lord of Day (the Sun).
He is marked with jewels, possesses ten million gold pieces, and is adorned with bracelets and other ornaments;
he is golden-hued, pot-bellied, crimson, and has two beautiful lotus-like hands.

Having meditated thus, one should offer three *arghya* oblations with the Sūrya mantra. Therein, the Sūrya mantra is: *oṃ hrīṃ haṃsaḥ sūryāya namaḥ*. Having offered these three *arghya*s, one should contemplate the Sun situated in the middle of the forehead in the form of a *bindu*. Having performed the worship of the Sun in this manner, one should perform the libation (*tarpaṇa*). It is as follows:

Having sat down near the water, washed one's feet and hands, and performed the ritual sipping (ācamana), one should visualize the *yantra* within the water; then, as before, drawing the sacred water (*tīrtha*) from the solar orb with the *aṅkuśa-mudrā*, one should display the mudrās for invocation and so forth, and perform the six-limbed ritual (*ṣaḍaṅga*) with the root mantra.
Having performed [the ritual], one should offer libations: *oṃ hrīṃ śivaḥ tṛpyatu*; *oṃ hrīṃ pīṭhādhikāriṇyaḥ devatāḥ tṛpyantu*; *oṃ hrīṃ guravaḥ pūrvācāryāḥ tṛpyantu*;
*oṃ hrīṃ śaktayaḥ tṛpyantu*; *oṃ hrīṃ paramamarīcayaḥ tṛpyantu*; *oṃ hrīṃ*.
May the deities pervading the six paths be satisfied. Oṃ hrīṃ! May the Lords of Obstacles (Vighneśvaras) be satisfied.
Oṃ hrīṃ! May the Lords of Mantras (Mantreśvaras) be satisfied. Oṃ hrīṃ! May the deity of the seven streams (Saptasrotā Deva) be satisfied.
Oṃ hrīṃ! May Brahmā, Viṣṇu, and Rudra be satisfied. Oṃ hrīṃ! May the World-Protectors (Lokapālas) be satisfied. Oṃ hrīṃ!
"May the planets be satisfied: Oṃ Hrīṃ! May the Siddhas be satisfied: Oṃ Hrīṃ! May those who hold authority over heaven be satisfied: Oṃ Hrīṃ!

And may those who hold authority over the sacred seats (pīṭha) and the medicinal herbs be satisfied: Oṃ Hrīṃ! Thus, with the *devatīrtha* [finger-position], one should satisfy the gods with water poured toward the east, and the humans from the middle.

"One should offer handfuls of water to the ancestors with the tips [of the grass] pointing south," so it is said in the *Agnipurāṇa*. Now, for the libation to the sages (*ṛṣitarpaṇa*): "May the father-in-law, the great father-in-law, and the elder father-in-law be satisfied; Oṃ Hrīṃ! May the Siddhas who preside over the four seats (*catuṣpīṭha*) be satisfied;
Oṃ Hrīṃ! May the deities who preside over the seats (*pīṭha*) be satisfied; Oṃ Hrīṃ! May the Gurus [be satisfied]."
"May the former teachers be satisfied; Oṃ Hrīṃ, may those presiding over the sacred seats (pīṭhas) be satisfied;

Oṃ Hrīṃ, may the medicinal herbs be satisfied"—thus, with the *manuṣyatīrtha* [the place between the index finger and the thumb, according to Amara], "Oṃ Hrīṃ, may the father, grandfather, and great-grandfather be satisfied; Oṃ Hrīṃ."

"May those born of the paternal lineage be satisfied; oṃ hrīṃ, may the maternal grandfather, the great maternal grandfather, and the great-great maternal grandfather be satisfied; oṃ hrīṃ, may those born of the maternal lineage be satisfied; oṃ hrīṃ, may those born of the father-in-law's lineage be satisfied"—thus [one offers] with the *pitṛtīrtha* (the thumb-root).

[The Pitṛ-tīrtha: Between the thumb and the forefinger is the supreme tīrtha for the ancestors (Kūrma Purāṇa). One may perform it with a single utterance or according to the requirements of the rite; there is no fault in following the path established by all people. Oṃ hrīṃ, the rays preceded by Śiva and Śakti, the deities dwelling in the six paths (ṣaḍadhvan).

"May the Vidyās, the Vidyēśvaras, the Mantras, the Mantreśvaras, Brahmā and the other world-protectors, the Mothers, the fierce Siddhas, and the medicinal herbs be satisfied"—thus with the *devatātīrtha*. "Oṃ Hrīṃ! May those who hold authority over the sacred seats (*pīṭha*), the Siddhas, the Bhūcarīs, the Gurus, and the former teachers be satisfied"—thus with the *manuṣyatīrtha*. Oṃ Hrīṃ.

"May those born in the lineages of my father, grandfather, great-grandfather, maternal grandfather, maternal great-grandfather, maternal great-great-grandfather, mother’s father, mother’s grandfather, mother’s great-grandfather, mother-in-law,
and father-in-law be satisfied"— with these words, he offers with the *pitṛ-tīrtha*. Then, [he offers] for his own paternal lineage beginning with the father.
One should satisfy [the deities]. Then, one should drink water with the root seed-syllable accompanied by the four limbs [with the mantras ending in the words "I purify" (*śodhayāmi*)].
This twenty-fourfold sipping of water (*ācamana*) is the purifier of the principles (*tattva*) of the body.
Having performed that, O Great Goddess, one should perform the libation with the root mantra.
First, having gratified the sacred seats (pīṭhas), one should then invoke the Goddess and gratify her;
having gratified the Goddess three times, one should then worship the surrounding retinue (āvaraṇa).
In the past, all mantras were proclaimed by Kamalā in the form of speech.
At the end of the root mantra with three *tāra*s, one should then utter the word *Bhuvaneśvarī* (or *Bhuvaneśī*),
followed by *namaḥ*, *śrīpādukā*, and finally *tarpayāmi*.
By means of this sequential method, one should perform the libation (*tarpaṇa*) upon the enclosure (*āvaraṇa*) in due order.

Namely: *Aiṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Oṃ Hrīṃ Bhuvaneśvaryambāyai Namaḥ*, "I satisfy the venerable sandals" (*śrīpādukāṃ tarpayāmi*)—having thus satisfied her three times; then, for the deities of the seat (*pīṭhadevatā*) and the deities of the enclosure (*āvaraṇadevatā*), one should offer libations with a single handful (*añjali*) for each, using the formula: "The three stars (*tritāraṃ*): *Namaḥ śrīpādukāṃ tarpayāmi*. In that regard:
We shall describe the deities of the seats and the enclosures later on.
At the conclusion of the libation, the lord of practitioners, having offered the five types of worship,
should then, becoming composed, perform recitation (japa) according to the number of libations.
Having rendered [the deity] partless, having respectfully dismissed the Goddess from the heart,
and having reconstituted [the self], one should withdraw [the deity] into the solar orb of the sacred site (tīrtha).
Having performed the recitation of the hymn, he should then proceed to the sacrificial hall;
without speaking in ordinary external speech, he should neither touch nor look [at anything profane].

Thus ends the commentary, beginning from the morning rites and ending with the libations (*tarpaṇa*), in the *Bhuvaneśvarīkramacandrikā* composed by Anantadeva— who resides in Mātṛpura and belongs to the tradition of Śrī Dāyīdeva— based upon the *Śāradātilaka* and various Tantric doctrines, according to the manual (*paddhati*) of Pṛthvīdharācārya.
The First Chapter. Śrī.

Having sipped water (ācamana) and performed breath control (prāṇāyāma), having proclaimed the place and time, and having made the formal resolve (saṃkalpa): "For the sake of removing all my defects and for the sake of attaining the grace of Bhuvaneśvarī, I shall perform the purification of the elements (bhūtaśuddhi) and the other ritual placements (nyāsas)," [one proceeds].
Therein, first is the rule regarding the seat (āsananiyama):
For one who knows mantras, a rite performed on a *vināsana* does not succeed;
the attainment of knowledge occurs on a black antelope skin, while the attainment of austerity occurs on a seat of *kuśa* grass.
On a seat of earth there is loss of fame; on a seat of leaves, confusion of mind;
on a seat of grass, there will be no success; a seat of reeds bestows renown.
Without a white sheepskin there is peace; on stone there is indeed disease;
on a tiger skin there shall be liberation; and on a wooden seat there is misfortune.
There would be a loss of strength with a bamboo mat; all purposes are fulfilled with a variegated woolen blanket.
For rites such as malevolent magic (*abhicāra*), a black one is used; and there is loss of sight through sleepiness.
A great loss of divine power always occurs through yawning;
with a flickering mind, one never attains success quickly.
Thus end the postures. Now, in an auspicious and pure place, having meditated upon the *mātṛkā*-lotus—

whose pericarp is the seed-syllable *aiṃ*, whose filaments are the pairs of vowels, whose petals in the cardinal directions are the eight consonant groups *ka, ca, ṭa, ta, pa, ya, śa,* and *la*, which is endowed with the seed-syllable *vaṃ* in the intermediate directions, and adorned with the seed-syllable *ṭhaṃ* in the corners— [one should recite] *aiṃ hrīṃ*.

Having worshipped with flowers, unbroken rice grains (*akṣata*), and other offerings, saying "Śrīṃ, obeisance to the lotus-seat of the foundational power (*ādhāraśakti*"), one should sit facing either east or north and pray to the earth:
"Pṛthivī, Merupṛṣṭha, Kūrma, Sutala— these are the seer (*ṛṣi*), deity (*devatā*), and meter (*chandaḥ*) for the prayer to the earth."
The application (viniyoga):
O Earth! By you the worlds are supported; O Goddess, you are supported by Viṣṇu.
Therefore, O Goddess, support me and make this seat pure.
Thus, having visualized the lotus of the Mātṛkās upon one’s own head by means of the *mṛgīmudrā*, one should worship Dīpanātha.
It is as follows:
having uttered the first syllable of the field (*kṣetra*), [one should offer] to Khaḍgīśa, whose nature is the *meda* [tissue], in such-and-such a field.

Having worshipped Dīpanātha with flowers, unbroken rice, and other offerings, [reciting]: "To Varṇeśānandanātha, who is of intensely red complexion and is joined by twelve red Śaktis; accept, accept this worship in this sacred field, svāhā!"
O you with sharp fangs! O you of massive body, resembling the fire at the end of an aeon!
Homage to you, Bhairava; you should grant me your permission.

Having thus received the command of Bhairava and formed a *añjali* with both hands holding flowers, [one should offer salutations]: *Aiṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ*, obeisance to the Gurus beginning with Śiva on the head (three times). *Gaṃ*, obeisance to Gaṇapati on the right shoulder (three times). *Vaṃ*, obeisance to Vaṭuka on the left shoulder (three times). *Duṃ*, obeisance to Durgā at the base of the right thigh (three times). *Kṣaṃ*...
"Salutation to Kṣetrapāla at the root of the left thigh"—thus one should place [the mantra] on the right and left sides, and above and below (p.
"By whom the entire moving and non-moving world is pervaded in the form of an unbroken circle..."
Salutation to that venerable Guru by whom that state has been revealed.
The foot is a sacred, far-reaching, ancient means by which, when purified, one overcomes evil deeds. Purified by that pure, sacred foot, may we cross over sin and the enemy.

Having recited the Guru’s sandals (*pādukā*) with such Vedic mantras as these, and having worshipped the venerable Guru-Nātha in the thousand-petaled lotus (*sahasrāravinda*) with the mantra: *aiṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ [Name]ānandanātha, joined with [Name]āmbā-Śakti, I worship your venerable sandals; obeisance!*, one should prostrate with the *yonimudrā*. Then, one should perform the expulsion of the elemental spirits (*bhūtotsāraṇa*).
May those beings depart who dwell upon the earth;
may those beings who create obstacles perish by the command of Śiva.
Having dispelled the obstacles with the Pāśupata weapon, *oṃ ślīṃ paśu huṃ phaṭ*, using the Nārāca mudrā,

one should drive away the obstacles residing in the netherworld, on earth, and in the sky, respectively, by striking the ground with the left heel, clapping the hands, and turning the face upward, while using the aforementioned Pāśupata weapon along with white mustard seeds, unbroken rice, and flowers.
Having wiped the palm of the left hand twice, starting from the wrist along with its back, using the right hand;
and having wiped the right hand once in the manner previously described— having thus performed the purification of the six parts of the hands—
one should [wipe] from the navel down to the feet, from the heart up to the navel, and from the head down to the heart.

Having pervaded [the space] with that very weapon-mantra, having performed three internal *tāla*-gestures and three external *tāla*-gestures, and having performed the binding of the ten directions, one should say: "Raṃ, obeisance to the fire-wall; Oṃ sahasrāra huṃ phaṭ svāhā. Having constructed two walls with the previously mentioned weapon-mantras and having performed the triple encirclement by fire, [one should proceed].
Having thus performed the protection, one should then perform the purification of the elements (*bhūtaśuddhi*). It is as follows:

having effected the purification of the channels (*nāḍīśuddhi*) by reciting the *praṇava* twelve times, one should raise the consciousness residing in the heart upward by means of the *haṃsaḥ* mantra and the *saṃghaṭṭamudrā*, and join it with the supreme light situated at the *dvādaśānta*.

Having performed protection with the Astra-mantra, one should purify the elements. For this Earth-mantra, Brahmā is the Seer (ṛṣi), Gāyatrī is the Meter (chandas), and Soma is the Deity; its application (viniyoga) is for the recitation intended for the purification of the elements known as the Earth-element.
From the feet up to the knees is the locus of the Earth; there is the yellow-colored Earth-maṇḍala.
The earth element is square, marked with vajras, and has Brahmā as its presiding deity; it possesses five qualities.
Having purified it by means of the application of six *udghātas* and the seed-syllable *oṃ laṃ* (repeated sixty times), one should cause it to dissolve into water.
For the Varuṇa mantra, Gautama is the seer (*ṛṣi*), Varuṇa is the deity (*devatā*), and *triṣṭubh* is the meter (*chanda*).

The application (*viniyoga*) is for the recitation (*japa*) intended for the purification of the elements (*bhūtaśuddhi*) known as Varuṇa. From the knees up to the navel is the locus of water, the white Varuṇa-maṇḍala, bow-shaped and marked with white lotuses at both ends; in its center is the seed-syllable *vaṃ*, white in color, having Viṣṇu as its presiding deity. By means of that—
I dry up the fourfold qualities of water by means of five *udghāta* applications. With the seed-syllable *oṃ vaṃ* (repeated 48 times), one should lead it to dissolution into fire.

For the Āgneya mantra, Kaśyapa is the seer (ṛṣi), Agni is the deity, Triṣṭubh is the meter, and its application (viniyoga) is for the recitation intended for the purification of the elements known as Āgneya. The locus of fire extends from the navel to the heart; therein is the circle of fire, triangular in shape and marked with svastikas at its three corners.

In its center is the seed-syllable *raṃ*, red in color, having Rudra as its presiding deity. By means of that, the three-fold fire, through the application of three blows, I dry up [the body]. *Oṃ raṃ* (repeated thirty-six times)—thus one should lead it to dissolution into the wind.
For the mantra of the wind, Kiṣkaṇdha is the seer (*ṛṣi*), Vāyu is the deity, and Triṣṭubh is the meter.

The application [of the mantra] is for the purpose of the purification of the elements (bhūtaśuddhi) as explained in the Vāyavya[-tantra]. The region of the wind extends from the heart up to the middle of the eyebrows. Therein is the wind-mandala, hexagonal in shape and marked with six dots;
in its center is the seed-syllable *yaṃ*, blue in color, having Saṅkarṣaṇa as its presiding deity, and consisting of three qualities (*triguṇa*).
"By means of the practice of double exhalation, I dry up the wind; *oṃ yaṃ* [twenty-four times]—thus one should lead it to dissolution into space (*ākāśa*).

For the mantra of space, Brahmā is the seer (*ṛṣi*), the great space is the deity, the *triṣṭubh* is the meter; its application (*viniyoga*) is for recitation (*japa*) for the purpose of purifying the element called space. From the center of the eyebrows..."

The space-element extends as far as the aperture of Brahma (*brahmarandhra*); therein is the sphere of the sky (*nabhomandala*), circular in shape and marked with a banner. In its center is the seed-syllable *haṃ*, smoke-colored, having Sadāśiva as its presiding deity.
By means of that, I dry up the single quality of space through the practice of a single upward expulsion (*ekodghāta*). *Oṃ haṃ* (twelve times), by this seed-syllable, into the Supreme Śiva.
One should lead [the breath] to dissolution.
Beginning from the number sixty, one should discard twelve by twelve;
the elements, beginning with earth, [are dissolved] in order into their respective causes.
Having thus contemplated the five great elements as unified within the supreme reality (*tattva*), one should then dissolve the elements.
*Oṃ lhāṃ brahmaṇe pṛthivyadhipataye nivṛttikalātmane huṃ phaṭ svāhā*. Pervading from the feet up to the knees, one should purify the earth. *Oṃ hrīṃ viṣṇave abdhipataye*.
With "pratiṣṭhākalātmane huṃ phaṭ svāhā," one should purify the water by pervading the area from the knees up to the navel.

With "oṃ hraṃ agnaye tejo'dhipataye vidyākalātmane huṃ phaṭ svāhā," one should purify the fire by pervading the area from the navel up to the chest. [With] "oṃ hyaiṃ īśvarāya... [one should purify the self].

*Vāyvadhipataye śāntikalātmane huṃ phaṭ svāhā*. Having pervaded from the heart up to the two eyebrows, one should purify the wind. *Oṃ hauṃ sadāśivāya vyomādhipataye śāntyatītakalātmane huṃ phaṭ svāhā*. Having pervaded from the eyebrows up to the aperture of Brahmā (*brahmarandhra*).

One should purify the space. Having thus performed the pervasion and bound the *yonimudrā*, one should raise the *kulakuṇḍalinī*, pierce the six lotuses, and unite her—whose form is the oil of the lamp of the individual soul—with the supreme light; then, according to the sequence to be described, one should perform the rites of drying and so forth.
Therein, first, one should meditate on the Person of Sin (pāpapuruṣa) in the left side of the belly:
having the murder of a Brahmin as its head, the theft of gold as its two arms,
the drinking of liquor joined with its heart, and the violation of the Guru’s bed as its two hips.

One should contemplate the sin within one's belly as black in color, possessing hair in the form of minor offenses (*upapātaka*), taking refuge in the limbs of major sins (*pātaka*), and bearing a sword and shield.

Having visualized the *pāpapuruṣa* (personification of sin) within the belly in this sequence and so forth, one should perform the drying out and other purifications of the body together with that [sin]. For example:
in the left nostril, there is a wind mandala joined with its seed-syllable *yaṃ*, [surrounded] by the consonants from *ka* to *ma*, excluding the sibilants (*sparśavarṇa*).
Having meditated upon the smoke-colored [deity] who has been served, and having filled [the breath] with sixteen measures (mātrās),

one should unite it with the prāṇa and apāna winds; then, together with the wind arising from that, one should thoroughly dry up the great sins and diseases of the body through thirty-two measures (32) of retention (kumbhaka), and [retain] for sixteen [measures].

Then follows the exhaling (*recaka*) and the burning. Having meditated upon the fire-mandala in the right nostril, conjoined with its seed-syllable and attended by the ten [vowels] beginning with *yā*, and having united it with the *prāṇa* and *apāna* winds, one should [burn away] the great sins of the body along with the fire arising therefrom.
Having incinerated [the body] along with the diseases as before, one performs the *kumbhaka* and *recaka*. Then follows the immersion (*plāvana*).

Having visualized in the left nostril the watery mandala, conjoined with its seed-syllable, white, bow-shaped, and attended by the sixteen vowels (16), one fills [it] as before with the wind residing in the *ādhāra*.
Having raised the fire-kuṇḍalinī, [the body] is flooded by its mass of flames;

then, as before, one performs inhalation (pūraka), retention (kumbhaka), and exhalation (recaka) while being flooded by the nectar from the lunar orb at the aperture of Brahmā (brahmarandhra). Having thus performed drying, burning, and flooding, [one proceeds] to the Supreme.

Having meditated upon one's own body as a bubble-like form reflected within the Śāmbhava Brahman, and having made it solid by means of the seed-syllable *laṃ* (earth), one should pierce it with the seed-syllable *haṃ* (space) and contemplate the evolution of the elements:
from the Imperishable comes space; from space, air; from herbs, food; from food, semen; and from semen, the person (*puruṣa*).

Having thus contemplated the sequence of emanation: *oṃ haṃ 12 oṃ hauṃ sadāśivāya vyomādhipataye śāntyatītakalātmane huṃ phaṭ svāhā*—this pervades from the aperture of Brahmā (*brahmarandhra*) down to the middle of the eyebrows.
*yaṃ 24 oṃ hraiṃ īśvarāya vāyvadhipataye śāntikalātmane huṃ phaṭ*.
*Svāhā*—pervading from the center of the eyebrows to the heart: *raṃ 36*. *Oṃ hraṃ agnaye tejo'dhipataye vidyākalātmane huṃ phaṭ svāhā*—pervading from the heart to the navel:
*vaṃ 48*. *Oṃ hvīṃ viṣṇave abdhipataye pratiṣṭhākalātmane huṃ phaṭ svāhā*.
Pervading from the navel down to the knees: *laṃ* (60) *oṃ hlāṃ brahmaṇe pṛthivyadhipataye nivṛttikalātmane huṃ phaṭ svāhā*. Pervading from the knees down to the feet;
thus, beginning with the number twelve and increasing up to sixty, while reciting "so 'ham" in sequence.
One should meditate upon the individual soul (jīva), whose nature consists of the thirty-six principles (tattvas), as being Śiva himself within the heart-lotus. Then,

having recited the Māyā-mantra twenty-one times, one should establish the vital breaths (prāṇas) from the *mūlādhāra* to the end of the *brahmarandhra* by means of the *prāṇapratiṣṭhā* mantra, using the index finger in the shape of a hook.
121) Now, one should perform the *prāṇapratiṣṭhā* (the ritual installation of the vital breath) according to the method that will be described, as follows:
for the *prāṇapratiṣṭhā* mantra, Brahmā, Viṣṇu, and Śiva are the seers (*ṛṣi*s); they are on the head. The *Ṛg*, *Yajur*, and *Sāma* Vedas are [the meters].

The *chandās* (Vedic meters) are in the mouth; the deity Prāṇa-śakti is in the heart. The application (*viniyoga*) is for the installation of the vital breath (*prāṇapratiṣṭhāpana*) at the end of the twelve finger-breadths (*dvādaśānta*). *Aṃ kaṃ khaṃ gaṃ ghaṃ ṅaṃ 5 āṃ*, to the heart which is the self of earth, water, fire, air, and ether: *namaḥ*. To the two thumbs: *namaḥ*.

Iṃ caṃ chaṃ jaṃ jhaṃ ñaṃ 5; to the head, svāhā, which has sound, touch, form, taste, and smell as its essence. Salutation with the two index fingers (tarjanī). Uṃ ṭaṃ ṭhaṃ ḍaṃ ḍhaṃ ṇaṃ 5; to the tuft (śikhā), vaṣaṭ, which has the ear, skin, eye, tongue, and nose as its essence. Salutation with the two middle fingers (madhyamā).
Eṃ taṃ thaṃ daṃ dhaṃ naṃ 5 Aiṃ: to the armor (kavaca) at the locations of speech, hands, feet, and genitals, Huṃ!
To the two ring fingers, Namaḥ! Oṃ paṃ phaṃ baṃ bhaṃ maṃ 5 Auṃ:
to the three eyes whose essence is speech, grasping, movement, excretion, and pleasure, Vauṣaṭ! To the two little fingers.

*Namaḥ*. Aṃ yaṃ raṃ laṃ vaṃ śaṃ ṣaṃ saṃ haṃ kṣaṃ aḥ. To the Self consisting of mind, intellect, ego, and consciousness (*manobuddhyahaṃkāracittātmane*)—[according to the reading in the *Āhnikakarmasūtrāvali*, "to the Self consisting of consciousness and cognition" (*cittavijñānātmane*)]. *Astrāya phaṭ*. [This is for] the palms and the backs of the hands. *Yaṃ*.

Salutation to the self of the skin; raṃ, salutation to the self of the blood; laṃ, salutation to the self of the flesh; vaṃ, salutation to the self of the fat; śaṃ, salutation to the self of the bone; ṣaṃ, salutation to the self of the marrow; saṃ, salutation to the self of the semen. Having performed the threefold pervasive [protection] with the three seed-syllables: oṃ, āṃ, hrīṃ, kroṃ.
Then the visualization (*dyāna*):

She is seated upon a radiant, deep-red lotus arising from a red ocean and supported by a boat; with her lotus-like hands, she holds a noose, a bow made of sugarcane, its string, a goad, and five arrows.

"Bearing a skull filled with blood, resembling the three-eyed [Śiva], enriched by full breasts, the Goddess, possessing the color of the rising sun— may the Supreme Power of Life (Prāṇaśakti) be the bestower of happiness upon us.
Thus is the meditation.
Placing the hand upon the heart, one should recite the mantra: *Āṃ hrīṃ kroṃ yaṃ raṃ laṃ vaṃ śaṃ ṣaṃ saṃ hoṃ*.

By my breath, may the breaths of the venerable Bhuvaneśvarī be here as breaths. 11. Together with my life-force (*jīva*), may the life-force of the venerable Bhuvaneśvarī abide here. 11. Together with all my senses, [may those of] the venerable Bhuvaneśvarī...

"May all the senses—speech, mind, skin, eyes, ears, tongue, nose, and breath—come here and remain happily for a long time; svāhā! This is the ritual for the installation of the vital breaths (*prāṇapratiṣṭhāvidhi*).
Now follows the sequence for the placement of the *mātṛkā* letters (*mātṛkānyāsakrama*).
Two finger-breadths above the anus, reaching the root-aperture of the *suṣumṇā*,
is a lotus of golden luster, shining with the fire of the four Vedas.
One should lead the extremely subtle streak of light, shaped like a flash of lightning and residing therein,
upward through the piercing of the six chakras, as the Kulakuṇḍalinī.

Having meditated upon the previously mentioned lotus of the Mātṛkās, situated in the center of the tree at the *dvādaśānta* and resembling fresh butter, [one should contemplate it] quickly illuminated by the luster of Kuṇḍalinī.
Having drawn forth the vital energy (tejas) into the hollowed palms, one should perform the ritual placement of the phonemes (mātṛkā-nyāsa).

One should place the six vowels—*aṃ*, *āṃ*, *i*, *īṃ*, *u*, *ūṃ*—on the palms and backs of the right and left hands, respectively, in the order of their pervasion. One should place the remaining ten vowels on the ten fingers, beginning with the thumbs and ending with the little fingers.
Then, starting from the right index finger and ending with the left little finger, one should place them on the tips of the first three [fingers] of each hand.
One should place four letters each from *ka* to *sa* on the two thumbs as the *halas*, and the final letter (*ha*) on the tips of the fingers. Then follows the six-limbed mantra of the script:
*aṃ kaṃ khaṃ gaṃ ghaṃ ṅaṃ 5 āṃ hṛdayāya namaḥ aṅguṣṭhābhyāṃ namaḥ*.

Iṃ caṃ chaṃ jaṃ jhaṃ ñaṃ 5, *īṃ* to the head, svāhā; to the two index fingers, *namaḥ*. Uṃ ṭaṃ ṭhaṃ ḍaṃ ḍhaṃ ṇaṃ 5, *ūṃ* to the crest-lock (*śikhā*), vaṣaṭ; to the two middle fingers, *namaḥ*. Eṃ taṃ thaṃ daṃ dhaṃ naṃ 5, *aiṃ* to the armor (*kavaca*), hūṃ; to the two ring fingers, *namaḥ*. Oṃ paṃ phaṃ... [and so forth].
Baṃ Bhaṃ Maṃ 5 Oṃ to the three eyes, Vauṣaṭ; to the two little fingers, Namaḥ. Aṃ Yaṃ Raṃ Laṃ Vaṃ Śaṃ Ṣaṃ Saṃ Haṃ Kṣaṃ 10 Aḥ to the weapon, Phaṭ; to the palms and backs of the hands, Namaḥ.

For this *śuddhabinduvisargamātṛkā*: Brahmā is the *ṛṣi*, located on the head; the goddess Gāyatrī is the *chandas*, located in the mouth; Śrī Mātṛkā Sarasvatī is the deity, located in the heart; the consonants are the *bījas*, located in the secret place; the vowels are the *śaktis*, located in the feet. This is the application (*viniyoga*) for the ritual placement (*nyāsa*) of the *śuddhabinduvisargamātṛkā*.
*Hsauṃ aṃ āṃ śauṃ*. Thus, one should extend the *mātṛkā* [mantra] three times. Regarding the ritual placement (*nyāsa*) therein, there is this verse:
"In the forest [forehead], the circle [face], the two eyes, the two ears, the cheeks, the lips, the roots of the teeth, the head, and the mouth;
in the joints of the arms and feet, at their tips, on the two sides, and on the back, the navel, and the belly."

One should then sequentially assign the syllables known as the "pervasive" (vyāpaka) to the heart, the base of the arms, the back, the throat, and the armpits; to the heart and so forth, the pair of hands and feet; and to the belly and the face.

Therein is the ritual placement (*nyāsa*): *Oṃ a*, salutation to the head; *Oṃ ā*, salutation to the face; *Oṃ i*, salutation to the right eye; *Oṃ ī*, salutation to the left eye; *Oṃ u*, salutation to the right ear; *Oṃ ū*, salutation to the left ear; *Oṃ ṛ*, salutation to the right nostril; *Oṃ ṝ*, salutation to the left nostril; *Oṃ ḷ*, salutation to the right cheek.

Oṃ Ḷ, homage to the left cheek. Oṃ E, homage to the upper lip. Oṃ Ai, homage to the lower lip. Oṃ O, homage to the upper row of teeth. Oṃ Au, homage to the lower row of teeth. Oṃ Aṃ, homage to the root of the tongue. Oṃ Aḥ, homage to the tip of the tongue. Oṃ Ka, homage to the base of the right hand. Oṃ Kha, homage to...

At the elbow of the right hand: Oṃ Ga, homage to the wrist of the right hand. (p. 123) Oṃ Gha, homage to the base of the fingers of the right hand. Oṃ Ṅa, homage to the tips of the fingers of the right hand. Oṃ Ca.

Namo at the base of the left hand. Oṃ cha, namo at the left elbow. Oṃ ja, namo at the wrist of the left hand. Oṃ jha, namo at the base of the fingers of the left hand. Oṃ ña, namo at the tips of the fingers of the left hand.
Oṃ ṭa, namo at the base of the right foot. Oṃ ṭha, namo...

At the right knee: Oṃ ḍa namo. At the right ankle: Oṃ ḍha namo. At the base of the toes of the right foot: Oṃ ṇa namo. At the tips of the toes of the right foot: Oṃ ta namo. At the base of the left foot: Oṃ tha namo. At the left knee: Oṃ da namo. At the left ankle: Oṃ...

*Dha* namas to the base of the toes of the left foot; *Oṃ na* namas to the tips of the toes of the left foot; *Oṃ pa* namas to the right side; *Oṃ pha* namas to the left side; *Oṃ ba* namas to the back; *Oṃ bha* namas to the navel; *Oṃ ma* namas to the abdomen; *Oṃ ya* namas to the heart; *Oṃ ra* namas to the right shoulder; *Oṃ la* [namas to the left shoulder].

Namo on the left shoulder. Oṃ va namo on the throat. Oṃ śa namo on the right armpit. Oṃ ṣa namo on the left armpit. Oṃ sa namo from the heart to the pair of hands. Oṃ ha namo from the heart to the pair of feet. Oṃ la namo from the belly to the mouth. [This is] the pervasive [mantra]. Oṃ kṣa namo from the head to the end of the feet. [This is] the pervasive [mantra].

Again, in that very same place, one should perform the placement of the *bindu-mātṛkā* in sequence: *oṃ aṃ namaḥ* on the head; *oṃ āṃ namaḥ* on the face-circle, and so forth. Again, in that very same place, one should perform the placement of the *visarga-mātṛkā* using the combination of the thumb and ring finger in sequence: *oṃ aḥ namaḥ* on the head; *oṃ āḥ namaḥ* on the face-circle, and so forth.
Now, as for meditation:
[one should meditate upon her] who resembles ten million moons released from the sun, whose full and lofty breasts are swelling,
whose head is adorned with the crescent moon, and whose three eyes are rolling with the intoxication of honey.

I take refuge in Vāgīśvarī, the primordial goddess, who holds in her hands a choice rosary, a trident, and a skull-cup; she is eternally youthful and proud of her youth, her body adorned with sacred marks.

Thus is meditation. Thus, the sequence of the placement (*nyāsa*) of the *mātṛkā* consisting of the pure *bindu*, the *visarga*, and the [vowels] is threefold. Now follows the sequence for the internal (*antara*) *mātṛkā* placement: for this venerable internal *mātṛkā* placement, Brahmā is the seer (*ṛṣi*), located on the head; Gāyatrī is the meter (*chandas*), located in the mouth; the goddess Sarasvatī, who is the internal *mātṛkā*, is the deity, located in the heart; the consonants (*hal*)...
The seed-syllables are in the secret place; the vowels are the Śaktis in the two feet; *kṣaḥ* is the *kīlaka* at the navel. This is the application (*viniyoga*) for the internal *mātṛkā*-placement.
Now, the six limbs (*ṣaḍaṅga*): *Oṃ hrīṃ aṃ kaṃ 5 āṃ*, salutation to the heart on the two thumbs. *Oṃ*... [and so forth].

Oṃ hrīṃ iṃ caṃ 5 īṃ śirase svāhā—on the two index fingers. Oṃ hrīṃ uṃ ṭaṃ 5 ūṃ śikhāyai vaṣaṭ—on the two middle fingers. Oṃ hrīṃ eṃ taṃ 5 aiṃ kavacāya huṃ—on the two ring fingers. Oṃ hrīṃ oṃ paṃ 5 auṃ netratrayāya vauṣaṭ—on the two little fingers. Oṃ hrīṃ aṃ yaṃ 9 aḥ astrāya—on the palms and backs of the hands.
*Phaṭ* is for the palms and the backs of the hands. The visualization (*dhyāna*):
She has the luster of the *bandhūka* flower, possesses three eyes, and wears red garments that shine upon her broad hips.
She is burdened by the weight of her full, high, and swelling breasts and hips, and is established in the fullness of youth.

I bow to that Goddess Mātṛkā, who is adorned with divine ornaments, whose eyes are like lotuses, whose head bears the reflection of the moon, and who holds a noose and a goad while extending the gestures of fearlessness and granting boons.

Thus is the meditation. Therein, for the sake of purification, having visualized a sixteen-petaled lotus facing upward, one should place [the syllables] upon those respective petals, starting from the east and proceeding clockwise, preceded by the seed-syllable: oṃ hrīṃ aṃ namaḥ; oṃ hrīṃ āṃ namaḥ;
oṃ hrīṃ iṃ namaḥ; oṃ hrīṃ īṃ namaḥ; oṃ hrīṃ uṃ namaḥ.

Oṃ hrīṃ ūṃ namaḥ | Oṃ hrīṃ ṛṃ namaḥ | Oṃ hrīṃ ṝṃ namaḥ | Oṃ hrīṃ ḷṃ namaḥ | Oṃ hrīṃ ḹṃ namaḥ | Oṃ hrīṃ eṃ namaḥ | Oṃ hrīṃ aiṃ namaḥ | Oṃ hrīṃ oṃ namaḥ | Oṃ hrīṃ auṃ namaḥ | Oṃ hrīṃ aṃ namaḥ | Oṃ hrīṃ aḥ |

*Namaḥ*. In this manner, one should place the sixteen vowels. Then, having meditated upon the *anāhata-cakra* as a twelve-petaled lotus, one should likewise place the letters beginning with *ka* and ending with *ṭha* in clockwise order: *Oṃ hrīṃ kaṃ namaḥ*; *Oṃ hrīṃ khaṃ namaḥ*; *Oṃ...*

Hrīṃ Gaṃ Namaḥ | Oṃ Hrīṃ Ghaṃ Namaḥ | Oṃ Hrīṃ Ṅaṃ Namaḥ | Oṃ Hrīṃ Caṃ Namaḥ | Oṃ Hrīṃ Chaṃ Namaḥ | Oṃ Hrīṃ Jaṃ Namaḥ | Oṃ Hrīṃ Jhaṃ Namaḥ | Oṃ Hrīṃ Ñaṃ Namaḥ | Oṃ Hrīṃ Ṭaṃ Namaḥ | Oṃ Hrīṃ Ṭhaṃ Namaḥ |

Then, having meditated upon the *maṇipūraka* wheel at the navel as a ten-petaled lotus, one should place the ten syllables beginning with *ḍa* and ending with *pha* upon those respective petals: *oṃ hrīṃ ḍaṃ namaḥ*; *oṃ hrīṃ ḍhaṃ namaḥ*;
*oṃ hrīṃ ṇaṃ namaḥ*; *oṃ hrīṃ taṃ namaḥ*; *oṃ hrīṃ thaṃ namaḥ*; *oṃ...*
*Hrīṃ daṃ namaḥ*. *Oṃ hrīṃ dhaṃ namaḥ*. *Oṃ hrīṃ naṃ namaḥ*. *Oṃ hrīṃ paṃ namaḥ*. *Oṃ hrīṃ phaṃ namaḥ*.
Then, having meditated upon the *svādhiṣṭhāna-cakra* as a six-petalled lotus at the base of the *liṅga*, [one should place them] on those respective petals.
One should place the six syllables beginning with *ba* and ending with *la*: *oṃ hrīṃ baṃ namaḥ*; *oṃ hrīṃ bhaṃ namaḥ*;
*oṃ hrīṃ maṃ namaḥ*; *oṃ hrīṃ yaṃ namaḥ*; *oṃ hrīṃ raṃ namaḥ*; *oṃ hrīṃ laṃ namaḥ*.

Then, having meditated upon a four-petalled lotus at the *mūlādhāra*, one should place the four syllables beginning with *va* and ending with *sa* on those respective petals: *oṃ hrīṃ vaṃ namaḥ*; *oṃ hrīṃ śaṃ namaḥ*; *oṃ hrīṃ ṣaṃ namaḥ*; *oṃ hrīṃ saṃ namaḥ*.
Then, having visualized the *ājñācakra* as a two-petaled lotus between the eyebrows, one should place two syllables upon each petal:
*oṃ hrīṃ haṃ namaḥ* and *oṃ hrīṃ kṣaṃ namaḥ*. Now follows the meditation on the six chakras:
In the foundation, at the genitals, the navel, the manifest heart, the root of the palate, and the forehead;
in the two-petaled, sixteen-spoked, twenty-two-spoked, ten-spoked, twelve-spoked, and four-spoked [cakras].

I bow to the form of the letters situated on all petals: the vowels at the end of the residence (the pericarp), accompanied by ḍa, pha, ka, and ṭha in the middle of the young ones (the inner circle), and the syllables *haṃ* and *kṣaṃ* endowed with the meaning of the principles (*tattva*) in the region of the throat.
Thus ends the meditation on the six chakras. This concludes the internal placement of the Mātṛkās (antarmātṛkānyāsa).
Now follows the external placement of the Mātṛkās encapsulated by Bhuvaneśvarī (bhuvaneśvarīsampuṭitabahirmātṛkānyāsa).
Of this mantra of the external Mātṛkās encapsulated by the venerable Bhuvaneśvarī, Brahmā is the seer (ṛṣi) located in the head; Gāyatrī is the meter...
The meter (chandas) is Mukha; the deity (devatā) is Sarasvatī, the external Mātṛkās, in the heart; the seeds (bījāni) are the consonants (hal) in the secret place;

the powers (śaktayaḥ) are the vowels (svarāḥ) in the feet; the pin (kīlaka) is *kṣaḥ* in the navel. This is the application (viniyoga) for the external Mātṛkā-nyāsa. Now, the six limbs (ṣaḍaṅga): *Oṃ hraṃ aṃ kaṃ 5 āṃ hrāṃ hṛdayāya namaḥ* on the two thumbs.

Oṃ hriṃ iṃ caṃ 5 īṃ hrīṃ śirase svāhā—on the two index fingers. Oṃ hrūṃ uṃ ṭaṃ 5 ūṃ hraṃ śikhāyai vaṣaṭ—on the two middle fingers. Oṃ hreṃ eṃ taṃ 5 aiṃ hraiṃ kavacāya huṃ—on the two ring fingers. Oṃ hroṃ oṃ paṃ 5 auṃ hrauṃ netratrayāya vauṣaṭ—on the two little fingers.
Oṃ hraṃ aṃ yaṃ [repeated ten times] aḥ hraḥ phaṭ for the weapon-mantra on the palms and backs of the hands. Thus is the six-limbed rite (ṣaḍaṅga). The visualization (dhyāna):
[One should meditate on the deity] whose face, arms, feet, hips, and chest are fashioned with the distinctions of the fifty letters...

I bow to that Bhāratī, who resides upon a lotus, whose hair is bound with a radiant crescent moon, who is as white as the moon or jasmine, who holds in her excellent hands a rosary, a water-pot, and a book marked with the thought [of wisdom], who possesses three eyes, and who bears the weight of full breasts and hips like those of a woman in the prime of youth.
She is marked with the book and the knowledge-mudrā, three-eyed, and crowned by the moon;
extending from the base to the aperture of Brahmā, she is more slender than a lotus fiber.
One who knows the mantra, having become absorbed in her, should contemplate that Goddess within— the destroyer of the threefold sins— and should not contemplate anything else.
Through this, one attains the difficult-to-attain state by means of Brahmā, Keśava, Rudra, and the others;
it is the wheel of phonemes (varṇacakra), perfectly joined, beginning with the letter *p* and ending with the wrathful syllable *kṣ*.
One should place [the seed-syllable] that is stainless and as lovely as the luster of the moon upon the body.
Regarding that placement, there is this verse:
"The first [vowel] is the head; then the next is the face; *i* and *ī* are the two eyes; and *u* and *ū* are the two ears."
The syllables *ṛ* and *ṝ* are the two nostril-pits; the following two syllables (*ḷ* and *ḹ*) are the two cheeks;

the dentals (*t*, *th*, *d*, *dh*, *n*) are the upper and lower rows of teeth; the diphthongs (*e*, *ai*, *o*, *au*) are, in order, the pair of lips; the vowel *u* with the visarga (*ḥ*) is the root of the tongue and the prominent point [on the palate]; and the vowel *a* is the neck.

The consonants beginning with *ka* are on the right arm, while those of the other group (*ca*, *ṭa*, *ta*, *pa*) are on the left arm; *ṭa* and so forth are in sequence on the two feet, and *kū* and *pha* are on the two sides of the belly.

O Ambika! The lineage (vaṃśa), the back (pṛṣṭha), the navel and heart (nābhi-hṛdaye), the three musical instruments (vādya-traya), the seven elements beginning with 'ya' (yādyāḥ saptadhātavaḥ), the vital breath (samīraṇa) with the letter 'sa' and 'kṣa', and Krodha—these are [the deities].

Namely: Oṃ hrīṃ aṃ namaḥ hrīṃ on the head; oṃ hrīṃ āṃ namaḥ hrīṃ on the face; oṃ hrīṃ iṃ namaḥ hrīṃ on the right eye; oṃ hrīṃ īṃ namaḥ hrīṃ on the left eye; oṃ hrīṃ uṃ namaḥ hrīṃ on the right ear; oṃ hrīṃ ūṃ namaḥ hrīṃ... [on the left ear].

At the left ear: *oṃ hrīṃ ṛṃ namaḥ*. At the right nostril: *hrīṃ*. At the left nostril: *oṃ hrīṃ ṝṃ namaḥ hrīṃ*. At the right cheek: *oṃ hrīṃ ḷṃ namaḥ hrīṃ*. At the left cheek: *oṃ hrīṃ ḹṃ namaḥ hrīṃ*. At the upper row of teeth: *oṃ hrīṃ eṃ namaḥ hrīṃ*. *Oṃ hrīṃ*... [continues].

Aiṃ namaḥ hrīṃ on the row of lower teeth. Oṃ hrīṃ oṃ namaḥ hrīṃ on the upper lip. Oṃ hrīṃ auṃ namaḥ hrīṃ on the lower lip. Oṃ hrīṃ aṃ namaḥ hrīṃ at the root of the tongue. Oṃ hrīṃ aḥ namaḥ hrīṃ at the tip of the tongue. Oṃ hrīṃ kaṃ namaḥ hrīṃ on the right shoulder. Oṃ hrīṃ khaṃ...

Namaḥ hrīṃ to the right arm. Oṃ hrīṃ gaṃ namaḥ hrīṃ to the right elbow. Oṃ hrīṃ ghaṃ namaḥ hrīṃ to the right wrist. Oṃ hrīṃ ṅaṃ namaḥ hrīṃ to the palm of the right hand. Oṃ hrīṃ caṃ namaḥ hrīṃ to the left shoulder. Oṃ hrīṃ chaṃ namaḥ hrīṃ to the left arm. Oṃ hrīṃ...
Oṃ hrīṃ jaṃ namaḥ hrīṃ on the left elbow; oṃ hrīṃ jhaṃ namaḥ hrīṃ on the left wrist;
oṃ hrīṃ ñaṃ namaḥ hrīṃ on the palm of the left hand; oṃ hrīṃ ṭaṃ namaḥ hrīṃ on the right hip;
oṃ hrīṃ ṭhaṃ namaḥ hrīṃ on the right thigh; oṃ hrīṃ ḍaṃ namaḥ hrīṃ on the right knee; oṃ...

Hrīṃ ḍhaṃ namaḥ hrīṃ on the right shank. Oṃ hrīṃ ṇaṃ namaḥ hrīṃ on the right foot. Oṃ hrīṃ taṃ namaḥ hrīṃ on the left hip. Oṃ hrīṃ thaṃ namaḥ hrīṃ on the left thigh. Oṃ hrīṃ daṃ namaḥ hrīṃ on the left knee. Oṃ hrīṃ dhaṃ namaḥ hrīṃ...

On the left calf: *oṃ hrīṃ naṃ namaḥ hrīṃ*. On the left foot: *oṃ hrīṃ paṃ namaḥ hrīṃ*. On the right flank: *oṃ hrīṃ phaṃ namaḥ hrīṃ*. On the left flank: *oṃ hrīṃ baṃ namaḥ hrīṃ*. On the spinal column: *oṃ hrīṃ bhaṃ namaḥ hrīṃ*. On the navel: *oṃ hrīṃ maṃ namaḥ*.

Hrīṃ, in the heart; Oṃ Hrīṃ Yaṃ Namaḥ Hrīṃ, in the skin at the base (ādhāra); Oṃ Hrīṃ Raṃ Namaḥ Hrīṃ, in the blood at the svādhiṣṭhāna, in the liṅga; Oṃ Hrīṃ Laṃ Namaḥ Hrīṃ, in the flesh at the maṇipūraka, in the navel;
Oṃ Hrīṃ Vaṃ Namaḥ Hrīṃ, in the fat at the heart; Oṃ Hrīṃ Śaṃ Namaḥ Hrīṃ, in the bone.

At the throat, in the Viśuddhi [cakra]: *oṃ hrīṃ ṣaṃ namaḥ*. At the palate, in the marrow: *hrīṃ*. At the center of the eyebrows, in the Ājñā [cakra], in the semen: *oṃ hrīṃ saṃ namaḥ hrīṃ*. On the forehead, in the vital breath (*prāṇa*): *oṃ hrīṃ haṃ namaḥ hrīṃ*. In the aperture of Brahmā (*brahmarandhra*), in the wrath: *oṃ hrīṃ kṣaṃ namaḥ hrīṃ*. Thus.
The external Mātṛkā-nyāsa encapsulated by Bhuvaneśvarī:
when this nyāsa has been performed in this manner, the practitioner of mantra is liberated from all sins;
by performing it at the three junctions of the day for three months, one attains liberation while living.
Even if one performs [this rite] only once daily through the ritual placement (*nyāsa*),
one becomes honored in the palace of the king and shall attract women.
Moreover, the Lotus-Dweller, remaining steadfast, increases day by day within his abode in order to benefit the entire universe.
Thus ends the fruit of the Mātṛkā-nyāsa.
Thereafter, one should perform three rounds of prāṇāyāma. Its characteristic is as follows:
one should fill the breath through the iḍā [nāḍī] with the vowels and retain it [in kumbhaka] with the consonants.
Then, with the letters beginning with 'ya' and so forth, together with Piṅgalā.
The *iḍā* is situated in the left nostril, while the *piṅgalā* is on the right;
between the *iḍā* and *piṅgalā* is the *suṣumṇā*, which flows through the aperture.

In this manner, one should perform three rounds of breath control (*prāṇāyāma*), or else [perform them] with the root mantra. Therein, first having recited the armor (*kavaca*): "To the Seer Śakti, obeisance upon the head; to the Gāyatrī meter, obeisance upon the mouth; to the deity Śrī Bhuvaneśvarī, obeisance upon the heart. *Haṃ*.

*Namo* to the Seed-syllable (*bīja*) at the secret place; *namaḥ* to *Īṃ Śakti* at the feet; *namaḥ* to *Raṃ Kīlaka* on all limbs. This is the application (*viniyoga*) for the recitation (*japa*) for the sake of pleasing the venerable Bhuvaneśvarī. Now follows the placement (*nyāsa*) of Hṛllekhā and others: *Oṃ hrīṃ*, *namaḥ* to Hṛllekhā on the head; *Oṃ hraṃ*...

*Oṃ gaganāyai namo mukhe* (Salutation to Gaganā on the face). *Oṃ hraiṃ raktāyai namo hṛdaye* (Salutation to Raktā on the heart). *Oṃ hrauṃ karālikāyai namo guhye* (Salutation to Karālikā on the secret place). *Oṃ hraḥ mahocchuṣmāyai namaḥ pādayoḥ* (Salutation to Mahocchuṣmā on the feet). Thus ends the *Hṛllekhā-nyāsa*. Now follows the six-limbed ritual (*ṣaḍaṅga*) of the root mantra: *Oṃ hrāṃ hṛdayāya namaḥ aṅguṣṭhayoḥ* (Salutation to the heart on the two thumbs). *Oṃ...* [The text continues with further mantras].

*Hrīṃ*, svāhā to the head, on the two index fingers; *Oṃ hrūṃ*, vaṣaṭ to the crest-lock (*śikhā*), on the two middle fingers; *Oṃ hraiṃ*, huṃ to the armor (*kavaca*), on the two ring fingers; *Oṃ hrauṃ*, vauṣaṭ to the three eyes, on the two little fingers; *Oṃ hraḥ*, phaṭ to the weapon (*astra*), on the palms and backs of the hands. Thus is the six-limbed ritual (*ṣaḍaṅga*).

Now, the placement (nyāsa) of Sāvitrī and others: Oṃ hrāṃ, salutation to Brahmā accompanied by Gāyatrī on the forehead. Oṃ hrīṃ, salutation to Viṣṇu accompanied by Sāvitrī on the right cheek. Oṃ hraṃ, salutation to Maheśvara accompanied by Vāgīśvarī on the left cheek. Oṃ hrauṃ, salutation to the Lord of Wealth (Kubera) accompanied by Śrī...

On the left ear: *Oṃ hrauṃ*, obeisance to Smara accompanied by Rati. On the face: *Oṃ hraṃ*, obeisance to Gaṇapati accompanied by Siddhi and Buddhi. On the right ear: *Oṃ hraḥ*, obeisance to Bhuvaneśvarī. Thus is the Sāvitrī-nyāsa and others.
Furthermore, one should place these separately upon the body as follows: *Oṃ hrāṃ gāyatryai namaḥ* at the base of the throat;
*Oṃ hrīṃ sāvitryai namaḥ* on the right breast; *Oṃ hrūṃ sarasvatyai namaḥ* [on the left breast].
On the left breast: *Oṃ hraiṃ brahmaṇe namaḥ*. On the right shoulder: *Oṃ hrauṃ viṣṇave namaḥ*.
On the heart: *Oṃ hraḥ śivāya namaḥ*. Having thus performed the placement (*vinyāsa*), [one continues]: *Oṃ hrauṃ hṛllekhāyai namaḥ* on the heart; *Oṃ hraiṃ gaganāyai namaḥ svāhā* on the head.

Oṃ hrūṃ, salutation to Raktā; vaṣaṭ to the crest-lock (śikhā). Oṃ hrīṃ, salutation to Karālikā; huṃ to the armor (kavaca). Oṃ hrāṃ, salutation to Mahocchuṣmā; vauṣaṭ to the three eyes. Hraḥ, salutation to the Giver of All Siddhis; phaṭ to the weapon (astra). This is the script for the placement of the five faces.

Now, the placement of the [six] Brāhmī goddesses (*brāhmyādinyāsa*): Oṃ hrāṃ, salutation to Brahmyā on the head. Oṃ hrīṃ, salutation to Māheśvarī on the right shoulder. Oṃ hrūṃ, salutation to Kaumārī on the right side. Oṃ hraiṃ, salutation to Vārāhī on the left shoulder. Oṃ hrauṃ, salutation to Caṇḍikā on the left side. Oṃ hraḥ...
"Salutation to Mahālakṣmī in the heart"—thus is the placement of the [six] Brāhmī goddesses (*brāhmyādinyāsa*).
Some also perform the placement of the sacred seats (*pīṭhanyāsa*) upon their own bodies.
Having performed the placement in this manner, one should perform the threefold pervasive placement (*vyāpaka*) with the root mantra. Now, the visualization (*dhyāna*): in the heart...

Having formed the *yonimudrā*, one should meditate [upon her] as having a luster equal to the rising sun, surpassing the splendor of fresh jasmine, crowned with a crescent moon, radiant on her head, three-eyed, adorned with earrings shining with various gems, and seated upon a lotus.

I bow to that Mother Ambikā, who wears necklaces, neck-ornaments, girdles, strings of gems, and bracelets, who is clothed in variegated garments, and who holds a noose, a goad, a lotus, and displays the gestures of granting fearlessness and bestowing boons.

Furthermore: I worship Bhuvaneśī, who possesses the splendor of the rising sun, who wears the moon as her crown, whose breasts are lofty, who is endowed with three eyes, whose face is smiling, and whose hands grant boons and hold the goad, the noose, and the gesture of fearlessness.
Having meditated thus and worshipped with mental offerings, one should recite [the mantra] three hundred and thirty-two times every day;

or alternatively, one may recite it one hundred and eight times. After the recitation, having again performed the ritual rinsing of the mouth (*ācamana*), breath control (*prāṇāyāma*), and so forth, as well as the placement of the six limbs (*ṣaḍaṅganyāsa*) and meditation, one should take water in the right hand and—
O protector of the most secret of secrets, accept this recitation performed by us;
O Goddess, Sovereign of the Gods, may success be mine through your grace!
Thus, accompanied by flowers and unbroken rice grains (*akṣata*), he should offer the recitation (*japa*) into the right hand of the Goddess on his left side.
He should prostrate with the five mudrās.
The Stambhana, the Caturaśra, the Matsya, and the Gokṣura— these,
along with the Yonimudrā, are renowned as the five mudrās for salutation.
Thus one should perform the salutation.
Thereafter, one should recite hymns, the Thousand Names, and so forth. Now follows the extraction of the various mantras: Lakulīśa mounted upon fire, with the left eye and the half-moon.
Its seed-syllable has been fully described; it is to be practiced by those who desire spiritual accomplishment.
Now follows the second extraction of the divisions:
A wise person should extract the mantra consisting of the three seeds— Vāgbhava, Śambhuvanitā, and Rāmā— which accomplishes the fruit of the three aims of human life.

The [selection of] sages and so forth is as before. We shall explain the number of recitations for the *puraścaraṇa* rite further ahead. Thus, in the manual (*paddhati*) of Pṛthvīdhara Ācārya, based on the various systems of the *Śāradātilaka*, [this was written] by Anantadeva, who resides at Mātṛpura and follows the tradition of the venerable Dāyideva.

In this *Bhuvaneśvarī-kramacandrikā* composed [by me], the second ritual section (*kalpa*), titled "The Exposition of the Rites Beginning with the Purification of the Elements (*bhūtaśuddhi*) and Ending with Japa," is complete. May it be offered to the venerable Guru-nātha.
[Now begins] the exposition of the worship of Bhuvaneśvarī.
Śrī (ḥ)
I salute the Guru, the light of consciousness, whose nature is the Supreme Brahman.
The great worship of Bhuvaneśī is performed by Anantadeva. 1.
Now, the method for worship, the installation of the deity in the yantra, japa, homa, puraścaraṇa, and so forth, is being written.
The Śrī Devī said: "O Lord, everything that bestows great wonder has been told!"
Now he said: "Tell me quickly the worship according to the prescribed ritual."
Śiva said:
Listen, O Queen of the Gods, to the worship that bestows success upon the practitioner.
Worship is traditionally known to be of three kinds: daily (nitya), occasional (naimittika), and optional (kāmya).
The extraction of the yantra is performed on gold, silver, copper, or a birch-bark leaf.
[It consists of] a point, a triangle, a hexagon, and a beautiful eight-petaled lotus.
The circular lotus, adorned with four gates, consists of sixteen squares.
One should carefully draw the yantra with camphor, agallochum, musk, sandalwood, and saffron, using a pen made of gold or silver.
Thus, in the absence of gold, silver, or other materials, this beautiful yantra should be prepared on ground smeared with cow dung;
the pedestal (pīṭha) is to be a perfect square, measuring twenty-four, sixteen, or twelve finger-breadths (aṅgula),
which constitutes the best, middling, and lowest [sizes] respectively.

Having drawn a square, a sixteen-petaled lotus, an eight-petaled lotus, a hexagon, a triangle, and a bindu with camphor, agallochum, musk, sandalwood, saffron, and other substances—one who desires the enjoyment of sovereignty should draw it with a golden stylus;
by means of dūrvā juice, one conquers death; by means of liquid gold, one conquers enemies; [it is also used for] immobilization (stambhana).

With the juice of turmeric. Regarding the rule for the pen (*lekhanī*) therein: one desiring sovereignty [should use] a pen made from the branch of a *pālāśa* tree, a *jāti* creeper, *sārasvata* grass, or a crow's wing; one desiring general prosperity [should use] one made of gold or silver;
for subjugation (*vaśya*), a red *aśvattha* tree with a cat's bone; and for the practice of attraction (*ākṛṣṭi*), red sandalwood; for immobilization (*stambhana*), [red sandalwood].
One should draw [the diagram] with a stylus made of turmeric. Having thus performed the construction of the yantra, one should worship the Goddess therein.
As it is stated in the Smṛti:
"The yantra is declared to be composed of the deity; the deity is in the form of the yantra."
Because of the confinement within all suffering arising from defects such as desire, anger, and the like.
They call it a "yantra" because, when worshipped, the deity finds delight within it—
just as the soul does in the body, or as a lamp does in its oil, O beloved.
O beloved, having learned from the mouth of the Guru how this yantra is established for all the gods, one should worship it all according to the prescribed rite.
Therefore, having performed the extraction of the moon according to the standard measure of the extraction, one should begin the worship.

First, there is the worship of the pavilion (*maṇḍapa*). Then, having made the temple of the deity beautiful, well-perfumed with incense, and adorned with many lamps, one should take a flower and [recite]: *aiṃ śrīṃ hrīṃ bhuvaneśvarīmaṇḍapāya namaḥ*.

Having worshipped with flowers, unbroken rice, and other offerings, one should begin the worship of the door. Having recited the root mantra and sprinkled [the area] with pure water from the four doors, one should worship the deities of the door. Having worshipped at the door with "Aiṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ, obeisance to Dvāraśrī," one should [worship] Aiṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ in the center of the upper lintel (ūrdhvodumbara).

Gaṃ, obeisance to Gaṇapati. Aiṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Sāṃ, obeisance to Sarasvatī; [place these] in the two corners thereof. Aiṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Kṣāṃ, obeisance to Kṣetrapāla. Aiṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Vāṃ, obeisance to Vaṭuka. Aiṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Dhāṃ, obeisance to Dhātṛ. Aiṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ, obeisance to Vidhātṛ. Aiṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ.

Gāṃ, salutation to Gaṅgā; Aiṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Yāṃ, salutation to Yamunā; Aiṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Śaṃ, salutation to Śaṅkhanidhi; Aiṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Paṃ, salutation to Padmanidhi; Aiṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ, salutation to the Ḍākinīs on the right branch; Aiṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ, salutation to the Śākinīs...

On the left branch [of the door], having worshipped within the pavilion with "Aiṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Deṃ, obeisance to the Door-sill (dehalī)," and on the door-sill with "Aiṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ, obeisance to Vāstupuruṣa"; thus, having worshipped the doors.

Contracting the left limb while touching the left branch, he should enter within with his left foot and worship the *tiraskariṇī* (the veil) at the doorway: *Oṃ aiṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ īṃ namastrailokyamohini mahāmāye sakalapaśujanamanaścakṣustiraskaraṇaṃ kuru kuru*.

Having worshipped the *tiraskariṇī* (the veil) with "Svāhā," I remember her who has disheveled hair, is naked, whose eyes roll with intoxication, and who causes the assembly of bound souls (*paśus*) to faint from the sight of her own womb. Having meditated on her as "she of disheveled hair," one should offer her an oblation (*bali*) consisting of liquor, meat, incense, and flowers, using the previously mentioned mantra.

Then the teacher, desiring to worship the portion of Bhuvaneśvarī in his own country, being restrained in speech, having conquered his senses and subdued his anger, wearing red ornaments and garments, with a pleasing appearance,
his body smeared with the eight perfumes and adorned with a garland of flowers, sits upon a red seat and [recites] *aiṃ hrīṃ*.

Having worshipped with "Śrīṃ, obeisance to the lotus-seat of the foundational power (ādhāraśakti)" and having sat down, one should worship two Śarabhas beneath the seat for the pacification of obstacles on the left and right sides, reciting: "Oṃ hrīṃ hrauṃ, obeisance to Śiva, the Great Śarabha; Oṃ hrīṃ hrauṃ, obeisance to Śivā, the Great Śarabhī."

Having established two lamps and placed the ritual offerings in the right hand, having tied the topknot with the root mantra and performed the ceremonial sipping of water (ācamana) with: "Oṃ hrīṃ, I purify the principle of the self (ātmatattva), obeisance; Oṃ hrīṃ, I purify the principle of the creator (vidhātattva);
Oṃ hrīṃ, I purify the principle of Śiva (śivatattva)," and having thus performed the ācamana, [one performs] inhalation (pūraka) sixteen times with the root mantra.
Having performed three rounds of *prāṇāyāma* by means of thirty-two *kuṃbhakas* and sixteen *recakas*, and having proclaimed the lunar day (*tithi*) and other details, [one should say]:

"For the sake of accomplishing all my desires, I shall perform the worship of Śrī Bhuvaneśvarī; I shall perform the purifications, nyāsas, and other rites that constitute its limbs; and I shall perform the placement of the vessels (*pātrasthāpana*) which are its constituent parts."
Having performed the mental resolve (*saṅkalpa*), the sequence of vessels therein is as follows:
first the *kumbha*, then the conch (*śaṅkha*), the *śrīpātra*, the *śaktipātra*,
the vessel for enjoyment (*bhoga*), the *gurupātra*, and the vessels for the offerings (*balipātra*), in due order.

Then, between the yantra and oneself, on one's left side, having fashioned with pure water a mandala marked by the syllable *māyā* (hrīṃ)— consisting of a circle, a hexagon, and a triangle— representing the flowing channel (*vahannāḍī*) of the hand, using the right hand in the *matsyamudrā* gesture, [one places it] upon the thumb of the left hand.

Without pressing [the ground] with the left [hand], having worshipped the center of the triangle with flowers and unbroken rice (*akṣata*) using the root mantra, both in the sequential and reverse orders, [one worships] in the hexagon: *aiṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ*, "I worship the venerable sandals of the Heart Goddess" (three times); "I worship the venerable sandals of the Head Goddess" (three times).

"I worship the Śrīpādukā of the goddess Śikhā," (three times); "I worship the Śrīpādukā of the goddess Kavaca," (three times); "I worship the Śrīpādukā of the goddess Netra," (three times); "I worship the Śrīpādukā of the goddess Astra. Having thus worshipped the six limbs (*ṣaḍaṅga*), [one worships] in the circle: "3 *laṃ* obeisance to Lakṣmī; 3 *kaṃ* to Kālī; 3 *saṃ* to Sarasvatī."
In the square [of the mandala], having worshipped those in the southeast and other directions with: "3 *kṣāṃ* salutation to the Ocean of Milk; 3 *iṃ* salutation to the Ocean of Sugarcane Juice;

3 *maṃ* salutation to the Ocean of Honey; 3 *pīṃ* salutation to the Ocean of Nectar," and having worshipped [the vessel] with the root mantra using perfumes and other offerings, one should take the base (*ādhāra*) which has been washed with the weapon mantra (*huṃ phaṭ*) and [place it] with the root seed-syllable.

Having established the base of the jar with the mantra: "I establish the base of the jar of Śrī Bhuvaneśvarī; obeisance," and having worshipped it with: "Rāṃ rīṃ rūṃ ramalavaraya-ūṃ raṃ, obeisance to the fire-maṇḍala, the base of the jar, whose self consists of ten digits (kalās) that bestow dharma," one should worship the digits (kalās) upon it in a clockwise direction.
p.
132) Namely: 3 Yaṃ Dhūmrārciḥ-kalā-śrī, 3 Raṃ Ūṣmā-kalā-śrī, Pā, 3 Laṃ Jvalinī-kalā-śrī, Mā, 3 Vaṃ Jvālinī-kalā, 3 Śaṃ Visphuliṅginī-kalā, 3 Ṣaṃ Suśrī-kalā.

Having worshipped with scents and other offerings using *saṃ svarūpaka* (3 times), *haṃ kapilāka* (3 times), *laṃ havyavahāka* (3 times), and *kṣaṃ kavyavahāka*, one should then take the water-pot (*kalaśa*) with the root mantra and wash the pot with the left hand while reciting: *oṃ hrīṃ hrīṃ hrūṃ hrūṃ brahmāṇḍacaṣakāya svāhā*. Then, [anoint it] with the ten-ingredient incense (*daśāṅga*).
Having fumigated [the vessel] with the mantra *oṃ aiṃ sandīpanī jvālāmālinī hūṃ phaṭ svāhā*,

having placed the *yonimudrā* upon the *kalaśa* and consecrated it with the *praṇava* (Oṃ), having veiled it with the *avaguṇṭhanamudrā*, [one should recite] the five seed-syllables: *oṃ krīṃ namaḥ*, *hrīṃ namaḥ*, *hraṃ namaḥ*, *krīṃ namaḥ*, *hvūṃ namaḥ*.

Having placed [the mantra] in the jar: *Oṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ hrīṃ oṃ namo bhagavati mahālakṣmi bhuvaneśvari paramadhāmni ūrdhvaśūnyaprakāśini paramākāśabhāsurasomasūryāgnibhakṣiṇi āgaccha āgaccha pātraṃ gṛhṇa*.
Having recited the vessel-mantra: *gṛhṇa prasphura prasphura phaṭ vauṣaṭ*, and having established it with:
*I establish the jar of the venerable Aniruddha-Sarasvatī; obeisance*, [one recites]:
*hrāṃ hrīṃ hrūṃ hamalavaraya-ūṃ haṃ, to the self consisting of the twelve kalās that bestow wealth*.

Having worshipped with "Obeisance to the Sun-disk vessel," one should worship the *kalās* (energetic digits) in clockwise order upon it, as follows: 3 *kaṃ bhaṃ*, obeisance to the venerable *Tapinī* digit; 3 *khaṃ baṃ*, obeisance to the venerable *Tāpinī* digit; 3 *gaṃ phaṃ*, obeisance to the venerable *Dhūmrārcis* digit; 3 *ghaṃ paṃ*, obeisance to the venerable *Marīci* digit; 3 *ṅaṃ naṃ*, obeisance to the venerable *Jvālinī* digit; 3 *caṃ*...
