Having worshipped the twelve digits (kalās) as follows: *dhaṃ* Rucikalā, *chaṃ daṃ* Suṣumṇākalā, *jaṃ thaṃ* Bhogadākalā, *jhaṃ taṃ* Viśvā, *ñaṃ ṇaṃ* Bodhinīkalā, *ṭaṃ ḍhaṃ* Dhāriṇīkalā, *ṭhaṃ ḍaṃ* Kṣamākalā; then, taking the vessel of nectar in the right hand, [recite] the root mantra (*mūlavidyā*).

Having filled the pitcher with a stream of water touching the second joint of the left hand, using the *mātṛkā* in both forward and reverse order; this is the purification of the second [joint]. Having purified the second [joint] with "Aiṃ Hrīṃ Jūṃ Saḥ, *tat savitur vareṇyam*" and the root mantra, one should pour a little [water] into the pitcher. With "Tryambakaṃ yajāmahe," [one purifies] the fish.

Having purified [the vessel] and cast [the water] into it with the mantra *tad viṣṇoḥ*, having purified [the vessel] and cast [the water] into it, and having consecrated it with the mantra *gaṅge ca yamune caiva*, one should release it from the curse of Brahmā by reciting: *vrāṃ vrīṃ vrūṃ vraiṃ vrauṃ vraḥ brahmaśāpavimocitāyai sudhādevyai namaḥ*. This is the purification of the substance (*dravyaśodhana*). [Then,] over the substance...

Having recited it ten times, one should perform the liberation from Kṛṣṇa’s curse: *oṃ kṛṣṇaśāpaṃ vimocaya vimocaya amṛtaṃ srāvaya srāvaya svāhā*. Having thus recited it ten times—one should meditate on the single, supreme Brahman, which consists of both the gross and the subtle, and is eternal.
By that [act], I purify the sin of Brahman-slaughter born from my hair.
O Goddess, born from the solar disc, arisen from the abode of Varuṇa,
composed of the seed-syllable Amā— may [this person] be liberated from the curse of Śukra.
p.

133) If the *praṇava* is the seed of the Vedas and consists of the bliss of Brahman, by that truth, O Goddess, may [your] Brahmin-slaughter [be removed]. (The portion contained within the brackets was originally at the beginning.)

This was not found in the manuscript due to its being fragmentary; furthermore, having obtained a separate copy, this section has been extracted from the manuscript titled *Dakṣiṇakālīpaddhati*, numbered 2735 in the collection of the Rājasthān Prācya Vidyā Prasāraka Maṇḍala, and inserted here. This manuscript, too, is by the author of this very *Paddhati*.
The wise should understand that this is indeed the work of the illustrious Anantadeva. [Editor:
May it dispel [all obstacles].
Thus, one should release the nectar from these two— the curse of Śukra and the sin of Brahman-slaughter— by churning it thrice with the Amṛta-vidyā mantra:
*oṃ hvāṃ hvīṃ hvūṃ hvaiṃ hvauṃ hvaḥ amṛte amṛtodbhave amṛteśvari amṛtavarṣiṇi amṛtasvarūpiṇi amṛtaṃ srāvaya srāvaya*.
"Release [the nectar] from the curse of Śukra! Release it! Salutation to Mocikā! Oṃ Hrīṃ Jūṃ Saḥ Svāhā!

Having stirred it three times with this mantra, one should dry the web of defects within that nectar by means of inhalation (*pūraka*) using the wind-seed syllable *yaṃ*, burn it by means of retention (*kumbhaka*) using the fire-seed syllable *raṃ*, and then transform it into nectar by means of exhalation (*recaka*) using the nectar-seed syllable *vaṃ*.

In that regard, one should perform the warding off of the ten defects as follows: *Hskhphreṃ* to the deities of the travelers, *huṃ phaṭ svāhā*. *Hskhphreṃ* to Āsphāligrāmacāṇḍālinī, *huṃ*. *Hskhphreṃ* to Dṛṣṭicāṇḍālinī, *huṃ*. *Hskhphreṃ* to Sṛṣṭicāṇḍālinī, *huṃ*. *Hskhphreṃ*...
*Sparśacāṇḍālinī* huṃ hskhphreṃ; *Ghaṭacāṇḍālinī* huṃ hskhphreṃ; *Tapanavedhacāṇḍālinī* huṃ hskhphreṃ; *Sarvajanadṛṣṭisparśadoṣacāṇḍālinī* huṃ hskhphreṃ;
*Paśupāśacāṇḍālinī* huṃ phaṭ svāhā. Thus [in] the nectar of the jar.

One should scatter flowers, unbroken rice, and food offerings. Having worshipped with the mantra: *sāṃ sīṃ sūṃ sa ma la va ra ya ūṃ saṃ kāmaprada-ṣoḍaśakalātmane somamaṇḍalāya kalaśāmṛtāya namaḥ*, one should worship the sixteen digits (*kalās*) upon it in a clockwise direction: 3. *aṃ amṛtākalā śrīpādukāṃ*.
I worship; salutations! 3 Āṃ, the digit Mānadā, Śrī. 3 Iṃ, the digit Pūṣā, Śrī. 3 Īṃ, the digit Tuṣṭi, Śrī. 3 Uṃ, the digit Puṣṭi, Śrī. 3 Ūṃ, the digit Rati, Śrī. Ṛṃ, the digit Dhṛti, Śrī.
3 Ṝṃ, the digit Śaśikā, Śrī. 3 Ḷṃ, the digit Candrikā, Śrī. 3 Ḹṃ, the digit Kanti, Śrī. 3 Eṃ.
Jyotsnākalā Śrī. 3 Aiṃ Śrīkalā Śrī. 3 Oṃ Prītikalā Śrī. 3 Auṃ Aṅgadākalā Śrī.
3 Aṃ Pūrṇākalā Śrī. 3 Aḥ Pūrṇāmṛtākalā Śrī.
Having thus worshipped the sixteen digits (kalās) of the Moon, one should perform the *prāṇapratiṣṭhā* (vitalization) of the digits: Oṃ Āṃ Hrīṃ Kroṃ Yaṃ...

Raṃ laṃ vaṃ śaṃ ṣaṃ saṃ haṃ laṃ kṣaṃ so haṃ haṃ saḥ. In this pitcher, which is endowed with the foundational [elements], the vital breaths (*prāṇa*) of the digits of Fire, Sun, and Moon are here; the vital breaths are here. Having recited the mantra again: "In this pitcher, which is endowed with the foundational [elements], the life-force (*jīva*) of the digits of Fire, Sun, and Moon is stationed here. Having recited the mantra again...

Having recited: "O all the senses—speech, mind, skin, eyes, ears, tongue, nose, and breath—having come here indeed into this vessel provided with the substratum, may you remain happily for a long time;
Svāhā! one should scatter flowers and unbroken rice-grains upon the vessel.

134) Having thus performed the consecration of the vital breath (*prāṇapratiṣṭhā*), worshipped the jar with perfumes and other offerings, tied a flower garland around its neck, one should mutter the mantra *haṃsaḥ śuciṣat*. Therein, in the four directions and the center, [one should place] *glūṃ*.
Salutation to Gaganaratna in the east; *slūṃ*, salutation to Svargaratna in the south; *mlūṃ*, salutation to Manuṣyaratna in the west;

*blūṃ*, salutation to Ṇatālaratna in the north; *nvlīṃ*, salutation to Nāgaratna in the center. Having thus worshipped the five jewels (*pañcaratna*), in their midst is the triangle consisting of the letters from *a* to *tha*, with *haṃ kṣaṃ* in the center.

Having written it again and having consecrated it three times with the previously mentioned Amṛtavidyā, one should mutter the Jātavedas-gāyatrī and the Tryambaka-mantra. Then, having consecrated it with the Śukraśāpavimocinī-vidyā, as follows:
*Oṃ aiṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ sohaṃ haṃsaḥ hvāṃ hvīṃ hvūṃ hvaiṃ hvauṃ hvaḥ tatsavitur*.
Hrāṃ, the most excellent; hrīṃ, we meditate upon the splendor of the divine; hrūṃ, [we meditate upon] those thoughts; hraiṃ, which may impel our intellects; hrauṃ, O Vaṃ!
O Immortal One, O Source of Nectar, O Showerer of Nectar, O Streamer of Nectar, O Bather in Nectar, fill, fill the vessel with nectar, O Dweller in the Lunar Orb!

Release, release the nectar from the curse of Śukra! Purify, purify the substance! Destroy, destroy the curse of Śukra! Cut, cut it asunder! Bestow, bestow auspiciousness! Rain down, rain down the nectar!
Devour, devour the sins of the vessel! [Destroy] the fallen, the pretas, piśācas, rākṣasas, ḍākinīs, and śākinīs!

[Protect, protect] from [them], O you who are served by hosts of yakṣas, gandharvas, gods, and sages; make it nectar, make it pure, hrūṃ! O Amṛteśvarī, rain down, rain down the digit of nectar, huṃ phaṭ svāhā! *Krauṃ*, obeisance to Śukra, the lord of the daityas—thus with this vidyā that liberates from the curse of Śukra.
Having consecrated it seven times, [one should pray: "O Supreme Nectar-Self, who produces the bliss of unbroken, singular flavor;
O you whose form is nectar, bestow here the spontaneous radiance of your own will!"

Having satiated the couple Ānandabhairava and Sudhādevī within the vessel with those very drops, reciting: *HA SA KṢA MA LA VA RA YA ŪṂ ĀNANDABHAIRAVĀYA VAUṢAṬ* and *SA HA KṢA MA LA VA RA YA ĪṂ SUDHĀDEVYAI VAUṢAṬ*.
O Supreme One, who abides in the non-clan (akula), whose form is nectar, and who bestows the knowledge of accomplishment—
place the state of immortality within this substance which has a moistened form.
Furthermore, having fully gratified the couple Ānanda-Bhairava with those very drops (bindus),

and having bestowed the state of blissful oneness in that form by means of *hrīṃ*, O Thou whose nature is this, becoming the very form of the Kula-nectar, cause the vibration of consciousness to arise within me!

Furthermore, having satiated the couple Ānanda-Bhairava with those very *bindus*, having consecrated it seven times with the root mantra, protected it with the weapon mantra (*astra*), veiled it with the armor mantra (*kavaca*), and rendered it nectarine with the seed-syllable of nectar (*amṛta*) "Vaṃ," one should display the *dhenu* and *yoni* mudrās and worship the eight couples beginning with Brāhmī.

Namely: Aṃ, I worship the sandals of the venerable Asitāṅga Bhairava; Namaḥ Āṃ, the venerable Brahmāṇī Ambā; Iṃ, the venerable Ruru Bhairava; Īṃ, the venerable Māheśvarī Ambā; Uṃ, the venerable Caṇḍa Bhairava; Ūṃ.
Kaumāryambā Śrī Ṛṃ; Krodhabhairava Śrī Ṝṃ; Vaiṣṇavyambā Śrī Ḷṃ;
Unmattabhairava Śrī Ḹṃ; Vārāhyambā Śrī Eṃ; Kapālibhairava Śrī Aiṃ.

Having worshipped the eight couples beginning with Brāhmī as follows: *Indrāṇyambā Śrī*, *Bhīṣaṇabhairava Śrī*, *Cāmuṇḍāmbā Śrī*, and *Saṃhārabhairava Śrī*, *Mahālakṣmyambā Śrī*; then, the meditation on the pitcher (*kumbha*) is as follows:
O Great Jar! You were born when the great ocean was being churned during the conflict between the gods and the dānavas; you were held in the hand by Viṣṇu.
From you all the gods have arisen; all the Vedas are dependent upon you. All beings abide in you; the vital breaths are established in you.
You alone are Śiva himself; you are Viṣṇu, you are Prajāpati;
you are all the Ādityas and other planets, and the Viśvedevas together with the ancestors.
Since you, the granter of the fruits of all desires, reside within this jar,
O Water-born One, I desire to perform this sacrifice through your grace.
By the mere sight of you, the great fruit of worldly enjoyment and liberation is attained;
O Kumbha, grant your presence and be forever gracious!

Thus ends the meditation on the jar (*kalaśa*). Now, the meditation on the nectar (*sudhā*): While the ocean of milk, the best of seas, was being churned, the goddess Nectar was born therein, assuming the form of a maiden.
She is endowed with eighteen arms, red in color, and possesses long eyes;
she holds a conch, a sword, a bow, a skull-cup, and likewise a pestle.
Holding a spear, a mace, an excellent bell, and a bell with her upper arms;
and [holding] a discus, a fist, an arrow, a trident, an iron shield, and a lance.
Holding a shield and a *bhiṇḍipāla* (javelin) with her right arms,
she has three eyes, long and slender limbs, and a radiance resembling the fire of cosmic destruction.
Having encircled the Mandara mountain with the terrifying whirlpools of foam,
he [created] nectar that had the color of cow's urine and milk, yet was ultimately black in hue.
Possessing the luster of both blue and non-blue colors, she is the supreme nectar of many forms;
terrifying all the asuras, she bestows fearlessness upon the gods.
That which is the nectar is the goddess Umā; that which is the intoxication is Maheśvara.
That which is the color is Brahmā; that which is the fragrance is Janārdana.
Soma is established in the sense of taste, the god Hutāśana in sound,
the god Manmatha in desire, and Bhairava indeed in play.
The goddess Gaṅgā resides in the foam; the seven oceans are situated at the place of awakening (bodhasthā).
The power of will (icchāśakti) is in the joy of nectar (sudhāmoda), while the power of knowledge (jñānaśakti) is in its essence (rasa).
And within its own flavor lies the power of action; when that is manifested, there is the supreme state.
Merely by beholding the nectar, one is liberated from all sins.
Merely by smelling its fragrance, one obtains the fruit of a hundred sacrifices;
merely by touching its nectar, one obtains the fruit of ten million holy pilgrimage sites.
"By merely tasting the nectar, one shall obtain the fourfold liberation.
Having thus meditated upon the nectar, one should recite the Sudhā-gāyatrī:
*aiṃ sudhādevi vidmahe hrīṃ samudrodbhave dhīmahi śrīṃ tanno raktākṣī*.

Having recited the Sudhāgāyatrī, "pracodayāt," seven times over the water-pot (kalaśa), and then having covered the nectar of the pot with another vessel, one should take up the vessel for drawing [the water] and say: "Oṃ, obeisance to Amoghā; Oṃ."

Having worshipped the four powers (śaktis) in that vessel with "Oṃ, obeisance to Sūkṣmā; Oṃ, obeisance to Ānandā; Oṃ, obeisance to Śānti," and having placed it upon the vessel used as a cover for the pitcher, one should display the mudrās beginning with the invocation (āvāhana). [The mudrās are: 1. Āvāhani, 2. Sthāpani, 3. Sannirodhini, 4. Avaguṇṭhini.

One should display these ten mudrās: *suprasāriṇī* (5), *sammukhīkariṇī* (6), *saṃkalariṇī* (7), *amṛtīkaraṇī* (8), *cakra* (9), and *yoni* (10). One should worship the jar with the ritual services beginning with fragrance (*gandha*) and ending with food offerings (*naivedya*). Thus concludes the installation of the jar (*kalaśasthāpana*).

Now, the installation of the conch (*śaṅkhasthāpana*). Then, on the right side of the vase, having fashioned a triangular, circular, and square mandala with pure water using the *matsya* (fish) mudrā with the upward-pointing hollows of both nostrils, one should grasp it with the right hand using the *śaṅkha* mudrā while holding it with the left.

Having worshipped with flowers and unbroken rice (*akṣata*) using the root mantra in both the individual and collective sequences, one should place the base (*ādhāra*), which has been rinsed with the weapon mantra (*astra-mantra*), in the center while reciting the root mantra; then, having worshipped it with "Oṃ *Raṃ* obeisance to the fire-mandala" (*agnimaṇḍalāya namaḥ*),
one should place the conch (*śaṅkha*) upon it while reciting the root mantra, and then [worship it] with "Oṃ *Haṃ* obeisance to the sun-mandala" (*sūryamaṇḍalāya namaḥ*).

Having worshipped with the root-mantra and filled [the vessel] with pure water, one should worship it with "Oṃ saṃ, obeisance to the lunar maṇḍala," and after casting perfumes and other offerings along with a drop from the *kalaśa*, one should consecrate it seven times with "Oṃ hsau, obeisance to Varuṇa; śauṃ, obeisance to Varuṇadevī," and recite: "O Gaṅgā and Yamunā... and so forth. "This [water] for me... [etc.]
Having consecrated [the water] with "Gaṅge... and so forth, the visualization (dhyāna) is as follows:
137) [I visualize the conch] Pāñcajanya, which has destroyed all the Dānavas by its great roar. (1)
Always bringing forth the milk from the tip of Mahāviṣṇu’s hand.

Thus is the meditation on the conch (*śaṅkha-dhyāna*). Having taken the water contained in the conch upon the palm of the right hand and covering it with the left hand, one should consecrate it three times with the root mantra (*mūla-mantra*). Then, having sprinkled oneself on the head three or nine times, and having sprinkled the articles of worship, one should form the conch mudrā (*śaṅkha-mudrā*).
One should demonstrate [this]. Thus ends the general installation of the *arghya*. Now follows the installation of the vessel for the special *arghya*:

in front of that, having formed a mandala consisting of a circle, a hexagon, and a triangle—marked internally with the *māyā* syllable—with water from a conch using the two hands raised upward by the flowing breath (*vahacchvāsa*).

Having grasped [the vessel] with the left thumb turned away from the body, one should worship the center of the triangle and the hexagon in both the sequential and reverse orders using the root-vidyā. Then, in the hexagon: *aiṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ*, "I worship the venerable sandals of the Heart Goddess, obeisance. *3*, "The Head Goddess, the venerable sandals... *3*, "The Crest Goddess, the venerable sandals... *3*, "The Armor Goddess, the venerable sandals... *3*.
Netradevī Śrī. Astradevī Śrī. In the square: 3 Kṣāṃ, obeisance to the Ocean of Milk; 3 Īṃ, [obeisance] to the Ocean of Sugarcane Juice;

3 Maṃ, [obeisance] to the Ocean of Honey; 3 Paṃ, [obeisance] to the Ocean of Nectar. Having thus worshipped those in the southeast and other directions, [worship] in the triangle: 3 Obeisance to the Kāmarūpa Pīṭha; 3 Obeisance to the Jālandhara Pīṭha; 3...

Having worshipped the four sacred seats (pīṭhas) by saying "Salutation to Pūrvagiri-pīṭha" in the center [and likewise to the others], and having established the base (ādhāra) washed with the root mantra while reciting "I establish the base for the special arghya-vessel of Śrī Bhuvaneśvarī; salutation," [The ritual continues: ...placing the vessel upon it.

Having worshipped with "RĀṂ RĪṂ RŪṂ RAṂ MA LA VA RA YA UṂ RAṂ, obeisance to the support of the special *arghya* vessel for the fire-maṇḍala, whose self consists of ten digits (*kalās*) that bestow dharma," one should worship the digits (*kalās*) upon it in a clockwise direction: "3 YAṂ, obeisance to the digit Dhūmrārcis, Śrī..."; "3 RAṂ, the digit Ūṣmā."

Śrī 3 Laṃ Jvalinīkalā, Śrī 3 Vaṃ Jvālinīkalā, Śrī 3 Śaṃ Visphuliṅginīkalā, Śrī 3 Ṣaṃ Suśrīkalā, Śrī 3 Saṃ Surūpākalā, Śrī 3 Haṃ Kapilākalā, Śrī 3 Laṃ Havyavahākalā, Śrī 3 Kṣaṃ Kavyavahākalā, Śrī— having thus worshipped with sandalwood paste and other offerings, upon that [seat]...

Having established it with the words, "I establish the special *arghya* vessel for Śrī Bhuvaneśvarī, made of gold, silver, copper, or *viśvāmitra* [iron], washed with the root-mantra and well-perfumed with incense, *namaḥ*," one should then offer: *Hāṃ Hīṃ Hūṃ Ha Ma La Va Ra Ya Ūṃ Saṃ*, to the solar disc (*sūryamaṇḍala*) whose self consists of twelve rays that bestow wealth.

Having worshipped with "Obeisance to the special arghya-vessel" (*viśeṣārghyapātrāya namaḥ*), one should worship the twelve kalās of the Sun in clockwise order upon it: 3 *kaṃ bhaṃ* Tapinī-kalā Śrī; 3 *khaṃ baṃ* Tāpinī-kalā Śrī;
3 *gaṃ phaṃ* Dhūmrā-kalā Śrī; 3 *ghaṃ paṃ* Marīci-kalā Śrī; 3 *ṅaṃ naṃ*.

Having worshipped thus: *Jvālanīkalā Śrī* 3, *Caṃ Dhaṃ Rucikalā Śrī* 3, *Chaṃ Daṃ Suṣumṇākalā Śrī* 3, *Jaṃ Thaṃ Bhogadākalā Śrī* 3, *Jhaṃ Taṃ Viśvākalā Śrī* 3, *Ñaṃ Ṇaṃ Bodhinīkalā Śrī* 3, *Taṃ Ḍhaṃ Dhāriṇīkalā Śrī* 3, *Ṭhaṃ Ḍaṃ Kṣamākalā Śrī* 3; then—
Having drawn out the water from the jar with the root-vidyā and the reverse-order Mātṛkā using a lifting vessel, [one should sprinkle it] with a stream touched by the second finger of the left hand.

Having filled the special *arghya* vessel for Śrī Bhuvaneśvarī with the mantra "I fill [this] nectar, *namaḥ*," and having placed a small amount from the second [vessel] into it with the root mantra, one should stir the nectar contained in that vessel with a flower using the thumb and ring finger while reciting "Oṃ Hrīṃ," and then discard that flower into its midst.

Having cast a flower moistened with the paste of the eight perfumes, having gazed upon it with the *gālinī* mudrā while uttering "Oṃ," and having consecrated it with the mantra "Gaṅge ca Yamune ca," one should purify the web of defects therein by means of inhalation (*pūraka*) using the wind seed-syllable *yaṃ*,
burn it away by means of retention (*kumbhaka*) using the fire seed-syllable *raṃ*, and transform it into nectar by means of exhalation (*recaka*) using the nectar seed-syllable *vaṃ*.

Having worshipped with the mantra: *sāṃ sīṃ sūṃ sa ma la va ra ya ūṃ saṃ kāmaprada-ṣoḍaśakalātmane somamaṇḍalāya viśeṣārghyapātrāmṛtāya namaḥ*, one should worship the sixteen digits (*kalās*) upon it in a clockwise direction: *3 aṃ Amṛtākalā śrī*; *3 āṃ Mānadākalā śrī*.
Iṃ Pūṣā-kalā Śrī 3; Īṃ Tuṣṭi-kalā Śrī 3; Uṃ Puṣṭi-kalā Śrī 3; Ūṃ Śakti-kalā Śrī 3;
Ṛṃ Dhṛti-kalā Śrī 3; Ṝṃ Śaśinī-kalā Śrī 3; Ḷṃ Candrikā-kalā Śrī 3; Ḹṃ Kānti-kalā Śrī 3; Eṃ Jyotsnā-kalā Śrī 3; Aiṃ Śrī-kalā Śrī 3; Oṃ Prīti-kalā.

Śrī0 3 Oṃ Aṅgadākalā Śrī0 3 Aṃ Pūrṇāmṛtākalā Śrī0 3 Aḥ Amṛtākalā Śrī0—thus one should worship the sixteen digits (kalās) of Soma. (Then) one should perform the vitalization (prāṇapratiṣṭhā) of the digits: Oṃ Āṃ Hrīṃ Kroṃ Yaṃ Raṃ Laṃ Vaṃ Śaṃ Saṃ Haṃ Laṃ Kṣaṃ So'haṃ.

"Haṃsaḥ; in this special arghya-water together with the support, the vital breaths of the digits of fire, sun, and moon are here, the vital breaths are here. Having recited the mantra again: "In this special arghya-water together with the support, the vital breaths of the digits of fire, sun, and moon are here, the vital breaths are here," and having recited the mantra once more.
In this special *arghya* accompanied by the *ādhāra*, the life-force (*jīva*) of the digits of Fire, Sun, and Moon resides here;

then, having recited the mantra again: "In this special *arghya* accompanied by the *ādhāra*, may all the sense organs—the speech, mind, skin, eyes, ears, tongue, nose, and vital breaths—of the digits of Fire, Sun, and Moon come right here."
"May they remain happily for a long time, svāhā! Having thus performed the *prāṇapratiṣṭhā*, one should [place] *glūṃ* Gaganaratnāya namaḥ in the center, *slūṃ* Svargaratnāya namaḥ in the east,
*mlūṃ* Manuṣyaratnāya namaḥ in the south, *blūṃ* Pātālaratnāya namaḥ in the west, and *nvlīṃ* in the north.

Having thus worshipped the five jewels, beginning with the jewel of the serpent (*nāgaratna*) in the center, one should write within that [space] the collection of letters beginning with *a* and ending with *kṣa*, consisting of a triangle, and having uttered the root-mantra:
"Arising from a fragment of the cosmic egg (*brahmāṇḍa*), produced from all essences..."
Having filled the great vessel, one should bring forth the essence of nectar.

Oṃ hrīṃ amṛte amṛtodbhave amṛteśvari amṛtavarṣiṇi amṛtaṃ srāvaya sāṃ jūṃ jūṃ saḥ amṛteśvaryai svāhā. Having consecrated [the water] three times with this Amṛtavidyā mantra, one should recite the Jātavedas Gāyatrī and the Tryambaka mantra. Śāṃ śīṃ śūṃ śaiṃ śauṃ śaḥ.
"Obeisance to the one who liberates from the curse of Śukra, svāhā! Having thus consecrated [the substance] three times with the mantra of the one who liberates from the curse of Śukra:
"In the supreme essence of nectar, which produces unbroken, singular-flavored bliss..."
Place your own spontaneous radiance there, within that which has the nature of nectar.

HA SA KṢA LA VA RA YA ŪṂ ĀNANDABHAIRAVĀYA VAUṢAṬ; SA HA KṢA MA LA VA RA YA Ū SUDHĀDEVYAI VAUṢAṬ— having thus gratified the couple Ānandabhairava and Sudhādevī with the drops from the midst of the *arghya* offering.
O Supreme One, who abides in the non-clan (akula), whose form is nectar, and who bestows the knowledge of accomplishment—
place the state of immortality within this substance which has a moist form!
Furthermore, having satiated the couple Ānanda-Bhairava with those very drops (bindus),

and having granted the state of blissful oneness in that form, become one whose nature is this [bliss] and cause the flash of consciousness (citsphuraṇa) to arise within me, who am of the form of the Kula-nectar.
Furthermore, having gratified the Ānanda-Bhairava couple with those very drops (*bindu*),

one should consecrate [the vessel] seven times with the root mantra (*mūla-mantra*), protect it with the weapon mantra (*astra-mantra*), veil it with the armor mantra (*kavaca-mantra*), and display the cow and womb mudrās (*dhenu-yoni-mudrā*). Then, meditating on the nectar (*sudhā*) while reciting "When the ocean was being churned," one should [recite] the Sudhā-Gāyatrī.

One should recite: *Aiṃ sudhādevi vidmahe hrīṃ samudrodbhave dhīmahi śrīṃ tanno raktākṣī pracodayāt*. Having thus recited the Sudhā-gāyatrī seven times, one should display the mudrās for invocation (*āvāhana*) and so forth, sprinkle oneself and the ritual implements with the water from the special *arghya* vessel, and [prepare] the vessel.

One should worship [the deity] with offerings beginning with fragrance and ending with food (naivedya). This concludes the installation of the special arghya vessel. In front of that, one should install the śakti-vessel with the root mantra (mūla-mantra). In front of that, one should install the bhoga-vessel with the root mantra. In front of that, one should install the guru-vessel with the vidyā of the guru’s sandals (pādukā). In front of that, one should install the ātma-vessel with the root mantra.

One should set them down. One should fill the vessels with the nectar from the jar using the root-vidyā. One should worship them with the offerings beginning with fragrance and ending with the final service. Furthermore, one should set out the offering-vessels at the time of presenting the bali-offerings. This is the procedure for the placement of the vessels.

Now, the worship of the Self (*ātmapūjana*). In that regard, first is the recitation of consciousness (*saṃvidvadana*); then, on the head-throne (*śiraḥ-pīṭha*), [one should worship] *hrīṃ*, followed by Śiva, Śakti, Sadāśiva, Īśvara,
