Having worshipped the seat of the venerable Guru on the head with sandalwood paste, unbroken rice, flowers, and so forth, saying: "Obeisance to the one whose self is the fire, water, and earth, the seat of Yoga," and having touched the vessel of the self with the seed-syllable *oṃ hrīṃ*, holding it in the right hand and taking unbroken rice in the left hand—

Having recited the root mantra, one should offer a handful of water for each, saying: "I worship and satisfy the four-petaled Mūlādhāra together with its deity; salutation. [Recite] the root mantra: "I worship and satisfy the six-petaled Svādhiṣṭhāna together with its deity. [Recite] the root mantra: "I worship the ten-petaled Maṇipūra together with its deity."
I satisfy. Root mantra: I worship and satisfy the unstruck (anāhata) chakra with twelve petals, together with its deity.
(p. 140) Root mantra: I worship and satisfy the purified (viśuddha) chakra with sixteen petals, together with its deity. Root mantra.

"I worship and satiate the two-petaled Ājñā-cakra together with its deity. Having thus satiated the six cakras, one again divides that radiance into three parts in the form of the three Puṣkaras; then, having worshipped at the Ādhāra with "Aiṃ, I worship and satiate the Śrīpādukā of the Svayaṃbhū-liṅga, obeisance," [one recites] "Īṃ" three times.
*Bāṇaliṅga* Śrī-tattva in the heart: *3 auḥ*. *Itaraliṅga* Śrī-tattva between the eyebrows: *3 aiṃ īṃ auḥ*.

*Paraliṅga* Śrī-tattva on the crown of the head: *3 aiṃ īṃ auḥ*. Having thus contemplated [these] in the foundation, heart, between the eyebrows, and the crown as being the forms of Fire, Sun, Moon, and their totality (*tatsamaṣṭi*), one should again render that splendor partless (*niṣkalīkṛtya*).
Situated within the cavity of the two emanations and resting upon the pair of manas and nakāra,
one should meditate on that which consists of a column of fire through the union of the Kula and Akula.

Having gratified her with: *oṃ hrīṃ bhuvaneśvarī parāmbā śrī0 pā0 ta0*, [one says]: *oṃ aiṃ ātmatattvarūpaṃ sthūladehaṃ śodhayāmi pū0 ta0*; *oṃ hrīṃ vidyātattvarūpaṃ sūkṣmadehaṃ śodhayāmi pū0 ta0*. Having thus gratified the three bodies and having recited the root mantra (*mūlavidyā*):
Having offered the arghya with the words: "I worship and honor Jīvaśiva, who consists of the supreme Mother Śrī Bhuvaneśvarī," he says:
"Having cast all conceptual constructions, such as their arising and so forth, into the single, dense abode of Light—just as an oblation of ghee is poured into the fire—by means of worship..."
Holding the sacrificial ladle (*sruca*) in the state of *unmanī* with the hands of light and space,
I offer into the fire the oblation of merit and demerit, using the essence of the *kalās* as the clarified butter.
With the mind as the ladle, I perpetually offer the sensory functions as oblations into the fire of the Self, which is kindled by the fuel of dharma and adharma, via the path of the suṣumṇā.

Having performed the internal oblation (*antarhavana*) with these and other [mantras], one should satisfy all beings in the *mūlādhāra* with the mantra: "May all beings be satisfied" (*sarvabhūtāni tṛpyantu*).

Then, one should satisfy the sixty-four crores of *yoginīs* in the pores of the skin with the mantra: "May the sixty-four crores of *yoginīs* be satisfied" (*catuḥṣaṣṭikoṭiyoginyaḥ tṛpyantu*). [Then recite: Oṃ hrīṃ, purify the *ātmatattva*. Oṃ hrīṃ, purify the *vidyātattva*. Oṃ hrīṃ, purify the *śivatattva*. Oṃ hrīṃ...

"May all reality (sarvatattva) be purified. Having thus performed the purification of the fourfold reality, one should contemplate oneself as the nature of Paramaśiva— having dissolved the three bodies because of being the witness thereof and because of being liberated from bondage.
In the principle ending with Māyā, "I am Śiva"; in the principle ending with Śakti, "I am Consciousness, I am Śiva";
and in the principle ending with Śiva, "I am Bliss, I am Śiva. Beyond this, I am the Full, the Unsurpassed.

One should recite: "There is nothing whatsoever beyond this. Having realized, "I am Śiva, I am Śiva," and being one whose all bonds have dissolved, one should live happily as one liberated while living (*jīvanmukta*). This is the worship of the Self.

Then one should perform the sacrifice of the five fires (*pañcāgniyāga*). Now follows the sequence for the worship of the deities of the pedestal’s enclosure (*pīṭhāvaraṇadevatā*): having joined the mind through the process of inhalation (*pūraka*), and having drawn up the prāṇa, apāna, samāna, and vyāna, one should [visualize] the wind agitated within, which has the form of a serpent struck by a staff, blazing with the play of lightning.

Having pierced the six wheels beginning with the *ādhāra* by means of the utterance of the root seed-syllable (*mūlabīja*), one should meditate upon the *Kulakuṇḍalinī*, having led her to the lunar orb at the end of the twelve fingers (*dvādaśānta*),
as she resides within the enclosure of the two groups of creation and rests upon the two vowels devoid of consonants (*anacka*).
One should meditate on [the goddess] consisting of the staff of fire (tejodaṇḍa) through the application of the Kula and Akula.

Having thus raised the Kuṇḍalinī, one should meditate upon her. There, having sprinkled the yantra with the water of the general *arghya*, one should worship the deities of the seat (*pīṭhadevatā*). It is as follows: *aiṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ gaṃ* obeisance to Gaṇapati;
*3 maṃ* obeisance to Maṇḍūka; *3* obeisance to Kacchapa; *3* obeisance to Ananta; *4* obeisance to Vārāha.
*Namaḥ*. 3 *Kālāya namaḥ*. 3 *Kūrmāya namaḥ*. 3 *Amṛtārṇavāya namaḥ*.

3 *Suvarṇadvīpāya namaḥ*. 3 *Ratnavedyai namaḥ*. 3 *Ratnasiṃhāsanāya namaḥ*. With these words, one should place eleven flowers along with unbroken rice (*akṣata*) upon the pedestal (*pīṭha*). In the corners beginning with the southeast (*āgneya*), [one should offer] 3 *Dharmāya*.

Homage! 3 Homage to Knowledge (jñāna). 3 Homage to Dispassion (vairāgya). 3 Homage to Sovereignty (aiśvarya). In the eastern directions: 3 Homage to Unrighteousness (adharma). 3 Homage to Ignorance (ajñāna). 3 Homage to Non-dispassion (avairāgya). 3 Homage to Lack of Sovereignty (anaiśvarya). One should worship the lineage of gurus from the northwest (vāyavya) to the northeast (īśāna): 3 To the gurus...
Salutation! 3. Salutation to the supreme gurus. 3.

Salutation to the gurus higher than the highest. 3. Salutation to the gurus who are the supreme abode. Salutation to the gurus beginning with Śiva. Hrīṃ, salutation to the four gates. 3. Salutation to the square. 3. Salutation to the sixteen-petaled lotus. 3. Hrīṃ, salutation to the eight-petaled lotus. 3.

Salutation to the hexagon. 3. Salutation to the triangle. 3. Salutation to the bindu. Hrīṃ, salutation to sattva, whose nature is light. Hrīṃ, salutation to rajas, whose nature is activity. Hrīṃ, salutation to tamas, whose nature is delight. Hrīṃ, salutation to the solar disc. Hrīṃ, salutation to the fiery disc. Hrīṃ.
Salutation to the lunar disc. Hrīṃ, salutation to the principle of the self (ātmatattva). Hrīṃ, salutation to the principle of knowledge (vidyātattva).

Hrīṃ, salutation to the principle of Śiva (śivatattva). Hrīṃ, salutation to the supreme principle (paramatattva). Hrīṃ, salutation to the self (ātman). Hrīṃ, salutation to the inner self (antarātman). Hrīṃ, salutation to the supreme self (paramātman). Hrīṃ, salutation to the lotus. Hrīṃ.
*Oṃ* *kaṇḍāya* *namaḥ*. *Hrīṃ* *malāya* *namaḥ*. *Hrīṃ* *nālāya* *namaḥ*. *Hrīṃ* *kesarebhyaḥ* *namaḥ*.
*Hrīṃ* *karṇikāyai* *namaḥ*. Having thus worshipped the seat (*āsana*), [one worships]: *Hrīṃ* *ātmaśaktikamalāsanāya* *namaḥ*. *Hrīṃ* *śaṅkhanidhaye* *namaḥ*. *Hrīṃ* *paṃ*...

Salutation to Padmanidhi. Then, one should worship the deities of the throne (pīṭhadevatā) in the order starting from the eastern direction: Hrīṃ, salutation to Jayā; Hrīṃ, salutation to Vijayā; Hrīṃ, salutation to Ajitā; Hrīṃ, salutation to Aparājitā;
Hrīṃ, salutation to Nityā; Hrīṃ, salutation to Vilāsinī; Hrīṃ, salutation to Dogdhrī; Hrīṃ...
*Oṃ aghorāyai namaḥ*. Having worshipped these [deities], one worships in the center with: *Hrīṃ maṅgalāyai namaḥ*.

Now, the mantra of the pedestal (*pīṭha-mantra*): *Oṃ namo bhagavatyai sarveśvaryai sarvajñānātmikāyai padmapīṭhāyai namaḥ*. Then, having taken a handful of flowers (*puṣpāñjali*) while maintaining the previously mentioned meditation (*dhyāna*), [one should proceed].

From the center of the triangle, or from one’s own heart, or from the solar disc, having brought forth the Supreme Goddess— who is endowed with all auspicious marks and whose form is radiant energy— through the right nostril (piṅgalā) to the outside for the sake of worship, and having visualized her while recollecting the root mantra:
Come, come, O Goddess of the lords of gods, Sovereign of the world, worshipped by the deities!
O you who are fond of supreme nectar, grant your presence quickly, O bestower of success!

O Mother, who dwells within the great lotus forest, whose form is compassion and bliss (or, according to another reading, the bliss of the cause), who is devoted to the welfare of all beings— come, come, O Supreme Goddess!
"Be present in this mandala, be present! *Namaḥ*. Saying this, one should cast flowers upon the *bindu*.
Having performed the ritual of integration (*sakalīkaraṇa*): "Hrīṃ, I integrate Bhuvaneśvarī, svāhā! Hrīṃ, I invoke Bhuvaneśvarī, svāhā!
Hrīṃ, I establish Bhuvaneśvarī, svāhā! Hrīṃ..."
"I restrain Bhuvaneśvarī, svāhā! Hrīṃ, I propitiate Bhuvaneśvarī, svāhā!
One should display these five mudrās.
Then, having performed the six-limbed placement (ṣaḍaṅganyāsa) and meditation upon the root mantra, [one should place it] in the center of the yantra.

One should perform the *prāṇapratiṣṭhā* (vitalization) of Śrī Bhuvaneśvarī. It is as follows: *Oṃ āṃ hrīṃ kroṃ yaṃ raṃ laṃ vaṃ śaṃ ṣaṃ saṃ haṃ laṃ kṣaṃ haṃ saḥ sohaṃ; in this maṇḍala, the life-breaths of Śrī Bhuvaneśvarī are here, the life-breaths are here.* *Oṃ āṃ hrīṃ kroṃ yaṃ raṃ laṃ vaṃ śaṃ ṣaṃ...*
Saṃ haṃ laṃ kṣaṃ haṃ saḥ sohaṃ; in this maṇḍala, the life-force (jīva) of the venerable Bhuvaneśvarī is stationed here.
Oṃ āṃ hrīṃ kroṃ yaṃ raṃ laṃ vaṃ śaṃ ṣaṃ saṃ haṃ laṃ kṣaṃ haṃ saḥ sohaṃ;
in this maṇḍala, all the sense-faculties (sarvendriyāṇi) of the venerable Bhuvaneśvarī [are stationed here].

"May speech, mind, skin, eyes, ears, tongue, nose, and breath come here and remain happily for a long time; svāhā! With this, one should scatter flowers and unbroken rice grains upon the yantra. Then, one should display the fifteen mudrās: "Hrīṃ! To Bhuvaneśvarī, I offer the nectar-mudrā; svāhā!"

In this manner, one should display the others: the Dhenu-mudrā (1), Yoni (2), Mahāyoni (3), Navayoni (4), Siṃha (5), Mahākrānta-mudrā (6), Granthita (7), Sama (8), Mukula (9), Padma (10), Pāśa (11), Aṅkuśa (12), Abhaya (13), and Varada (14); these one should display. Furthermore: "She who has the luster of the rising sun and a crown of moons..."

Having meditated and recited the root mantra, [one says]: "I worship the sandals of the venerable Mother Bhuvaneśvarī Ambā; obeisance! I offer libation! Having thus offered three handfuls of flowers at her feet and performed the libation, one should then prepare a seat for the Goddess with the root mantra as follows: *Hrīṃ, obeisance to the seat of Bhuvaneśvarī; Hrīṃ.*
*Hrīṃ*, to Bhuvaneśvarī, *arghya*, svāhā! *Hrīṃ*, to Bhuvaneśvarī, *pādya*, svadhā!
*Hrīṃ*, to Bhuvaneśvarī, *ācamanīya*, svadhā! *Hrīṃ*, to Bhuvaneśvarī, *madhuparka*, svadhā!
*Hrīṃ*, to Bhuvaneśvarī, I offer golden sandals; *namaḥ*. (To the north)

Having prepared the bathing pavilion and having seated [the deity] upon the jeweled lion-throne: *Hrīṃ, to Bhuvaneśvarī, I offer the cleansing of the hair and an oil massage; obeisance! Hrīṃ, to Bhuvaneśvarī, I offer the fragrant *āmalaka* scrub; obeisance!* [Recite] the root seed-syllable (*mūlabīja*).
The phrase "to Bhuvaneśvarī" is to be applied everywhere.
143) I offer the bath with warm water; obeisance. I offer the bath with the five products of the cow; obeisance.

I offer the bath with the five nectars; obeisance. I offer the holy-water bath accompanied by fruits, jewels, and other offerings; obeisance. I offer a cloth for the purpose of wiping the limbs; obeisance.
I offer the grooming of the hair and the cleansing of the locks; obeisance. "Please accept the garment"; obeisance.

I offer a pair of garments; obeisance. Having performed the auspicious rites beginning with the waving of lights (*nīrājana*), I offer the seating upon the jeweled throne in the adorned pavilion; obeisance.
[I offer] a crown, gems, earrings, a pearl nose-ornament, a neck-ornament, a necklace, armlets, bracelets, finger-rings, and anklets...
Salutations! I offer a garland of white lotuses at the throat; salutations! I offer divine collyrium to the eyes;

salutations! I offer protection to the forehead; salutations! I offer the sight of a mirror; salutations! Having offered the umbrella and chowries, and having led [the deity] into the worship pavilion onto the lap of Śiva...
I offer a seat. I offer fragrance. I offer unbroken grains of rice.
I offer three handfuls of flowers and the sound of the bell. I offer incense. I offer a lamp. I offer food offerings. I offer hand-unguents. Betel nut.

I offer [this]. I offer the waving of lights (*ārārttika*). Having satisfied [the deity] with the first [mantra] and so forth for as many times as possible, and having taken a handful of flowers (*puṣpāñjali*), [one says]:
"O Supreme Goddess, whose nature is consciousness, who delights in the essence of supreme nectar!"
Grant me permission, O Goddess of gods, for the worship of my retinue.

Thus, having obtained permission preceded by an offering of handfuls of flowers (*puṣpāñjali*), one should worship the deities of the enclosures (*āvaraṇadevatā*) with the *tattvamudrā*, using either the left-hand (*vāmācāra*) or right-hand (*dakṣiṇācāra*) practice, together with a drop (*bindu*) accompanied by a second unbroken grain (*akṣata*).
It is as follows: "Oṃ hrīṃ, obeisance to the Binducakra"—having thus offered three handfuls of flowers—Oṃ hrīṃ...

"I worship the Śrī-pādukā of Bhuvaneśvaryambā; salutations, I satiate her. Having satiated her three times, [one should offer] from the beginning with "May this Śrī Bhuvaneśvarī, the presiding deity of the Bindu-cakra, together with her weapons, her vehicle, and her ornaments, being well-worshipped with all the offerings (upacāras), be the granter of boons," and so forth, up to the handful of flowers (puṣpāñjali) including the scents (gandha) and other items.
One should offer it:
"O Bhuvaneśī, worshipped by the gods, grant me the attainment of my desired goal;
with devotion, I offer to you this worship of the first enclosure."
Thus one should display the *yonimudrā*. This concludes the first enclosure (*prathamāvaraṇa*).

Now, the second enclosure (*dvitīyāvaraṇa*). In the center, in front of the triangle, one should worship the lineage of gurus (*gurupaṅkti*) with the substance contained in the guru-vessel. It is as follows: having offered three handfuls of flowers with "Oṃ Hrīṃ, salutation to the triangular wheel (*trikoṇacakra*)," [one says]: "Aiṃ Hrīṃ Śrī, salutation to the gurus; O Śrī, I worship and satisfy you. [Three times: "Salutation to the supreme gurus (*paramaguru*)."
Śrī... I worship, I satiate. 3. Homage to the Gurus higher than the highest (parātpara-guru); Śrī... I worship, I satiate. 3.
Homage to the Gurus who are the supreme teachers (parameṣṭhi-guru); Śrī... I worship, I satiate. 3. Homage to the Gurus beginning with Śiva;
Śrī... I worship, I satiate. Then, in the intermediate directions: Hrāṃ, homage to the Heart; [homage to] the Heart-Śakti.
Śrī, I worship and satisfy. In the southeast: Hrīṃ, svāhā to the head; I worship and satisfy the Śakti of the head, Śrī. In the northeast:

Hrūṃ, vaṣaṭ to the crest-lock; I worship and satiate the Crest-lock Śakti, O Śrī! [In the] South-west. Hraiṃ, huṃ to the armor; I worship and satiate the Armor Śakti, O Śrī! [In the] North-west. Hvauṃ, vauṣaṭ to the three eyes; I worship and satiate the Eye Śakti, O Śrī! [In the] front. Hraḥ, to the weapon.

*Phaṭ*, I worship and propitiate the Astra-Śakti, Śrī... [in the four directions]. In the center of the triangle: *Hrāṃ*, I worship and propitiate Hṛllekhāmbā, Śrī... in the center. *Hrūṃ*, I worship and propitiate Gaganāmbā, Śrī... in the east. *Hraiṃ*, I worship and propitiate Raktāmbā, Śrī... in the south.

Hrauṃ, I worship and propitiate the venerable Karālikāmbā in the west; Hraḥ, I worship and propitiate the venerable Mahocchuṣmāmbā in the north. These deities of the second enclosure situated within the triangle have been fully worshipped and propitiated with all ritual offerings, along with their limbs, weapons, vehicles, and ornaments.
With the words "May they be so" (*saṃtu*) and others, one should offer [the articles] beginning with incense and ending with a handful of flowers.
"O Bhuvaneśī, worshipped by the gods, grant me the attainment of my desired goal!
With devotion, I offer to you this worship of the second enclosure."
Thus one should perform the salutation with the Mahāyonimudrā. This concludes the second enclosure.
Now the third enclosure (āvāraṇa). 3. On the filaments of the six-pointed star: Hrīṃ, I worship and satisfy Śrī Anaṅgakusumāmbā. Hrīṃ, I worship and satisfy Śrī Anaṅgakusumāturāmbā.
Hrīṃ, I worship and satisfy Śrī Anaṅgamadanāmbā. Hrīṃ, [I worship and satisfy] Śrī Bhuvanapālāmbā.
I worship, I satisfy. Hrīṃ, I worship, I satisfy the venerable Gaganāmbā. Hrīṃ, I worship, I bow to, and I satisfy the venerable sandals of Gaganamekhalāmbā.
Then, upon the petals of the hexagon: Hrīṃ, [to her] who is accompanied by Pitāmaha (Brahmā), holding a staff, a lotus, a rosary, and making gestures of granting fearlessness and boons...

To Gāyatrī Ambā, Śrī [Oṃ], in the southeast corner. Hrīṃ! To Sāvitrī Ambā, who holds the conch, discus, mace, and lotus, who is clad in yellow garments, and who is accompanied by Viṣṇu, Śrī [Oṃ], in the southwest corner, I worship and I offer libations. Hrīṃ! To her who is white, who wears white garments, and who displays the gestures of granting boons and fearlessness while holding the *svadhā* vessel and the rosary.
To the Mother Sarasvatī accompanied by Rudra, Śrī0, I worship; I offer libations in the northwest corner.

To the Great Mother Mahālakṣmī, who holds a jeweled pitcher and a jewel-casket, who is seated upon the lap of Kubera, who remains embracing Kubera with her right hand, and who holds a lotus with her other [left] hand, Śrī0.

I worship, I satisfy, in the southeast: Hrīṃ, to the Mother Rati, who holds a bow, arrows, a noose, and a goad, who is accompanied by Madana, who embraces her husband with one arm and holds a blue lotus with the other, and who sits upon the lap of her lover;
Śrī0, I worship, I satisfy, in the west: Hrīṃ.
To the King of Obstacles, who wields the goad and the noose;

who stands resting upon the finger of his beloved, dear, beneficial, and lovely consort; who is reeling from the intoxication of honeyed wine; who holds a jeweled goblet in his lotus-hand; who is the color of vermilion; and who possesses another lovely, full, and intoxicated woman.

I worship and satiate Śrī, who stands embracing [the deity] while touching his banner with her other hand, which holds a red lotus; she is in the northeast (Īśānī). The two treasures (Nidhis) are to be worshipped on the sides of the hexagon: "Hrīṃ, I worship and satiate Padmanidhi Śrī"; "Hrīṃ, I worship and satiate Śaṅkhanidhi Śrī. These...

One should offer the third circle of deities situated within the hexagon, together with their limbs (aṅgas), beginning with perfumes and ending with handfuls of flowers; then one should display the nine-yoni mudrās while reciting, "Grant me the attainment of my desired goal. Thus ends the third circle.

145) Now, the fourth enclosure: "Salutation to the eight-petaled lotus. Having thus offered three handfuls of flowers, one worships and gratifies [the deities] upon the petals of the eight-petaled lotus, starting from the base: *Hrīṃ, I worship and gratify Anaṅgarūpāmbā Śrī*. *Hrīṃ*...

Hrīṃ, I worship and satisfy Anaṅgamadanāmbā Śrī. Hrīṃ, I worship and satisfy Anaṅgamadanāturāmbā Śrī. Hrīṃ, I worship and satisfy Bhuvanavegāmbā Śrī. Hrīṃ, I worship and satisfy Lokapālikāmbā Śrī. Hrīṃ, I worship Sarvatomukhyambā Śrī.

I offer libation. Hrīṃ, I worship and offer libation to Anaṅgavasanāmbā Śrī. Hrīṃ, I worship and offer libation to Anaṅgamekhalāmbā Śrī. In the center of the eight petals: Hrāṃ, I worship and offer libation to Brāhmī Ambā Śrī. Hrīṃ, I worship [and offer libation] to Māheśvarī Ambā Śrī.

I satisfy. Hrūṃ, I worship and satisfy the venerable Mother Kaumāryambā Śrī. Hraiṃ, I worship and satisfy the venerable Mother Vaiṣṇavyambā Śrī. Hrauṃ, I worship and satisfy the venerable Mother Vārāhyambā Śrī. Hraḥ, I worship and satisfy the venerable Mother Indrāṇyambā Śrī. Aiṃ, I worship the venerable Mother Cāmuṇḍāmbā Śrī.
I offer libations. Hrīṃ, I worship and offer libations to Mahālakṣmyambā Śrī.

One should place the Mātṛkās on the tips of the petals: Hrīṃ aṃ āṃ iṃ īṃ uṃ ūṃ ṛṃ ṝṃ ḷṃ ḹṃ eṃ aiṃ oṃ auṃ aṃ aḥ on the eastern petal; Hrīṃ kaṃ 4 on the southeast; Hrīṃ caṃ 4 on the south; Hrīṃ ṭaṃ 4...
In the southwest: *hrīṃ taṃ* four times; in the northwest: *hrīṃ paṃ* four times; in the west: *hrīṃ yaṃ raṃ laṃ vaṃ*; in the north:
*hrīṃ śaṃ ṣaṃ saṃ haṃ laṃ kṣaṃ*; in the northeast: [the same].
These are the deities of the fourth enclosure situated within the eight petals, together with their limbs, up to the offering of handfuls of scented flowers.
One should offer [the oblation]. Saying, "Grant me the accomplishment of my desired goal," one should display the *pāśamudrā*.
Thus ends the fourth enclosure (*āvaraṇa*).
Now, the fifth enclosure: one should worship Karālikā and the others upon the petals of the sixteen-petaled lotus. As follows: 3.

Salutation to the sixteen-petaled lotus. Having thus offered three handfuls of flowers, [one should recite]: *Hrīṃ*, I worship and gratify the venerable Karālī Ambā; *Hrīṃ*, I worship and gratify the venerable Vikarālī Ambā; *Hrīṃ*, I worship and gratify the venerable Umā Ambā; *Hrīṃ*, I worship and gratify the venerable Sarasvatī Ambā.

Hrīṃ, I worship and satisfy Śrī Ambā. Hrīṃ, I worship and satisfy Śrī Durgāmbā. Hrīṃ, I worship and satisfy Śrī Ūṣmāmbā. Hrīṃ, I worship and satisfy Śrī Lakṣmyambā. Hrīṃ, I worship and satisfy Śrī Śrutyambā. Hrīṃ...

Hrīṃ, I worship and offer libations to the venerable Mother Smṛti. Hrīṃ, I worship and offer libations to the venerable Mother Dhṛti. Hrīṃ, I worship and offer libations to the venerable Mother Śraddhā. Hrīṃ, I worship and offer libations to the venerable Mother Medhā. Hrīṃ, I worship and offer libations to the venerable Mother Bhṛti. Hrīṃ.
I worship and satisfy Kāntyambā Śrī; I worship and satisfy Hrīṃ Āryāmbā Śrī.
These are the deities of the fifth enclosure located within the sixteen petals;
one should offer them everything from the scents up to the handful of flowers, saying: "Grant me the accomplishment of my desired goal."

One should display the goad mudrā (*aṅkuśamudrā*). Thus ends the fifth enclosure. Now, for the sixth enclosure: one should worship Indra and the other world-protectors (*lokapāla*) in order starting from the east.
Having offered three handfuls of flowers with the mantra "Obeisance to the wheel of the earth-grahas (*bhūgrahacakra*)," [one says] "Hrīṃ! To Indra, the lord of the gods (*surādhipati*)."

Salutation to the one with the vajra in hand, mounted upon Airāvata, together with his retinue and his weapon; I worship and satiate the venerable sandals. Hrīṃ! Salutation to Agni, the lord of splendor, mounted upon a ram, holding a spear in hand, together with his retinue and his weapon; I worship and satiate the venerable sandals. Hrīṃ! To Yama...
Homage to the Lord of the Pretas, who is mounted upon a buffalo, together with his retinue, and holding a spear in his hand; O Śrī...
I worship you, I satiate you.

Hrīṃ, salutation to Nairṛti, the lord of the Rākṣasas, who has a preta as his vehicle, holds a sword in his hand, is accompanied by his retinue, and possesses his own power; O Śrī, I worship you, I satisfy you. Hrīṃ, salutation to Varuṇa, the lord of the waters, who holds a noose in his hand, is mounted upon a makara, is accompanied by his retinue, and possesses his own power; O Śrī, I worship you.

I offer libations. Hrīṃ! Salutation to Vāyu, the lord of the vital breaths, who holds a banner in his hand, is mounted upon a deer, together with his retinue and his Śakti; I worship, I offer libations to the illustrious one. Hrīṃ! Salutation to Soma, the lord of the Yakṣas, who is mounted upon a horse, holds a goad in his hand, together with his retinue and his Śakti.

Śrī, I worship, I satisfy. Hrīṃ, obeisance to Īśāna, the lord of beings, mounted upon a bull, holding a trident in his hand, together with his retinue and his Śakti; Śrī, I worship, I satisfy. Then the weapons are to be worshipped in order starting from the east: Hrīṃ, obeisance to the Vajra; Śrī, I worship, I satisfy.

Hrīṃ, obeisance to Śakti; O Śrī, I worship you, I satiate you. Hrīṃ, obeisance to Daṇḍa; O Śrī, I worship you, I satiate you. Hrīṃ, obeisance to Khaḍga; O Śrī, I worship you, I satiate you. Hrīṃ, obeisance to Pāśa; O Śrī, I worship you, I satiate you. Hrīṃ, obeisance to Dhvaja; O Śrī, I worship you.
I satiate. Hrīṃ, obeisance to the mace; Śrī, I worship, I satiate. Hrīṃ, obeisance to the trident;
Śrī, I worship, I satiate. Hrīṃ, obeisance to Brahmā, the lord of the worlds, together with his vehicle, his weapons, his retinue, and his powers; Śrī, I worship, I satiate.
Between Īśāna and the East: Hrīṃ, obeisance to Viṣṇu, the lord of serpents, mounted upon Garuḍa, together with his weapons, his retinue, and his powers; O Śrī, I worship you, I satiate you.
Between the East and Agni: in front of that, the weapons are to be worshipped. Hrīṃ, obeisance to the conch (Śaṅkha).
Śrī, I worship, I satisfy. Hrīṃ, obeisance to the discus; Śrī, I worship, I satisfy. Hrīṃ, obeisance to the mace; Śrī, I worship, I satisfy. Hrīṃ, obeisance to the lotus; Śrī, I worship, I satisfy.
The weapons of the Goddess are to be worshipped in front of the triangle. Hrīṃ, obeisance to the noose; Śrī...

I worship, I satisfy. Hrīṃ, obeisance to Aṅkuśa; Śrī0, I worship, I satisfy. Hrīṃ, obeisance to Abhaya; Śrī0, I worship, I satisfy. Hrīṃ, obeisance to Varada; Śrī0, I worship, I satisfy. Then, one should worship Baṭuka on the left side of the Goddess. Aiṃ Hrīṃ Klīṃ.
Salutation to Baṭukanātha; O Śrī, I worship you, I satiate you. One should worship Gaṇeśa in the southeast corner:

Aiṃ Hrīṃ Glauṃ, salutation to Gaṇapati; O Śrī, I worship you, I satiate you. Aiṃ Hrīṃ Klīṃ, salutation to the deities of the doorway; O Śrī, I worship you, I satiate you. Hrīṃ, salutation to the sacred seats (pīṭhas) beginning with Kāmākṣā.

Salutation to Śrī; I worship, I offer libations. Aiṃ Hrīṃ Klīṃ, salutation to the Lords of the Pīṭhas (pīṭhanāthas); Śrī, I worship, I offer libations. Aiṃ Hrīṃ Klīṃ, salutation to the Mistresses of the Pīṭhas (pīṭheśvarīs);
Śrī, I worship, I offer libations. On the first line of the subterranean chamber (bhūgṛha), Hrīṃ, salutation to Sattva; Śrī, I worship.
I offer libations. To the second [line], *hrīṃ* obeisance to Rajas; *śrī* I worship, I offer libations. To the third [line], *hrīṃ* obeisance to Tamas; *śrī* I worship, I offer libations.
These are the deities of the sixth enclosure located within the earth-pavilion (*bhūgṛha*), together with their limbs; thus, from the offering of scents up to the handful of flowers (*puṣpāñjali*).
One should offer [the oblation], saying, "Grant me the attainment of my desired goal," and display the mudrās of fearlessness and the boon-granting gesture. Thus ends the sixth enclosure.

Again: *Hrīṃ Bhuvaneśvaryambā Śrī* [Name], I worship and satisfy you. Having first offered a handful of flowers (*puṣpāñjali*) into the *bindu*, having satisfied the Root Goddess three times, and having worshipped her with offerings such as fragrance (*gandha*), one should place the vessel for the great food offering (*mahānaivedya*) containing rice and its base, while reciting the *astra-mantra*.

Having protected [the incense] with perfumes and other offerings, worshipped it, and formed the *dhenumudrā*, one should worship the bell with the mantra "Oṃ jagaddhvani mantramātaḥ svāhā," hold it in the left hand, and while shaking it, offer the incense low.

One should offer [the flower] together with its root using the mantra "vanaspatyudbhava. Then, the lamp [should be offered] with the following verse: "This great lamp, brilliantly shining, which dispels darkness everywhere, the light within and without—may this lamp be accepted."

Thus, one should offer it while joined with the root mantra. Having sprinkled the food offering (naivedya) with the root mantra, performed the rites of drying and so forth with the seed-syllables of Vāyu and the others, and rendered it nectarine by means of the Surabhi-mudrā, [one should recite]:
"The food offering, endowed with the six tastes and accompanied by the five kinds of eatables..."
May this most noble essence of nectar be accepted together with Śiva.

Oṃ hrīṃ, may the venerable Bhuvaneśvarī, sovereign of the principle of the self (ātmatattva), be satisfied. Hrīṃ, may the venerable [Bhuvaneśvarī], sovereign of the principle of knowledge (vidyātattva), be satisfied. Hrīṃ, may the venerable [Bhuvaneśvarī], sovereign of the principle of Śiva (śivatattva), be satisfied. Having thus offered satisfaction in these four ways and having said, "Thou art the under-layer of nectar" (amṛtopastaraṇam asi), one should display the mudrās of the vital breaths (prāṇa) and so forth. As follows: Oṃ, svāhā to Prāṇa—with the thumb.

One should touch the little finger and the ring finger with the mantra: *oṃ vyānāya svāhā*. One should touch the index finger and the middle finger with the thumb, saying: *oṃ udānāya svāhā*. One should touch the ring finger, the middle finger, and the index finger with the thumb, saying: *oṃ samānāya svāhā*. One should touch all [the fingers] with the thumb, saying: *oṃ samānāya svāhā*. In the center, one should touch the curtain (*javanikā*).
Having eaten until the point of satiety, one should recite the root mantra. Then,

having offered the mid-meal water, the final sipping water (uttarāpośana), water for washing the hands, water for rinsing the mouth, hand-rubbing powder, fruit, betel, and the sacrificial fee (dakṣiṇā) using the root mantra;

Then one should perform the daily fire-oblation (*nityahoma*). It is as follows: having drawn a square mandala on the right side of oneself, or else having brought a perfected sacrificial pit (*siddhakuṇḍa*), one should visualize the yantra therein;
having sprinkled it there with the root mantra followed by *phaṭ*, and having established the fire with the root mantra, one should sweep around the fire with the root mantra.

Having performed the six-limbed ritual (*ṣaḍaṅga*) with the root-mantra (*mūlavidyā*), having meditated upon the Goddess in the fire, worshipped her with perfumes and other offerings, and displayed the *jvālinī* mudrā, one should offer oblations of clarified butter with the *vyāhṛti* mantras; then,
having offered sixteen oblations of clarified butter with the root-mantra, one should again present offerings beginning with perfumes and ending with betel-leaf using the root-mantra.
Having again performed the ritual placement (*nyāsa*) and meditation (*dhyāna*):
"O Fire, O you of great power, accomplisher of all rites!
You have been appointed to another task; go, O God, as you please!"
Thus one should dismiss [the deities]. One should perform a salutation with the *saṃhāramudrā*.
148) Having thus performed the daily fire offering (*nityahoma*), one should present the sacrificial offering (*balidāna*). It is as follows—at the front of the *yantra*:

Having fashioned four mandalas consisting of a circle, a hexagon, and a triangle on the right, back, and left sides [of the central area], and having placed four vessels with their bases upon them, one should worship Baṭuka, Yoginī, Gaṇeśa, and Kṣetrapāla within them in sequence: *vāṃ* obeisance to Baṭuka; *yāṃ* [obeisance] to the Yoginīs.

Salutations! *Gaṃ*, salutations to Gaṇeśa; *Kṣāṃ*, salutations to Kṣetrapāla. If there is only one vessel, one should worship the four [deities] in that very vessel. Having placed it to the north of the conch (*śaṅkha*) and filled it with water from the jar (*kalaśa*), one should take the *caru* oblation prepared with the first and second [mantras].

One should offer the bali-oblation to the principal deity. It is as follows: Then, having prepared a square mandala with a triangle in front of the Goddess, one should place upon it [the mantra]: "Aiṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Bhuvaneśvari, accept, accept this bali, svāhā! Over the offering of the bali, by means of the union of the thumb and the ring finger—

Having offered a continuous stream [of water] using the substance contained in the special *arghya* vessel, one should present the lamp, incense, flowers, unbroken rice grains (*akṣata*), and so forth. Then, to the west of the Goddess, [one recites]: *Oṃ hrīṃ vāṃ ehi ehi devi-putra baṭukanātha piṅgala-jaṭābhāra-bhāsura tri-netra jvālāmukha mama sarva-vighnān nāśaya nāśaya*.
"Accomplish my desire, accomplish it! Accept, accept this *bali* offering together with all the ritual services, *huṃ phaṭ svāhā*!

Having thus presented the *caru* along with a lamp, scents, unbroken rice, and flowers to the *Baṭuka*, one should meditate while pouring a stream from the substance contained in that vessel using the left forefinger and thumb.
Whatever yoginīs there may be—whether fierce, gentle, most terrible, or supreme;
whether moving in the sky, on the earth, or in the void—may they always be pleased with me.

To the east: *glāṃ glīṃ glūṃ glaiṃ glauṃ glaḥ gaṇapate ehi ehi mama vighnaṃ nāśaya mama īpsitaṃ kuru kuru imaṃ baliṃ gṛhṇa gṛhṇa svāhā*. With this mantra, one should offer to Gaṇeśa a sacrificial pap (*caruka*) accompanied by a lamp, along with perfumes, unbroken rice (*akṣata*), and flowers.

Pouring a stream [of water] from the substance contained in that vessel using the left thumb, one should meditate: [He whose] lotus-hands have their fingers raised with a citron, a mace, a sugarcane bow, a discus, a lotus, a noose, a blue lotus, the tip of a grain of rice, his own tusk, and a jewel-pitcher;...

The Lord, the three-eyed one, embraced by his beloved who holds a lotus in her hand, is the cause of the creation, destruction, and maintenance of the universe; he is free from obstacles and the bestower of supreme goals.

On the right: *Kṣāṃ kṣīṃ kṣūṃ kṣaiṃ kṣauṃ kṣaḥ hūṃ!* O Guardian of the Site and Field (*sthānakṣetrapāla*), adorned with a crown, a skull-bowl, and a garland of severed heads; you who bear a most terrifying form; you with coarse hair; victory, victory! O sky-clad one (*digambara*), who causes terror to the retinue of great spirits (*mahābhūta*); you with eyes of fire; you intoxicated by the madness of drinking wine!
O wielder of the trident weapon, intent on playing the horn, come, come! Destroy, destroy my obstacles!
Devour, devour the wicked one named so-and-so! Fulfill, fulfill my desire! Accept, accept this offering! Hūṃ Phaṭ Svāhā!
By this [verse], having offered the sacrificial pap (*caruka*) together with a lamp, along with perfumes, unbroken rice, and flowers, to the Guardian of the Field (*kṣetrapāla*),
one should meditate while pouring a stream from the substance contained in that vessel using the union of the left little finger and the thumb.
One [hand] holds a khaṭvāṅga, another a serpent, another a noose, and another a trident;
one hand holds a skull-cup and a sword, while the left hand holds a ḍamaru drum and a bow (pināka);
he has the crescent moon as his crest, is adorned with a garland of skulls, holds an excellent arrow, and wears a snake as a sacred thread.
May Bhairava, the protector of the sacred field (Kṣetrapāla), who bears a skull as his vessel, take away my fear.

"May he who dwells in this field and is a servant of the Kṣetrapāla be pleased by this offering of bali; may he grant me protection from all [harm]. Having thus performed the bali-offering—according to the opinion of some: *huṃ*.

With the mantra "Salutation to all beings who create obstacles," one should cast outside the house an offering of cooked rice (caru) accompanied by a lamp, along with honey, meat, and liquor, and provided with perfumes, unbroken grains, and flowers. This is the *bhūtabali*.
Then, from flour made of rice, wheat, and so forth, mixed with jaggery, cumin, and sugar, [one should fashion] triangular shapes.

Having prepared nine, five, or three [cakes] in the form of hand-drums (ḍamaru) and cooked them with ghee, one should fashion an eight-petaled lotus and a triangle within a vessel of copper or similar metal; having worshipped it with the root mantra, one should place eight lamps upon the eight petals and one lamp within the triangle. Having thus established nine lamps, [one should worship] with the root mantra.

Having placed fruits, flowers, betel, gold, and so forth into the vessel, and having ignited it with the root mantra while reciting two verses pertaining to the observance (samaya), one should rotate it three and a half times over the Goddess with the root mantra, unifying the inner light and the outer light without interruption:
"Unifying the inner light and the outer light continuously..."
Having whirled the family-lamp three times above the Goddess, one should offer it.
The moon and the sun, the earth, lightning, and likewise fire—you alone are all the luminaries; may this lamp be accepted.

Then, having removed the [obstructing] vision with the root mantra using salt, neem leaves, and so forth, or with balls of ground rice and the like, one should subsequently recite the root-vidyā thirty-two times, or else one hundred and eight times.
One should offer the recitation to the Goddess with the verse beginning "guhyātiguhyā. Then, having recited the hymn of praise, the thousand names, and so on—
One should perform a salutation with the *yonimudrā*.
Next is the worship of the Śakti. Having summoned one's own Śakti or the Śakti of a Vīra, and having fashioned a triangle on one's left side, one should invoke her upon it:
Come quickly, O boon-granting goddess, upon the surface of the maṇḍala;
accept this worship, O Queen of Gods, from me who am the vessel of your grace.

Having thus invoked her and performed worship beginning with the washing of her feet, and having adorned her with turmeric, saffron, collyrium, and so forth, one should give her a vessel of *śakti* accompanied by meat, consecrated with the root mantra; the mantra for that occasion is as follows:
This vessel of wine, accompanied by meat, is offered to you;
having accepted it, O fortunate goddess, grant victory and consume the enemy.
With this mantra, one should offer it thus:
"O child, this nectar of the lineage (kulāmṛta), the remainder of what I have drunk, is given by me to you.
I shall slay your enemy; I grant you all that you desire."

Having personally accepted that remainder with this mantra, and having given her garments, bodices, ornaments, and so forth according to one's ability, one should perform a prostration. This is the worship of Śakti.
Then, one should worship Kumāra in the form of Vaṭuka. Then, one should worship Kumārī.
Now, the worship of the Guru. Then, if the Guru is present, having performed his worship and so forth, one should offer the *gurupātra* to him. The mantra for that is:
"Then, to the one who is the form of the venerable Guru, and who is Paraśiva himself..."
Having lifted the vessel with both hands, one should offer it along with its companion.

With this, one should offer the oblation. If the Guru is not present, one should worship an excellent Ācārya who has received the Pūrṇābhiṣeka in his stead. If even the Ācārya is not present, one should satisfy the Śrī Guru three times with the substance contained in the Guru-vessel within the thousand-petaled lotus, and then take [the remainder] oneself. Thus concludes the worship of the Guru.

Then, having performed the worship of the heroes (*vīrapūjā*) and other rites, and having sprinkled them with water from a conch shell, one should give them vessels. Then, taking a handful of flowers (*puṣpāñjali*), one should offer that handful of flowers to the Goddess with the root mantra (*mūla*), or with a hymn (*stotra*), or else with a Vedic mantra. One should perform a salutation with the five mudrās.
The square [mudrā] is for immobilization, as are the fish and the gokṣura;
this is declared to be the yoni-mudrā among the salutation of the five mudrās.

Thus are the five mudrās. Now, the offering of the family lamp: holding the lamp together with the sacrificial porridge (caru) in the left hand and holding the vessel in the right hand, one should recite the root mantra—(p.

All the deities residing in the body, the elephant-faced ones, the lords of the sacred fields (kṣetrapālas), the Bhairavas, the Yoginīs, the Vaṭukas, the Yakṣas, the Pitṛs, the Bhūtas, the Piśācas, the Grahas,
and others who move in the quarters, on the earth, in the sky, in the trees, in the Vetālas, and in the waters—
May they be satisfied as they drink the beverage, along with the lamp and the sacrificial porridge, for the sake of this son of noble family.
With this, one should consume the lamp along with the sacrificial porridge (caru) and take up the vessel. Thus concludes the offering of the Kula-lamp.
"I do not know the invocation, nor do I know the worship;
I do not know the dismissal—may you forgive me, O Supreme Goddess! (1)
O Pārvatī! O Goddess! May that which has been worshipped by me—though deficient in mantra, deficient in ritual action, and deficient in devotion—become complete for me. || 2 ||
You are Īśa, Viṣṇu, and the four-faced Brahmā; you alone are devotion and you alone are primordial nature (prakṛti).
You alone are the sun and the lord of the night (the moon); you alone are power (śakti) and you alone are primordial nature.
You alone are my mother and you alone are my father; you alone are my kinsman and you alone are my friend.
You alone are my knowledge and you alone are my wealth; O Goddess, O Goddess, you alone are everything to me. 4.
You alone are the agent, the cause of the instrument, the protector, the ordainer, and you alone are the dissolution;
you are the elements, you are the instruments, you are indeed the knowledge of Brahman, and you alone are the Self.
Umā is the known, Umā is the enjoyer, and Umā is this entire world;
Umā triumphs everywhere, and he who is Umā is indeed myself. (6)
When one praises the deity with this hymn of praise, she, being pleased, bestows sovereignty,
long life, health, knowledge, fame, prosperity, and happiness.
Thousands of offenses are committed by me day and night;
considering me as your servant, forgive me, O Supreme Goddess! (8)
O Śivā! Whether done with knowledge or without knowledge, whatever I have performed—O Mother, forgive me for all this that I have done. || 9 ||
Having thus asked for forgiveness in many ways preceded by prostrations, and having taken special *arghya* water in his cupped palms, he says:
"Whatever [sin] was previously committed by me—through the authority of my vital breaths, intellect, body, and duties; during the states of waking, dreaming, deep sleep, and the fourth (*turya*);
whether by mind, speech, or action; with the two hands, the feet, the belly, or the generative organ; whatever was remembered..."

Having recited, "Whatever has been spoken and whatever has been performed—all that is offered to the Guru and the Deity; may all this become an offering to Brahman," one should offer it at the lotus-feet of the Goddess. Then, having awakened the Goddess with three *tāla*-claps by saying "Oṃ Hrīṃ Bhuvaneśvarī, forgive me," one should [dissolve] her, who is in the form of light, by means of the *saṃhāra-mudrā*.

Having extracted that splendor from the withered flower (nirmālya-puṣpa), having smelled it, and by means of the practice of inhalation (pūraka), having reached the thousand-petaled lotus, [one should remain] there for a moment.
Having meditated [on her] by way of the *suṣumṇā* channel, one should bring her to the heart-lotus with the mantra "Aiṃ, obeisance to the Heart," and while meditating there, recite:
"Oṃ Hrīṃ! Stay, stay in the supreme abode, in your own place, O Supreme Goddess!"
Therein, all the gods, beginning with Brahmā, abide within my heart.
Having thus established [the deity] within the lotus of the heart, one should then recite the Śāntistava. As it is said in the Vāmakeśvaratantra:
"Oṃ! May the *preta*-kūṣmāṇḍas perish; may the malevolent men perish."
May there be auspiciousness for the practitioners who preserve the sacred tradition.
May all the Mothers be victorious; may the hosts of Yoginīs be victorious;
may the Siddha-Ḍākinīs be victorious; may the lineages of Gurus be victorious.
May those who have attained the power of atomization rejoice; may Bhairava and the others rejoice;
may all the deities, including the Siddhas and Vidyādharas, rejoice.
May those mantra-practitioners who are pure in their sacred tradition, possessed of purified intellects,
whose hearts rejoice in all bliss, and who protect the lineage, be filled with joy.
May Indra and the others be gratified; may the deities of the dwelling be satisfied;
and may the gods, beginning with the Moon and the Sun, be gratified through my devotion.
May the constellations, the planets, the astrological conjunctions, the karaṇas, and all others likewise,
as well as the months and lunar days, all go forth in happiness.
May all the ancestors, the seasons, the years, and so forth,
as well as those who move in the sky and those who move upon the earth, be satisfied through my devotion.
May those who move through the atmosphere, those born of other divine species,
all the rivers, and all the birds likewise attain happiness.
May animals, trees, mountains, valleys, and caves;
may all sages and brahmins always grant me peace.
May there be auspiciousness for me everywhere, regarding my sons, wife, wealth, and so forth;
may kings be happy, and may there always be safety on my path.
May sacred fords, cattle, cows, and whatever other holy places there are,
as well as elderly women devoted to their husbands, always grant me auspiciousness.
May my days pass auspiciously; may my friends be well-disposed toward me. May the practitioners and reciters be successful, and may the worshippers abide in peace.
Those who possess distorted intellects, who delight in their own ornaments, who revile me during my worship;
those whose hearts are ruined by conduct contrary to divine law, who are wicked and harmful;
and those blind-hearted ones who, upon seeing the unprecedented Cakra, harbor hatred toward the Kaulikas—[may they be destroyed].
May they go to destruction here at this moment by the command of Śrī Bhairava.
May those who hate practitioners and always defile the sacred tradition go into the mouths of the ḍākinīs, so that they may be satiated by their flesh.
May my enemies, as well as those who revile me,
and those who hate practitioners, go to their destruction by the command of Śiva.
May those who revile me go to destruction; may those who practice [this path] become accomplished Siddhas.
May the Goddess’s compassionate gaze be everywhere, and may the Supreme Mistress be present before me.

Having recited this peace-chant (*śāntipāṭha*), one should sprinkle all the initiates (*sāmayika*) with the water from the general offering vessel (*sāmānyārghya*). Then, having lifted the special offering vessel (*viśeṣārghyapātra*), one should offer it to the venerable Guru situated upon the head. Thereafter, having performed the Kaula duties and so forth together with the initiates, one may enjoy oneself as is pleasant. Then—

One should offer the *ucchiṣṭa-mātaṅgī* oblation with all the remains. As follows: having drawn a triangular mandala on one's left side with the mantra "Klīṃ, obeisance! O Ucchiṣṭacāṇḍālī, Mātaṅgī, you who bring all under control, Svāhā!", one should deposit the flowing oblation there. The visualization (*dhyāna*) is as follows:
One should meditate upon the goddess Ucchiṣṭamātaṅgī, the sole enchantress of the world,

who delights in the play of playing the lute and singing, who is radiant in blue garments, whose lips are like the bimba fruit, whose feet are moist with fresh lac-dye, and whose dark locks of hair are scattered about.
I bow to the goddess Mātaṅgī, who has beautiful limbs, who wears earrings of nine gems, who is radiant with red ornaments, whose face bears a gentle smile, and who is dark as a parrot.
Having meditated thus, one should perform a salutation with the five mudrās.
After giving betel, sacrificial fees (*dakṣiṇā*), and so forth to all, one should dismiss them.
Thus, following the *Pṛthvīdharācārya-paddhati* and the *Śāradātilaka*, and relying upon the doctrines of various tantras—

Thus ends the third ritual manual, titled "The Exposition of Worship," within the *Bhuvaneśvarīkramacandrikā*, composed by Anantadeva, who resides in Mātṛpura and belongs to the Śrīdā-Īśvara Sampradāya. Om.
May this be offered to the venerable Guru-deva.
The *Laghusaptaśatīstotra* composed by Śrī Pṛthvīdhara Ācārya:
(Oṃ, regarding this mantra of the *Śrīlaghusaptaśatīstotra*, the Blessed Sadāśiva is the Seer; [he is to be placed] upon the head.)
Salutation to the Anuṣṭubh meter in the mouth; the Trimūrti deity in the heart; the Vāgbhava seed-syllable *aiṃ*;
Māyā *hrīṃ* as the power (*śakti*); Śrī Lakṣmī as the bolt (*kīlaka*); and the application (*viniyoga*) for my fourfold human goals in the recitation throughout all the limbs.
Salutations to the beloved of Viriñci; salutations be to you, the beloved of Śaṅkara;
salutations to the beloved of Nārāyaṇa; I take refuge in Śrī Caṇḍikā. || 1 ||

O Goddess Śrī Caṇḍikā! Brahmā and the other gods, as well as all the sages headed by Vasiṣṭha, worship you; I constantly remember you, who are the color of vermilion and possess the splendor of the rising sun. (2)

O Śrī Caṇḍikā! I constantly remember you, whose splendor is equal to a thousand moons and suns, who possesses the reddish luster of the bandhūka flower and the lotus, and whose radiance is like a blazing fire. 3.
O Śrī Siddhinātha, sole lord of the world! This speech of yours, consisting of supreme nectar and residing within the Upaniṣads,
has been heard by me, who have no other refuge and have not heard it before.
Round-faced, she is the natural abode of the ocean of compassion. Om, salutations to Caṇḍikā. [The portion within brackets is not found in the second manuscript. Om, salutations to Śrī Gaṇeśa.
Those who know the truth declare that all such actions as sacrifice and the like, which are said to be the abode of Dharma, are entirely centered in you alone;
for, having reflected upon the mind, it is you who are consciousness.
O Eternal One! I take refuge in Your two feet. || 1 ||
This is the Lord of the Daughter of the Ocean, the Ancient Puruṣa, whose body is cherished upon the couch of Śeṣa.
O Mother of the World! Helpless under the snare of delusion caused by you, even he lay down with his eyes rolling. || 2 ||
O Mother! Even for that Janārdana, from whose ears were born the two demons named Madhu and Kaiṭabha, those two were not easily slain. Yet, even he was [easily overcome] by your curiosity.
Distraught by your māyā, those two have gone to their destruction.
That buffalo form, endowed with unprecedented strength; that which surpassed the prowess of the Lord of Heaven;
and that whose heart was bound by a vow to produce sorrow in the world—
O Girijā, it has been crushed by you with nothing more than a glance! || 4 ||
O Daughter of the Mountain King, he who was renowned on earth as Dhūmralocana,
and whose power was celebrated, was reduced to ashes by the sound of "huṃ" from your foot for the sake of destroying all the asuras.
I believe this oblation has been offered into the fire of my own pride. || 5 ||
Even for some, beginning with the Lord of the Thirty-three,
Caṇḍa and Muṇḍa were never easy to conquer;
yet those two, intoxicated with pride, suddenly [assumed forms equal to Śambara].
O Mother, our heads have fallen shattered from your sword-blade.
On account of his mission, even the God whose power is renowned as "Śiva" went to the abode of the Lord of the Dānavas.
She further proclaimed his deeds:
"Be gracious, O messenger of Śiva; this is the manifestation of your power."

O Aparṇā, it is a marvel that those who could not be conquered even by the immortals became infinite seeds of their own blood upon the ground when struck by weapons and fell with blood flowing from them.
Yet even all those [poisons] have been swallowed by you alone within the sky [or: within your mouth]. || 8 ||
It is a complete marvel that these two enemies of the gods—
known as Śumbha and Niśumbha, whose hands were strengthened by plundering the splendor of the three worlds— were slain on earth with weapons.
O Mother! By your policy, even those two did not go to the world of the gods.
Into this fire of yours, the conflagration at the time of universal dissolution, wherein the worlds instantly go to their destruction,
the lords of the Dānavas fall like moths.
For all states of existence are indeed reduced to ashes! What is there to wonder at in this? || 10 ||
What then shall I say of you, who are intent upon quenching the fever of worldly existence for those who bow before you?
What then shall I say of you, who are intent upon quenching the fever of worldly existence...?
[She is] devoted to the nurturing of those who stand in opposition. || 11 ||
O Bhavānī! You hold in your left hand and its opposite, as described above,
a vessel filled with the essence of nectar, a choice citron,
a shield, and a mace.
Those wise ones who meditate upon her, who resembles the dawn, are indeed the truly accomplished. || 12 ||
Or rather, O Mother of the World, he who daily remembers this seed-syllable of Yours— which is beyond Varuṇa and mounted upon Fire— [even he is liberated].
Marked by Māyā and adorned with the dot of the young moon, he enjoys here a kingdom that is not dull due to the resonance of Nāda. || 13 ||
Though residing within all living beings in the form of a thread,
you shine forth here externally in the form of the entire universe;
what profusion of verbal expression can describe you who transcend all words?
O Mother! protect me, a wretched person free from worldly illusion. 14.

O Goddess! Whatever has been done by me here out of delusion— the invocation, the description of the sacrifice, the fire-oblation, the dedication of the rite, and the dismissal— all these transgressions, I offer unto You.
O Mother, O Giver of Boons, who dwellest both within and without, forgive me! || 15 ||
Whoever on this earth recites daily, at the three periods of the day, this incomparable account of Caṇḍī, which brings about the end of the Danujas,
shall be illustrious, happy, victorious, fortunate, and patient.
He may be a renunciant, possessing an ancient body, a sovereign among poets. || 16 ||
By the grace of Śrī Śambhunātha— the sole lord of the world, who is also known by the name Śrī Siddhanātha—
and through all the scriptures, [this has been attained].
Pṛthvīdhara composed this hymn: [In the manuscript *kh*, the following additional reading is found:
"The first is Viṣṇu-māyā, and the second is consciousness (*cetanā*);
then intellect (*buddhi*), sleep (*nidrā*), hunger (*kṣudhā*), shadow (*chāyā*), power (*śakti*), and thirst (*tṛṣṇā*) is the eighth. (18)
Patience, birth, as well as modesty, tranquility, faith, and beauty; prosperity, conduct, mindfulness, compassion, and likewise radiance. (19)
Tuṣṭi, Puṣṭi, Mātā, and Bhrānti, who is the soul of all—
these are the auspicious goddesses numbered as twenty-three.
For those men who possess the pure recitation, enjoyment and liberation are not far away.

O Lord! You made Your bed at the edge of the Jayā river, complete with a citron, a staff, a spittoon, and a drinking vessel; for the sake of creation, You remain there as a mendicant. To You, I eternally go for refuge.
This hymn to the Goddess, consisting of wisdom, was perfectly composed by the eminent teacher Pṛthvīdhara;
it is the essence extracted from the Saptaśatī.
It is endowed with all [virtues], the essence of the Veda. || 18 ||
Thus ends the *Laghusaptaśatīstotra* composed by Ācārya Pṛthvīdhara.
